title: Programming supramolecular polymer network topology via homochiral self-sorting
abstract: While stereochemistry has a strong influence on polymer structure and assembly, its use as a design handle to regulate polymer network topology remains unexplored. Here we demonstrate that homochiral self-sorting can be harnessed to suppress primary loops in end-linked polymer networks. We synthesized linear polymers terminated with heterochiral bi-2-naphthol-based ligands that cross-link via palladium(II)-mediated Pd2L4 metal-organic cage (MOC) assembly. This design exploits a thermodynamic preference for homochiral MOCs, enforcing a bias against intramolecular cyclization. Compared with networks formed from homochiral polymers, which can form primary loops through MOC formation, networks formed from heterochiral polymers exhibit lower primary loop densities and enhanced mechanical properties. The presence of sacrificial loops at low concentrations also enables topology editing by adding functionalized free ligands with minimal impact on network integrity. This work establishes chiral self-sorting as a versatile approach to controlling polymer topology and provides a generalizable strategy for designing robust and functional polymer networks.

title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr2
abstract: Niobium oxide dihalide films show a second-harmonic generation (SHG) efficiency scaling with their thickness, owing to their weak interlayer electronic coupling, but their use in integrated nonlinear photonics has been limited by the lack of robust electrical tuneability. Here we integrate ferroelectric NbOBr2, of thicknesses ranging from 20 nm to 40 nm, with a silicon nitride microring resonator to realize electrically reconfigurable SHG on a photonic chip. NbOBr2 combines strong second-order susceptibility from intrinsic inversion-symmetry breaking with electrically switchable in-plane ferroelectric polarisation. By modulating the Schottky barrier at the NbOBr2-metal interface, ferroelectric switching controls carrier injection, free carrier absorption and dispersion, thereby tuning the cavity-enhanced nonlinear response. The device achieves an SHG conversion efficiency of 158% W-1 under continuous-wave excitation and a 53% electrical modulation depth. The polarisation states can also be programmed over multiple levels and retained after switching, enabling non-volatile control of the optical response. Using the fundamental and frequency-converted outputs as complementary channels, we further demonstrate dual-channel edge detection.

title: Engineered wood from nanoscience to real-world materials
abstract: Engineered wood technologies are rapidly expanding the capabilities of one of the world’s most familiar materials. Nature Reviews Materials speaks with Liangbing Hu, professor at Yale University and founder of InventWood, about the development of Superwood, the diversification of wood-based technologies and the path towards commercialization.

title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
abstract: As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.

title: Pulling sugars off salt activation
abstract: The chemical assembly of oligosaccharides hinges on the reactivity of the anomeric site. In 1980, the introduction of a Lewis acid-catalysed method for the activation of anomeric imidates marked an important step in carbohydrate synthesis, becoming the foundation of complex synthetic strategies to this day.

title: Modular benzylamine synthesis through trifunctional zirconium catalysis
abstract: Photocatalysis can expand the reactivity of transition-metal catalysts by enabling new reaction pathways under mild conditions. Now, a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system is developed that combines photochemical, redox and Lewis acid catalysis for the modular assembly of diverse benzylamines directly from aryl aldehydes, alkanes and nitriles under mild conditions.

title: Spin order steers a light–matter condensate
abstract: Light–matter condensates get a magnetic control knob. In the layered magnet CrSBr, reorienting the spins with a modest field shifts the condensate’s colour by more than 10 meV.

title: Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
abstract: It has been surprisingly difficult to calculate how much warming different regions of the Earth have experienced since pre-industrial times. Now, research shows that in most land regions, the temperature thresholds that governments agreed to in Paris to keep below are already dangerously close.

title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
abstract: Global temperatures have averaged 1.2 °C above pre-industrial levels over the past decade, yet regional warming patterns and remaining warming budgets under Paris Agreement limits remain uncertain owing to insufficient historical observations. Here we quantify and attribute warming across all IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) regions since pre-industrial times using a Bayesian framework combining multi-model simulations with observations, enabling robust estimates in data-sparse regions. Regional warming is already pronounced. By 2025, attributed regional warming had reached about 90–94% of the levels expected at 1.5 °C global warming and 65–76% of those expected at 2 °C. Attribution confidence is the highest in tropical regions, including much of Africa, where low internal variability enables robust results. Attributed warming is the greatest in northern high-latitude regions, exceeding 2.5 °C. Greenhouse gases dominate, partially offset by aerosol cooling. These results reveal that current warming is already indistinguishable from a 1.5 °C world, highlighting the shared urgency of adaptation across all regions. Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.

title: Bioprinting, ten years on: from shape to function
abstract: Bioprinting has moved from building organ-like shapes that keep cells alive to constructs judged by function. However, function only emerges when computational design, printing hardware and instructive bioinks are coupled in one process. Making this coupling routine and reproducible is essential for translating printed tissues into credible therapies and models.

title: Higher warming leads to a larger zero-emissions commitment
abstract: Scientific grounds for a net-zero policy assume near-zero committed warming over a few decades after CO2 emissions cease. A modelling study suggests that if prior peak temperatures rise above 2 °C before cessation of CO2 emissions, committed warming increases, making it harder to stabilize global warming.

title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Global fossil fuel CO
                    2
                    emissions have grown 0.8% per year on average between 2019 and 2025. Here we project a decrease of 0.4% in 2026, probably as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power offset about 64–79% of increasing emissions from demand growth through 2028; acceleration in clean technology deployment is needed to guarantee emissions peak and subsequent decline.

title: Early evidence links data centre exposure to coal power retirement timelines
abstract: Data centre expansion may slow the coal-fired power plants phase-out, complicating decarbonization pathways. This study finds that coal units exposed to post-2020 data centres have lower retirement risks and their potential lifetime extensions could cause large additional CO2 emissions.

title: Benchmarking mechanistic credibility in electrocatalysis through data-driven evaluation
abstract: The performance of electrocatalytic reactions has rapidly advanced in recent years, yet there remain numerous controversies in the underlying mechanistic understanding of these systems. This Perspective proposes a framework for rating the strength of evidence and cross-community validation of mechanistic claims for the most-studied electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Coal power lives longer next to data centres
abstract: Data centres are among the world’s fastest growing electricity consumers. An analysis of more than 9,000 facilities worldwide links the artificial intelligence-era expansion of data centres to delayed coal plant retirements and around 2 Gt of additional carbon dioxide emissions.

abstract: In a Beijing park, a dispute over square dancing versus basketball changed how Haiyun Xu heard the music of women dancers — and revealed unwritten rules that govern whose movements belong in public space.

abstract: Soft polymer coatings spontaneously rearrange on nanosphere surfaces to form directional bonds, unlocking an alternative route to delicate nanoparticle superlattices.

title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
abstract:
Abstract
                  Agricultural nitrogen (N) surplus (the residual of total N inputs after harvest removal, plant-tissue storage, runoff and atmospheric losses) is a leading cause of groundwater and other environmental contamination in intensive food-producing regions, yet N surplus estimates often depend on inconsistent fertilizer, harvest and manure datasets in an N balance. Using California’s Central Valley as a data-rich test case, we propagate expert, survey-based, regulatory and county-level datasets through a fixed crop-specific N surplus framework to generate 24 cases. Holding model structure and land use constant, we quantify the large divergence in estimated N surplus arising from data choice, especially for manure-treated field crops. The uncertainty about N surplus is consequential: it can reorder which crops, regions and pathways receive priority for groundwater protection. The resulting spread among N surplus outcomes is large enough to alter hotspot rankings, mitigation priorities and screening-level estimates of economic burden. Credible nitrogen assessment at farm to global scales therefore requires explicit propagation of agricultural data source uncertainty, which can materially affect resulting N surplus estimates. Absent specific local data, the uncertainty magnitudes reported here may guide N surplus uncertainty assessment in other regional, national and global analyses.

title: Programming golden triple helices
abstract: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.

abstract: Ancient rocks in northern China reveal that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust had been buried rapidly to depths greater than 50 kilometres and partly melted. This crust was derived from a mantle reservoir that had been left behind when the crust separated from the early mantle as early as 4.3 billion years ago. Zircon crystals found in some of Earth’s oldest rocks suggest that the source rock was once buried about 50 kilometres into the mantle.

title: Proteins that form the nuclear pore barrier move like liquids
abstract: Nuclear pores control molecular traffic into and out of the cell nucleus. Measurements in living cells, together with molecular-dynamics simulations, show that flexible protein chains that form the selectivity barriers of nuclear pores are highly mobile, and that a sugar modification and the carrier protein importin-β help to preserve this dynamic state. The motion of the nuclear pore protein NUP98 is regulated by a transport receptor and a sugar modification.

title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses and discrete length scales. Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes or repeating features1,2. In contrast, as network science has revealed, real-world and biological systems—from the Internet to the brain—derive their function from broad, multiscale variability in connectivity and link length3, 4, 5–6. Here we introduce scale-rich metamaterials, a design framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials, achieving orders-of-magnitude heterogeneity in ligament lengths, thicknesses and connectivity. Governed by only two parameters, scale-rich networks span orders of magnitude in structural features, overcoming previous constraints in metamaterial design. Translating these network models into physically realizable materials, we use simulations and experiments to show that scale-rich metamaterials exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems, including highly tunable elastic anisotropy, delocalized nonlinear deformation with high energy absorption, enhanced energy dissipation under dynamic loading and programmable elastic-wave control. This network-based framework establishes a minimal and universal model for engineering multifunctional materials whose mechanical behaviour emerges directly from scale diversity, and also opens avenues of enquiry for network science itself. A network-science-based framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials is used to produce scale-rich metamaterials that exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems.

title: Cacti are severely threatened by drought in a warming world
abstract: Forecasts of the effects that climate change will have on biodiversity typically rely on long-term climate averages while excluding extreme events. Projections that include severe drought predict that a majority of the 993 cactus species assessed will see large losses of suitable climatic area: more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of it by 2100. Models that ignore extreme events might underestimate the dangers of climate change for this plant family.

title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes
abstract: Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.
