title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
abstract: Eukaryotic genomes are exposed to numerous sources of DNA damage that impede replication. Only a decade ago, repriming by the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL was identified as a pathway that enables cells to tolerate DNA damage1-4. However, the molecular mechanism that underlies repriming remains poorly understood, and it is unclear how PRIMPOL is precisely targeted to stalled forks, where along single-stranded DNA PRIMPOL binds and how PRIMPOL is regulated to minimize error-prone DNA synthesis. Here, to dissect the molecular basis of repriming, we perform real-time single-molecule imaging in nuclear extracts that recapitulate genome maintenance. We directly visualize how stalled forks restart through repriming. We show that PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG). This facilitates primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis. At near-physiological concentrations, PRIMPOL reprimes leading strands in a CMG-dependent manner and polymerase ε extends those primers. This primary mode of repriming does not require DNA damage checkpoint signalling. PRIMPOL overexpression and checkpoint activation promote a secondary mode of repriming, whereby PRIMPOL restarts DNA synthesis far from CMG and polymerase δ extends those primers. Our data reveal a simple yet effective mechanism that directs PRIMPOL's activity to stalled forks awaiting restart, and suggest a strategy to inhibit the repriming pathway.

title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
                    1
                    , in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP)
                    2
                    . Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm
                    1,2
                    . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated
                    3–13
                    . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β-
                    N
                    -acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG–FG and FG–importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations
                    14
                    of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization
                    4,5,7,9,15
                    and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
abstract: Extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1. Their effects on species' distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood2-9. Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Here we integrate new spatial data on severe drought10, including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58-61% to 69-72%. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26-43% to 55-58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1-15% to 25-35%. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69-72% to 84-85% across SSPs. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints
                    1,2
                    . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability
                    3
                    . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image
                    1–4
                    of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features
                    3,5–7
                    , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source
                    8,9
                    . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers
                    1,2
                    . However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples
                    3
                    , collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis1. IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function2,3, with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities4-8. Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health.

title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice
abstract: Nuclei in early mammalian embryos undergo epigenetic reprogramming that enables the zygote to develop into a complete organism. Whereas changes in chromatin state during this critical transition period have been extensively studied1-3, changes in the nucleus that houses chromatin remain poorly understood. Here, using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation methods, we find that nuclei attain profound softness and plasticity during the two-cell embryonic stage in mice, facilitating major zygotic gene activation. The prominent nuclear deformability is attributable to the rapid clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope by the autophagy factor LC3. Nuclear stiffening by lamin B1 retention or its overloading results in incomplete activation of zygotic genes and impaired development. However, embryos that maintain nuclear deformability escape from this transcriptional interference. High-resolution microscopy and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization analyses revealed an accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the deformable nuclear envelope. An engineered molecular tether that stiffens the nuclei restricts these nuclear activities and suppresses expression of key zygotic gene activation genes. Together, our study identifies a distinct physical nuclear state that embryos acquire at the beginning of life that supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene
                    1
                    , and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats
                    2–7
                    , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
abstract: The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth's early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1-3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8-16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740-820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource
                    1
                    . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs
                    2,3
                    . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

title: Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?
abstract: Decades-old papers are increasingly being pulled from the literature, bringing a host of challenges.

title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors
abstract: RNA-derived 2',3'-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1-3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2',3'-cNMPs; 2',3'-cAMP and 2',3'-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3'→5')-guanosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Exogenous application of 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling.

title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity
                    1–5
                    . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)
                    6
                    . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by
                    Nr3c1
                    ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (
                    Rgs2
                    ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of
                    Nr3c1
                    during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation
                    1–9
                    . Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I
                    +
                    –Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn–I
                    2
                    and Al–I
                    2
                    batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation
abstract: Disconnects between in vitro and in vivo results in experimental biology have long been recognized as potential hurdles to understanding health and disease. A prototypical example of such a disconnect is the NLRP3 inflammasome, which mediates inflammation in diverse settings of disease and protective immunity1,2. Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro requires two signals: (1) priming by pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as bacterial lipopolysaccharides and (2) activation by molecules that disrupt cellular homeostasis1,3. By contrast, the NLRP3 inflammasome in vivo is activated by lipopolysaccharide alone. The mechanisms that underlie the difference between in vitro and in vivo activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome are undefined. Here we report that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness is a determinant of NLRP3 activities and that in vitro systems using physiological ECM stiffness enable one-signal in vivo-like NLRP3 activities to occur in human and mouse phagocytes. Physiological ECM stiffness induced expression of the transcription factor NRF2, which was found to be necessary for one-signal NLRP3 activation. Mechanistically, we identify Panx1 as an NRF2-regulated gene that promotes NLRP3 activity. Macrophages derived from the stiff matrix of the bone-osteoclasts-had reduced NRF2 levels and impaired NLRP3 activity. Moreover, alveolar macrophages from patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity. Finally, NRF2 was required for antitumour immunity induced by cancer vaccines consisting of NLRP3 agonistic adjuvants. These findings indicate that NRF2 may be a transcriptional checkpoint that controls NLRP3 inflammasome activity.

title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    TDP-43 nuclear depletion is a defining pathological feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia that induces widespread cryptic splicing defects in hundreds of transcripts
                    1–8
                    . Despite this, whether TDP-43 loss affects synaptic function has remained unclear. Here we show that TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact but suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication. Genetic correction of a single cryptic splicing event in
                    UNC13A
                    was sufficient to rescue these deficits. We developed splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that correct
                    UNC13A
                    cryptic splicing in human cortical and spinal motor neurons and in a humanized mouse model. In human neurons this intervention restored spontaneous and evoked synaptic vesicle release, release probability at individual synapses and wider network synchrony. Together, this establishes
                    UNC13A
                    splice correction as a mechanistically defined and genetically validated therapeutic strategy relevant to roughly 97% of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and roughly 50% of patients with frontotemporal dementia with TDP-43 pathology.

title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    In 2025, a
                    Lancet
                    Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status
                    1
                    . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the
                    Lancet
                    Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity
abstract: Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS-STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45–MCM–GINS) helicase
                    1,2
                    . Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability
                    3–6
                    . Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment
                    4
                    . In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress
                    7–10
                    , but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A
                    9,11
                    is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

title: Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?
abstract: As global energy markets grapple with a period of sustained political volatility, researchers are digging deep for solutions.

title: Personal incentives for public officials drove a drop in China’s fertility
abstract: Once the promotion prospects of bureaucrats became tied to birth targets, the country’s one-child policy became more effective. Can the state now reverse this effect?

title: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method
abstract: A framework for diagnosing obesity that was proposed in 2025 incorporates waist circumference and related measures and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity on the basis of obesity-induced organ dysfunction. In an international multi-cohort study of 844,108 adults, this framework outperformed conventional body-mass-index-based criteria in diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk. A combination of body and organ-function metrics does better at classifying obesity than does body mass index.

title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) displays, originating from early optical see-through head-mounted systems1, have evolved towards lightweight glasses that seamlessly integrate digital information with the physical world2,3. However, their widespread adoption requires compact optical systems that enable bright, wide-field and comfortable viewing. Diffractive waveguides (WGs) offer a promising approach towards lightweight AR displays yet face inherent trade-offs among field of view (FoV), optical efficiency and eyebox size owing to limited degrees of freedom in light control. Here we show an all-day-wearable AR glass prototype based on spatially varying, interwoven metasurfaces that provide several grating vectors for multidirectional light control. The resulting dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide (meta-WG) achieves a 30° FoV and an 8 × 8-mm2 two-dimensional (2D) eyebox while maintaining an average luminance efficiency of 1,938 nits lm-1 (up to 4,225 nits lm-1) within a 1.5-mm-thick form factor. The prototype produces bright and stable virtual images under outdoor ambient illumination, demonstrating the compatibility of meta-WGs with practical wearable display requirements. By expanding the degrees of freedom for light routing beyond conventional diffractive WGs, our approach provides a scalable framework for balancing efficiency, viewing range and form factor, bringing high-performance AR glasses closer to practical consumer applications.

title: Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers
abstract: Scientists are editing microbes to supply more nitrogen to staple crops.

title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1-3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4-7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1-10. Notably, even China's total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China's one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China's total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research.

title: How I balance my life as a professional surfer and a university researcher
abstract: Cliff Kapono shares his advice on ways to navigate and grow two different careers.

title: Nonlinear waveguide polaritons for long-distance propagation of spins at room temperature
abstract: In spintronics, the spin of particles is used to transfer information but the propagation distances are short, whereas photons carry spin further but lack the nonlinear interactions necessary for logic gates. Now, polariton waveguides built from transition metal dichalcogenides enable spin propagation of up to 100 μm at room temperature and maintain large polariton nonlinearities.

title: Interfaces are a nano problem
abstract: Interfaces are a common theme in diverse areas of nanoscience. Understanding and engineering them creates fertile ground for fundamental discoveries and technological advances.

title: Author Correction: Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime
abstract: In the version of the article initially published, in the second paragraph of the “Degradation in realistic conditions” section, the text “lifetime mileage up to 195,000 miles” should have read “lifetime mileage up to 195,000 km”. This correction has been made to the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h
                    −1
                    cm
                    −2
                    , which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%.

title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles
abstract:
Abstract
                  Chemotaxis—directed movement in response to environmental cues—is fundamental to biological systems but remains rare in artificial systems, where it typically relies on complex catalytic pathways or intricate adaptive designs. The molecular mechanisms underlying artificial chemotaxis are still scarce and poorly understood, posing challenges for the rational design of advanced artificial chemotactic systems. Here we present a minimal polymeric system that achieves negative chemotaxis through intrinsic conformational dynamics, enabling mechanical transduction and directional movement without the need for catalysis or external energy input. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular mechanism in which hydrophobic membrane domains dynamically reconfigure in response to chemical signals, triggering a cascade of events, from conformational rearrangements to interfacial tension alterations that generate self-sustained motile behaviour. By elucidating the interplay between membrane dynamics, interfacial forces and directional transport, our findings advance the molecular understanding of synthetic systems that emulate cytoskeletal remodelling in biological motility and establish a versatile framework for engineering functional artificial protocells with life-like behaviours.

title: Zero-excess sodium-metal batteries for post-lithium energy storage
abstract: Zero-excess sodium-metal batteries combine high energy density, resource abundance and simplified manufacturing, positioning them as a potential post-lithium energy-storage technology. This Review examines the promise of this technology, the failure mechanisms and design principles of zero-excess sodium-metal batteries, and their deployment readiness.

title: A high-polarity molecular-anchor design for stable high-mobility perovskite transistors
abstract: Molecular polarity can be used to guide the rational and targeted design of additives that suppress ion migration in metal halide perovskite transistors, leading to mobilities of over 40 cm2 V−1 s−1 and stabilities of over 9,000 on/off cycles.

title: Designing additives for perovskite transistors using molecular polarity as a guide
abstract: Molecular polarity can be used as a predictive descriptor to screen potential additives for halide perovskite lattices, allowing robust and high-performance tin-based perovskite transistors to be created.

title: Making van der Waals heterostructures through substitution
Turnstile metal–organic framework for the efficient separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons
abstract: The industrial separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons is crucial but challenging. Now, a metal–organic framework is developed that features –CF3 pairs at the pore apertures. Through a synergy of thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientation locking, this ‘turnstile’ metal–organic framework enables the stepwise separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane.

title: Using industrial ecology to avoid burden shifting
abstract: Industrial ecology can improve the environmental coherence of low-carbon chemical innovation by avoiding burden shifting across materials, ecosystems, places and time.

title: Orientational locking in a turnstile metal–organic framework for cyclohexene/cyclohexane separation
abstract: This study presents a metal–organic framework that enables the stepwise ternary separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane via two temperature-tuned fixed-bed columns operated at room temperature and higher temperatures, exploiting thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientational locking for selective discrimination.

title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential for the transition of the energy sector and the achievability of climate objectives are not well understood. Here, using the Integrated Assessment Modeling framework REMIND–MAgPIE, we derive future mitigation pathways under different AFOLU policy portfolios. We show that, without AFOLU contributions to mitigation, limiting warming to 1.5 °C is out of reach within the twenty-first century and for keeping peak warming below 1.7 °C consumption loss relative to a current-policy baseline increases from 1.3% to 3.5%. A portfolio of options alleviates the burden of energy sector decarbonization and substantially reduces energy price markups, but puts the AFOLU sector under stress. We show that prudent policy measures, such as limiting total bioenergy use to 100 EJ yr
                    −1
                    and restricting CH
                    4
                    and N
                    2
                    O pricing to US$75 per tonne of CO
                    2
                    equivalent, can largely attenuate this pressure by reducing the need for yield increases and diminishing food price markups without severely compromising the achievability of climate targets. Our findings highlight both the need for effective climate action in the AFOLU sector and the importance of balanced and judicious sectorally aligned policies.

title: A Multicyclic Catalytic Network Enabling ROS Amplification, Metabolic Disruption, and Immune Modulation for Antitumor–Antibacterial Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Intratumoral bacteria are increasingly recognized as important regulators of tumor progression, immune suppression, and metastasis, whereas current therapeutic strategies remain insufficient to address the coupled tumor–bacteria microenvironment. Here, we report a multicyclic catalytic network (VBC-Net) that integrates alkaline polyoxovanadate with a Bi2WO6–CuSx p–n heterojunction for coordinated antitumor–antibacterial immunotherapy. Unlike conventional single-mechanism nanozymes, VBC-Net establishes interconnected catalytic cycles that sustain ROS amplification, oxygen activation, and glutathione depletion, thereby converting transient catalytic activity into persistent oxidative stress. Simultaneously, the alkaline microenvironment and Bi-associated interference with respiratory-chain-related processes may contribute to metabolic perturbation, coupling oxidative stress with metabolic disruption. VBC-Net is further associated with dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced T-cell infiltration, and pro-inflammatory immune modulation, suggesting remodeling of the tumor–bacteria–immune microenvironment. In murine 4T1 tumor and MRSA-infected models, VBC-Net achieves pronounced tumor suppression, bacterial clearance, reduced metastatic progression, and accelerated wound healing with good biocompatibility. This work establishes a multicyclic catalytic strategy for targeting complex tumor-associated ecosystems and provides a promising framework for antitumor–antibacterial therapy.

title: Molecular Anchoring and Multiscale Porosity Synergize in 3D Printed Polyimide Composites for High-Temperature Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The large-scale application of energy storage systems such as lithium-ion batteries, which feature high energy density and considerable flammability risks, has created an urgent demand for thermal management materials that offer lightweight construction, high-temperature resistance, efficient insulation, and customizable shaping. Polyimide (PI) is a promising candidate; however, its additive manufacturing is constrained by the high temperatures required for thermal imidization and the severe shrinkage that accompanies this process. To overcome these limitations, herein, an interfacial chemical anchoring strategy is introduced, through which amino-functionalized hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) are covalently integrated into a soluble PI matrix. The achieved composite ink is well-suited for vapor-induced phase separation (VIPS)-assisted direct ink writing (DIW), allowing in situ porosification. The 3D printed constructs thus feature a hierarchical thermal resistance architecture, including macroscopic air gaps from printing, microporous networks derived from phase separation, and hollow HGM cavities, which synergistically suppresses solid conduction, gas convection, and thermal radiation. In addition, the covalently anchored microspheres also serve as crosslinking nodes, enhancing compressive strength. The optimized composites achieve a 35% reduction in density, shrinkage below 5%, a thermal conductivity of 0.048 W·m–1·K–1, and a nearly fourfold improvement in compressive strength. Together, these results demonstrate that the synergy between interfacial chemical anchoring and VIPS-assisted DIW provides a versatile platform for engineering lightweight, high-strength insulation components with tailored geometries for demanding high-temperature applications.

title: Enzyme-Powered Nanomotor as a Mobile Immobilization Carrier for Facilitating the Enzymatic Degradation of Chitin
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chitin, the second most abundant biomass after cellulose on earth, can be degraded into chitin oligosaccharides (CHOS), which hold considerable commercial value. However, the sustainable bioconversion of chitin is impeded by its mass transfer limitations and poor accessibility of chitinase to the substrate. Herein, a Janus urease-powered nanomotor (JUNM) was synthesized via a facile approach and employed as an immobilization carrier for chitinase (Chi B) to improve the enzymatic production of CHOS. It was demonstrated that the structural asymmetry of JUNM enabled the asymmetric decomposition of urea, thereby achieving more efficient self-propulsion at low urea concentrations than a symmetric urease-powered nanomotor (UNM). The self-propulsive behavior of the resulting immobilized chitinase nanomotor (Chi B@JUNM) enhanced its enzymatic performance. Compared with the passive counterpart, the enhanced enzyme–substrate contact induced by the autonomous movement and by the substrate adsorption resulting from electrostatic interactions improved the substrate affinity (a 50% decrease in apparent Km) and led to a 53% increase in catalytic efficiency (apparent kcat·Km–1). Moreover, the immobilization of Chi B on JUNM exhibited typical advantages of enhanced stability and reusability. As a result, the final CHOS yield achieved by the self-propelled Chi B@JUNM (with 50 mM urea) was 1.34 and 2.15 times the yield of passive Chi B@JUNM and free Chi B, respectively. Taken together, the reported enzyme-powered nanomotor provided an efficient platform for chitin degradation and paved the way for the design of advanced immobilization carriers to facilitate enzymatic reactions.

title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

title: Superhydrophobic Self-Cleaning Polyvinyl Alcohol-Based Films for Enhanced Passive Radiative Cooling and Durability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing sustainable and durable superhydrophobic passive radiative cooling materials is crucial for reducing building energy consumption in a warming world, yet conventional radiative cooling materials often rely on nonrenewable polymeric substrates and fluorosiloxane-based surface modifiers, and present materials have poor durability of superhydrophobicity under harsh conditions, limiting their environmental sustainability and long-term applicability. Herein, we develop a biomass-derived superhydrophobic radiative cooling film by integrating waste straw cellulose with starch and poly(vinyl alcohol) as a renewable film-forming matrix, TiO2 as a solar-reflection filler, and a fluorosiloxane-free surface engineering strategy. The resulting cooling film exhibits a solar reflectance of 76.06% and an infrared emissivity of 96.66% within the atmospheric window. The film achieves an average temperature reduction of 28.2 °C relative to the blank cavity during the test period. Moreover, the superhydrophobic surface imparts excellent self-cleaning capability and enables the film to withstand acid/alkali corrosion, water washing, and prolonged high-temperature treatment (>100 °C for 8 h), demonstrating its robust environmental durability. Beyond passive thermal regulation, the cooling film exhibits an excellent water collection rate of 2476.2 mg cm–2 h–1. The combination of renewable agricultural waste as the structural feedstock, fluorosiloxane-free superhydrophobicity, efficient solar reflection, high infrared emission, and multifunctional environmental stability distinguishes the cooling film from conventional petroleum-based radiative cooling systems. This work provides a sustainable materials-design strategy for converting agricultural waste into multifunctional radiative cooling materials with potential applications in energy-efficient building envelopes and sustainable thermal management.

title: Electric-Field-Driven Surface Ionic Transport on Hydroxylated SiO2 Governs Transient Leakage and Hybrid Bonding Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding is critical for 3D integrated circuit packaging, where dielectric surface activation impacts bonding quality and long-term reliability. NaOH-based wet chemical activation is a promising approach for a scalable and cost-effective processing under ambient conditions. However, this route introduces residual ions at the SiO2 surface, raising concerns regarding electrical leakage and dielectric stability. In this study, electric-field-driven surface ionic transport on NaOH-activated SiO2 and its role in transient leakage and hybrid bonding reliability were investigated. Reversible and polarity-dependent transient current peaks observed in cyclic electrical measurements provide evidence for electric-field-driven migration of the mobile ionic species at the SiO2 interface. In addition, higher NaOH concentrations promoted greater residual Na+ accumulation and intensified transient leakage peaks, supporting the selection of 0.5 M NaOH as an effective activation condition. Systematic decoupling experiments demonstrate that residual mobile Na+ ions are the dominant contributors to the transient leakage current rather than fixed hydroxyl groups. Quantitative analysis reveals Na+ surface mobility of approximately 3 × 10–10 m2V–1s–1, an order-of-magnitude upper-bound estimate that is consistent between constant-bias and ramped-bias measurements and about six orders of magnitude higher than that in bulk SiO2, suggesting a surface-dominated transport. An optimized 3 min deionized water (DI) rinse reduces the mobile Na+ population below the electrical detection limit and decreases the Na 1s XPS intensity by roughly an order of magnitude, suppressing the transient leakage to near-baseline levels while maintaining hydrophilicity and achieving the SiO2–SiO2 bonding strength of 19.7 ± 1.8 MPa, comparable to Ar plasma activation. The leakage measurements were performed on Cu/SiO2 damascene comb structures, whereas the bonding validation addresses the dielectric part of the hybrid-bonding interface; Cu–Cu contact and long-term stress testing remain to be verified. This work provides a framework for understanding electric-field-driven surface ionic transport and practical guidelines for contamination control of the dielectric surface in wet-activated Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding.

title: A Rutin–Glycyrrhizic Acid Self-Assembled Nanohydrogel Promotes Early Osteogenic Differentiation Potential and Antioxidant Activity via Synergistic Inhibition of the IL-1β/NF-κB Axis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Plant-derived natural compounds have gained increasing attention in biomaterial development due to their intrinsic bioactivity and favorable biocompatibility. The anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and osteogenic properties of rutin and glycyrrhizic acid have rendered them increasingly attractive candidates for therapeutic biomaterial development. However, their poor bioavailability significantly restricts their broad biomedical applications. Inspired by a supramolecular self-assembly strategy, we successfully constructed a rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU–GA). The microstructure and formation mechanism were investigated through experimental characterization and computational simulations. Rutin (RU) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) self-assemble into a carrier-free hydrogel in aqueous solution via hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking interactions, exhibiting favorable injectability, shapeability, and stability. RU–GA can disperse in water and release rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanoparticles (RG NPs) with homogeneous particle sizes, while the hydrogel material possesses degradation and sustained-release properties. The bioavailability of RU and GA is synergistically improved through size effects and continuous release. Notably, the RU–GA hydrogel significantly promotes antioxidant activity and early osteogenic differentiation potential relative to the individual monomer components. Bioinformatics analysis further suggested that these bioactivities are associated with IL1B. Il1b knockdown experiments validated that RU and GA may synergistically suppress IL-1β-mediated NF-κB activation, thereby reducing oxidative stress and enhancing early osteogenic differentiation potential. Collectively, the rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU–GA) represents a promising functional biomaterial, providing a strategy for the broad application of natural compounds in biomedical and related fields.

title: Effective Suppression of Cu+-Migration Assisted Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells with Cu2O as the Hole Transport Layer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formamidinium-based double-cation perovskite solar cells exhibit rapid performance degradation when the Cu2O hole transport layer is in direct contact with the perovskite. This degradation is attributed to Cu+ migration into the perovskite lattice, causing structural distortion and the formation of CuI and PbI2. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects Cu+ ions even at the antipodal surface of the perovskite, indicating long-range diffusion of the Cu+ ions, probably through grain-boundary migration. To suppress this, a thin film of benzotriazole is introduced at the Cu2O/perovskite interface as a diffusion-blocking layer that also provides mild surface passivation. Adding poly(acrylonitrile-co-methyl acrylate) to the perovskite synthesis solution passivates the grain boundaries and further prevents the migration of Cu+ towards the perovskite. These modifications effectively curb Cu+ migration and its reaction with the perovskite. Consequently, p-i-n perovskite solar cells with the architecture ITO/Cu2O/perovskite/C60/BCP/Ag, incorporating both modifications, exhibit a significant improvement in power conversion efficiency, from ≈4.7 to 14.4%.

title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ > G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

title: Multiscale Intercalation Strategies for Reconstructing Lamellar MXene Membranes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lamellar MXene membranes, constructed by stacking MXene nanosheets to form two-dimensional nanochannels with ultrafast transport and sieving ability, have emerged as a promising platform for molecular and ionic separations as well as osmotic energy harvesting. However, the performance of these MXene membranes is often constrained by swelling-induced unstable nanochannels and monotonous chemistry environments within nanochannels. One of the most effective routes to these challenges lies in the incorporation of functional intercalation matters into the confined nanochannels of MXene, which not only orchestrate interlayer spacing and nanochannel chemistry but also improve stability by forming multiple interactions with neighboring nanosheets. Over the past decade, a series of multiscale intercalation matters have been designed and explored, mainly spanning from ions to small molecules, polymers, and nanomaterials. Despite significant achievements, a timely and comprehensive review that systematically elucidates how various multiscale intercalation matters reconstruct MXene membranes is missing. In this review, we discuss recent advances in intercalation strategies for lamellar MXene membranes, categorized by the chemical nature and dimensionality of the intercalating matters. We underscore their critical roles in modulating both the structural and chemical features of nanochannels, and we systematically analyze the corresponding effects on transport behavior and separation performance. Finally, some key unresolved challenges and future directions are highlighted to guide the design and synthesis of high-performance lamellar MXene membranes.

title: Monolithic Fabrication of Flexible Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Synapses with Bandgap-Engineered Centimeter-Scale SnSe2 van der Waals Layers
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The transition of bandgap energies in two-dimensional (2D) materials driven by their miniaturization opens up opportunities for emerging device technologies unattainable with conventional approaches. Herein, “all” 2D optoelectronic synapse devices are reported employing the transition characteristics of wafer-scale 2D tin diselenide (SnSe2) layers directly grown on polymeric substrates at a low temperature of 300 °C. Specifically, a significant thickness-dependent reduction in their band energy from 0.8 to 0.25 eV enables a “monolithic” fabrication of flexible device arrays composed of extremely thin active/passive components; i.e., n-type semiconducting 2D channels seamlessly interfaced with heavily doped metallic-like 2D electrodes. These 2D/2D interfaces exhibit reliable Ohmic transports without the need for work function engineering of contact metals as well as well-preserved mechanical deformability. A variety of optoelectronic synaptic properties are demonstrated in the all-2D devices, including deformation-invariant plasticity updates, which are implementable for high-accuracy pattern recognition of artificial neural networks (ANNs). This study suggests new methodologies for integrating the dimensionally tunable electrical properties of near atom-thickness materials into their scalable manufacturability for emergent neuromorphic applications.

title: Fe-Regulated Sulfidation of Ni-MOF to Construct an Fe-Ni(OH)2/Ni3S2 Heterojunction for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution in Both Acidic and Alkaline Media
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and durable non-precious electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in both acidic and alkaline media is a critical challenge. Herein, we report a Fe-regulated sulfidation strategy that converts a Ni-MOF precursor into a Fe-doped Ni(OH)2/Ni3S2 heterojunction catalyst. Fe acts as a kinetic phase regulator that suppresses the complete conversion of Ni(OH)2 into Ni3S2, stabilizing a mixed phase architecture with abundant heterointerfaces and enlarged electrochemically active surface area. The optimized catalyst delivers exceptional HER performance, requiring overpotentials of only 163.3 mV at –10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and 214.3 mV at –100 mA cm−2 in 0.5 M H2SO4, along with outstanding durability (200 h at –500 mA cm−2 in alkaline electrolyte and 100 h at –100 mA cm−2 in acidic electrolyte). Post-stability characterizations reveal pH-dependent reconstruction: under alkaline conditions, the Ni(OH)2 phase partially dissolves while the Ni3S2 framework remains; under acidic conditions, Fe2+ oxidation to Fe3+ forms a protective M-OH-rich oxide layer on Ni3S2. Density functional theory calculations identify Ni as the primary active site, with Fe functioning as an electronic modulator that redistributes electron density toward Ni and optimizes the d-band center. In alkaline media, the cooperative charge effect and upshifted d-band center synergistically promote water dissociation, with OH* desorption identified as the rate-determining step; in acidic media, strong electrostatic attraction from the highly negatively charged Ni sites dominates H* adsorption. This work highlights the pivotal role of heterojunction engineering and phase regulation in designing durable pH-universal HER catalysts.

title: Nanofibrous Thermo-Optical Materials for Spacecraft Passive Thermal Control
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Passive thermal control is essential for spacecraft operating in extreme extraterrestrial environments, where minimizing solar heat absorption while maximizing thermal radiation is critical for maintaining acceptable onboard temperatures without additional energy consumption. Here, electrospun nanofibrous materials, represented by a polymeric polytetrafluoroethylene:polyethylene oxide (PTFE:PEO) composite and ceramic silica, are introduced as a new class of lightweight spacecraft thermal control materials combining ultrahigh solar reflectance (or ultralow solar absorptance), strong infrared emittance, and environmental durability.
