title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacterial pangenomes provide a shared reservoir of antiphage defenses, yet the ecological and functional constraints shaping this reservoir remain unclear. Here, we combine comparative genomics of 206 Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) genomes with cross-infection assays of 50 strains against 36 phages and heterologous expression of 24 defense systems in a phage-sensitive Xoo chassis. The Xoo pan-defensome comprises a conserved core of 9 subtypes and a variable layer of 35 accessory and cloud subtypes structured by host phylogeography. Phages are more infectious on sympatric than allopatric hosts, consistent with local adaptation. Variable systems show stronger apparent activity than core systems, whereas resistance breadth is not predicted by defense system number. Co-expression of representative co-occurring and mutually exclusive system pairs reveals synergistic and antagonistic interactions underlying non-random repertoire assembly. Together, these findings extend the pan-immunity framework by showing that population-level immune reservoirs are shaped by both ecological structure and functional compatibility.

title: Robust hydrogel ion channels for osmotic energy harvesting and environmental sensing
abstract: Salinity gradient blue energy offers a promising alternative to fossil fuels. Here the authors develop ultrarough, self-healing hydrogel ionic conductors that achieve an excellent power density while maintaining over 91% of their performance after damage and enable autonomous environmental sensing.

title: scMomer: a pretraining framework for inferring robust cellular representations from single-cell transcriptomes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-quality cellular representations are important for understanding complex biological systems. However, due to limitations in both data availability and practical utility, most existing computational methods are designed for a single modality (e.g., scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq), restricting their ability to capture cellular heterogeneity. Here, we propose scMomer, a multistage pretraining framework designed to infer robust cellular representations by integrating multimodal knowledge into scRNA-seq-only inputs. The framework progressively learns through three stages. Firstly, it pretrains unimodal encoders on single-modality datasets to obtain modality-specific representations. Secondly, it aligns these modalities using paired data to learn joint representations. Thirdly, it applies knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge of the missing modality (scATAC-seq) into a cross-modal student encoder, enabling the inference of multimodal-aware representations from scRNA-seq-only inputs. We perform extensive experiments show that the representations learned by scMomer achieve superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods across diverse tasks, including cross-modality translation, cell annotation, drug response prediction, perturbation prediction, and gene property prediction, demonstrating its robustness and versatility. Overall, we demonstrate that scMomer enables unimodal data to yield robust cellular representations, providing an effective solution to missing-modality modeling.

title: Engineering Ultrathin, Tough Polymer Networks for Stable Lithium Metal Anode Interphases
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial degradation and dendritic lithium (Li) growth remain critical bottlenecks for practical Li metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we introduce a tough, ion-conductive poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (pDMAEMA) nanolayer on Li metal via photo-initiated chemical vapor deposition (piCVD). The photo-mediated, solvent-free piCVD enables nanometer-scale coatings with systematic control over photo-crosslinking and chain entanglement without compromising Li surface integrity. This systematic control yields an optimized polymer network balancing toughness (36.3 MJ m–3) and viscoelasticity (10.3% linear viscoelastic strain limit) to accommodate repeated Li volume changes. Furthermore, interactions between pDMAEMA and PF6– anions promote a mechanically durable LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, thereby supporting uniform Li deposition. Pouch-type bi-cells employing the optimized 100 nm polymer-coated Li anode achieve an energy density of 338 Wh kg–1 and 80% capacity retention after 90 cycles under practical conditions (N/P = 2, E/C = 3 g Ah–1). This ultrathin, tough polymer network offers a promising design principle for high-energy LMBs.

title: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) regulate plant development, stress responses and genome stability by guiding ARGONAUTE (AGO) proteins to their targets. AGO1 is the major effector of microRNA (miRNA) and 21/22-nucleotide (nt) secondary small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways in Arabidopsis thaliana. However, how AGO1 subcellular dynamics shape sRNA loading and silencing remained unclear. Here, we validate a functional nuclear localization signal (NLS) in the N-terminal extension of AGO1 and identify IMPORTIN α2 (IMPα2) as a nuclear import factor acting within a larger importin α network. Using engineered nuclear-only and cytoplasmic-only AGO1 variants, we show that exclusive cytoplasmic AGO1 allows full miRNA target repression and secondary siRNA production in ago1 mutants, whereas nuclear-retained AGO1 only partially rescues miRNA function and exerts a dominant-negative effect on secondary siRNA biogenesis. sRNA immunoprecipitation assay reveals that miRNAs are preferentially loaded into AGO1 in the nucleus, while tasiRNA loading predominantly occurs in the cytoplasm. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that AGO1 spatial partitioning itself quantitatively shapes the efficiency and specificity of sRNA loading and the silencing outputs.

title: Towards practical photosynthetic biohybrid systems
abstract: Photosynthetic biohybrid systems can convert sunlight to chemicals and fuels. This Perspective explores how to better design photosynthetic biohybrid systems to achieve practical sustainable solar-driven biomanufacturing.

title: Cellulose-Derived Water-Free, Anti-Freezing, and Self-Initiated Ionogel for Flexible Wearable Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable flexible electronics has positioned cellulose as a promising candidate, yet its efficient dissolution and functionalization remain challenging due to its highly crystalline structure and strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. While a wide variety of cellulose dissolution systems have been reported in the literature, most systems still depend on toxic initiators or complex processes. Herein, we report a sunlight-driven, initiator-free green synthesis of cellulose-based ionogels that enables direct cellulose dissolution and in situ photopolymerization, which provides a facile and sustainable route to anti-freezing ionogels via the direct in situ polymerization of ionogel precursors without initiators or crosslinkers. Notably, the incorporation of cellulose, along with the intrinsic properties of the 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([Bmim]Cl) and ethylene glycol (EG) significantly enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive ionogel, which exhibited outstanding mechanical performance (fracture strain of 935%, fracture stress of 166.5 kPa), robust adhesive properties (1.48 MPa), excellent conductivity (0.028 mS·cm–1) and wide work temperature range (–20∼60 °C). These properties enabled the ionogel to function not only as a wearable strain sensor for motion detection but also as a self-powered controller for operating a remote-controlled car via human-computer interaction. This work provides a versatile and sustainable strategy for fabricating high-performance cellulose ionogels, paving the high value-added way for future soft electronic systems with multifunctional integration.

title: Porous-Architectured Composite for Fully 3D-Printed Biodegradable Soft Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Biodegradable electronics offer the promise of implantable devices that disappear after use, reducing the need for surgical removal and mitigating chronic inflammatory responses. Achieving both tissue-level mechanical softness and sufficient electrical conductivity is critical for bioelectronics. Composite materials provide a versatile platform to satisfy these electrical and mechanical requirements, while 3D printing allows precise and customizable fabrication of complex and multi-material structures. However, in fully biodegradable composites, limited material options restrict simultaneous optimization of mechanical and electrical properties. Here, we introduce engineered internal porosity into a biodegradable electronic composite to achieve softer mechanical properties while maintaining electrical performance. In metal-polymer composites, a porous matrix promotes filler aggregation, forming a percolating conductive network at a lower filler loading compared to non-porous counterparts, thereby reducing stiffness. Engineered porosity within the printed structure reduces its elastic modulus by orders of magnitude and accelerates degradation. We also demonstrate multi-material 3D printing of porosity-programmed electronic inks for printed circuit boards and sensors applications. This structural strategy can be extended to other biodegradable filler-binder systems, thereby expanding the material palette for next-generation transient electronics.

title: A Biomimetic Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoreactor Reshapes ROS Homeostasis and Activates STING Pathway for Synergistic Chemodynamic–Immunotherapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The combination of chemodynamic therapy (CDT) and immunotherapy offers a promising therapeutic paradigm for advanced cancer treatment, yet its translation is largely hindered by inadequate intratumoral reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and the lack of a robust link between ROS-induced cytotoxicity and durable immune activation. To address these challenges, we herein engineer a multifunctional biomimetic nanoplatform (ZMGM) by encapsulating Mn2+ and glucose oxidase (GOX) within zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8), followed by surface functionalization with 4T1 breast cancer cell membranes. This design integrates three synergistic functions: (1) GOX depletes glucose and generates hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) within the acidic tumor microenvironment; (2) the produced H2O2 fuels the Mn2+-mediated Fenton-like reaction to amplify ROS production; and (3) Mn2+ simultaneously serves as a potent stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist, triggering type-I interferon responses and promoting dendritic cell maturation. Meanwhile, the homologous cancer cell membrane coating endows ZMGM with specific tumor homing and enhanced tumor localization. Both in vitro and in vivo findings demonstrate that ZMGM not only efficiently eradicates primary tumors but also induces a systemic antitumor immune response, characterized by increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, that effectively suppresses distant metastatic lesions. Notably, the synergistic CDT–STING immunotherapy achieves a primary tumor inhibition rate of 84.22% without obvious systemic toxicity. This work provides a paradigm for rationally designing a single nanoplatform that bridges ROS-mediated cell killing and innate immune activation, offering a promising avenue for combating metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.

title: Dual Conical Fibers for Controllable Liquid Transfer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solution processes, especially those using open systems, have shown advantages of mild conditions, cost-effectiveness, and broad substrate compatibility in making micro-patterned functional films of optoelectronic devices. Owing to the extreme dynamics of liquids, finely controlling liquid transfer remains largely unsolved, particularly across dimensions from μm- to cm-scale. Here, we propose a model structure of dual conical fibers (dual-CFs) that enables liquid transfer to proceed in a well-controllable manner for micro-patterning. The critical structural parameters for fully holding liquid within dual-CFs are clarified, and quantitative correlations between fiber topology and steady liquid transfer are established. The dual-parallel-fibrous structure, representing the minimum number of CFs for the structure model, helps suppress Plateau–Rayleigh instability by virtue of the confined noncircular cross-sectional liquid film; while the conical structure enables effectively holding liquid, without any leakage during the transfer process, due to the as-generated Laplace pressure difference. The dual-CFs benefit from minimizing the rupture energy of the liquid film by the minimal cross-sectional area confined at the tips, which leads to finely anchoring the three-phase contact line. As a synergistic consequence, liquid can be transferred onto substrates in a controllable manner, resulting in micro-patterns with well-defined profiles. More importantly, the model structure of dual-CFs can be programmably arranged into multi-conical fiber arrays, by which direct-writing micro-patterns from μm-scale microlines to cm-scale uniform films can be realized. The direct-writing strategy is applicable for making functional micro-patterns, offering inspiration for micro-patterning liquid materials using fibrous open systems.

title: Ionic Liquids and Deep Eutectic Solvents as Functional Interfacial Phases in Membrane-Based Separations
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this Spotlight on Applications, we describe our progress in developing membrane-based separation processes in which ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) act as functional interfacial phases rather than merely as alternative solvents or extractants. Starting from stability limitations identified in supported ionic liquid membranes, our work evolved toward architectures in which polymeric materials selectively contact, confine, distribute, or stabilize ionic and eutectic liquid phases. We organize these contributions according to the location and function of the active interface: external polymer–ionic liquid interfaces in dense membrane systems; localized ionic or eutectic phases confined within multilayer membrane architectures; distributed polymer–DES domains in dense hybrid membranes; membrane-stabilized contact with mobile immiscible liquid phases; and liquid–vapor–membrane interfaces in ionic-liquid-driven osmotic distillation. Each architecture builds on an established membrane-process category – perstraction, coated liquid membranes, polymer inclusion membranes, membrane contactors, and osmotic distillation – and is distinguished by the location, flow regime, and function of the ionic or eutectic phase. These configurations were applied to fermentation-product recovery, selective separation of target molecules, ethanol dehydration, food concentration, and water recovery from saline streams. Across these applications, performance emerged from the synergistic coupling of polymer sorption and diffusion, liquid-phase affinity, wetting, morphology, interfacial stability, and resistance distribution. COSMO-RS provided a complementary progression from solute–ionic-liquid screening to direct polymer screening and, subsequently, to thermodynamic interpretation of hybrid polymer–eutectic membrane environments. Collectively, these studies indicate that the polymer, ionic or eutectic phase, solute, interface, operating mode, and membrane architecture should be designed as an integrated interfacial system.

title: Cu-Doped Highly Porous SnO2 for Long-Lasting Acidic CO2 Electroreduction at 1000 mA cm–2
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) to formic acid (HCOOH) provides a carbon-neutral route. SnO2-based catalysts suffer from limited activity and instability at industrial current densities. We develop a Cu-doped highly porous SnO2 catalyst (SnO2-Cu) that enhances activity and stabilizes the SnO2 framework. The porous structure exposes numerous active sites while confining local OH– within the bulk acid electrolyte, enabling high-current-density operation. Cu doping strengthens CO2 chemisorption and Sn–O bond covalency, boosting CO2RR activity while suppressing SnO2 self-reduction. SnO2-Cu sustains 1000 mA cm–2 for 19 h with 98.5% FE and 800 mA cm–2 for 72 h with 94.1% FE in a flow cell at pH 1.82. It achieves a HCOOH production cost of 722.7 USD tonne–1 in a solid-state electrolyte (SSE) device calculated based on onshore wind power, demonstrating economic competitiveness. This work demonstrates that rational Cu doping of porous SnO2 addresses activity and durability limits, offering an effective platform for high-rate, economically viable HCOOH electrosynthesis.

title: Ultrasound-Responsive Iron-Barium Titanate Schottky Heterojunction-Embedded Hydrogel Accelerates Burn Wound Healing through Bidirectional Hydrogen-Piezocatalytic Redox Modulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Burn wound healing is regulated by a spatiotemporal redox hierarchy, where early reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload drives inflammation, while late ROS deficiency hinders regeneration. Programming this bidirectional sequence requires time-phased, counter-directional ROS control. Herein, we report a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates hydrogen therapy with piezocatalytic therapy, enabling on-demand redox programming across the entire healing cascade. The system constructs a metal-semiconductor Schottky heterojunction derived from the in situ reduction of Fe2+ within the mesopores of barium titanate. The mesoporous confinement and interfacial coupling program the hydrolysis of nanoscale zero-valent iron for sustained, early-stage hydrogen delivery to scavenge toxic ROS, while the established Schottky barrier efficiently suppresses charge recombination, thereby executing ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization and charge separation for on-demand ROS generation in later-stage pro-regenerative signaling. Embedded within a polyacrylamide/carboxymethyl chitosan double-network hydrogel with inherent antibacterial activity, the resulting system exhibits superior antioxidant capacity and piezocatalytic responsivity, as well as promotion of fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse burn model, this redox-programmable platform orchestrates phased healing, attenuating early inflammation, sustaining neovascularization, and suppressing late fibrosis, achieving accelerated wound closure. Collectively, this work establishes a redox programming paradigm via heterojunction catalysis, coupling spatiotemporal ROS scavenging and generation for dynamic tissue regeneration.

title: Synergistic Effect of Hybrid Polarized Spin Currents Enables Sub-Nanosecond and Energy-Efficient Field-Free Switching on a Wafer-Scale Platform
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spin–orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory (SOT-MRAM) exhibits intrinsic potential for next-generation magnetic memory, whereas robust wafer-level field-free switching (FFS) of nanosized perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (pMTJ) remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, we present a robust FFS of 90 nm pMTJs on 300 mm wafers driven by the synergistic effect of y- and z-polarized spin currents generated at the antiferromagnetic (AFM)/nonmagnetic (NM) interface. Experimental results demonstrate that an appropriate combination of both y- and z-spin polarizations is able to significantly improve the FFS performance. 90 nm pMTJ arrays are fabricated on 300 mm wafers, where a mean tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 140%, an endurance of exceeding 1012 cycles, and a robust field-free SOT switching at sub-nanosecond (down to 0.2 ns) are simultaneously achieved. Robust FFS is observed at temperature up to 100 °C, and the switching polarity remains unchanged after 1T magnetic field disturbance. With the assistance of the voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the switching current density is reduced by 20% and the switching energy can be as low as 0.35 pJ/bit. This work paves the way for SOT-MRAM toward commercialization.

title: Engineering CAR-Vδ2 T cells to boost persistence and anti-tumor function
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-modified Vδ2 T cells are an attractive therapeutic cell platform for cancer immunotherapy. However, their clinical efficacy is limited by short in vivo persistence due to insufficient cytokine support and high susceptibility to activation-induced cell death (AICD). Through comparison of membrane-bound (mb) cytokines, we identified mbIL-18 to support superior anti-tumor activity of CAR-Vδ2 T cells in vitro and in vivo. To reduce constitutive surface exposure of IL-18 and enable antigen-driven signal 3, we fused MyD88 - the key IL-18R signaling mediator - to an extracellular domain of Fas (Fas88). Antigen stimulation-induced FasL engagement of Fas88 triggered IL-18 signaling while simultaneously protecting Vδ2 T cells from AICD. Fas88-armed human CAR-Vδ2 T cells produced superior yet stimulation-dependent in vivo expansion and functional persistence in xenograft models of hematologic and solid malignancies. Together, these findings highlight the importance of IL-18 signaling and AICD resistance for CAR-Vδ2 T cell activity, enabling a single-transgene modification to limit inflammatory risk and facilitate clinical translation.

title: Alkali-Assisted MOCVD Growth of Polycrystalline MoS2 with Micrometer-Scale Domains on Soda-Lime Glass
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving large-scale, uniform MoS2 films with reduced grain boundary density remains a central challenge for scalable device applications. Previous studies have reported that alkali-assisted growth promotes lateral domain expansion through eutectic intermediate formation. Here, metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) of MoS2 on commercial soda-lime glass is investigated. The intrinsic alkali content of soda-lime glass provides a uniform supply across the substrate, while partial surface softening at growth temperature facilitates the incorporation of Mo species within the near-surface region of the glass. The systematic variation of precursor flow conditions enables controlled modulation of nucleation density and domain size while suppressing graphitic carbon co-deposition arising from precursor ligand pyrolysis. High-quality polycrystalline MoS2 with lateral grain sizes ranging from ∼500 nm to 1.5 μm is achieved as uniform, coalesced centimeter-scale films, demonstrating the scalability of this method. Substrate roughness and wafer-to-wafer variability are key factors governing nucleation, highlighting opportunities for substrate optimization. To correlate the material properties with device performance, the films are wet-transferred and integrated into bottom-gated, top-contact field-effect transistors featuring either non-interdigitated or interdigitated source-drain electrodes. The devices exhibit on/off current ratios up to ∼107 and mobilities of ∼8 cm2 V–1 s–1. Overall, this work demonstrates an accessible and scalable route for the growth of electronic-grade polycrystalline MoS2 on soda-lime glass substrates.

title: Depth-Resolved Magnetic Reversal of La0.7Sr0.3Mn1– x Ru x O3-Based Synthetic Antiferromagnets
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Synthetic antiferromagnets based on transition metal oxides provide a versatile platform for engineering magnetic functionalities beyond those of conventional metallic systems. However, the microscopic pathways by which their magnetization reverses remain difficult to determine because conventional magnetic measurements cannot resolve the layer-specific magnetic configurations that emerge during switching. Here, we combine polarized neutron reflectometry, magnetometry, magnetotransport, and an extended Stoner–Wohlfarth model to investigate the magnetization reversal mechanisms in epitaxial La0.7Sr0.3Mn1–xRuxO3/LaNiO3 multilayers. Depth-resolved polarized neutron reflectometry reveals non-collinear magnetic configurations that are hidden from macroscopic probes and identifies the competition between tilted magnetic anisotropy and comparable bilinear and biquadratic interlayer exchange interactions as the origin of the observed behavior. Depending on the magnetic-field orientation, the system undergoes either abrupt switching between magnetic fan and synthetic antiferromagnetic states or a gradual opening of the magnetic fan. Our results establish the intimate connection between magnetic anisotropy, interlayer exchange, and reversal dynamics in oxide synthetic antiferromagnets, revealing correlated oxides as a powerful platform for tuning the balance between competing interactions and engineering tailored magnetic reversal pathways and functionalities.

title: Controllable Synthesis of Porous Core–Shell NiCo Bimetallic Selenides for High-Performance Supercapacitors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF)-derived electrode materials suffer from poor conductivity and structural instability. Herein, a porous core–shell NiCo bimetallic selenide (NiCo PBA–Se) is synthesized via a multistep liquid-phase transformation followed by low-temperature selenization. A Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-67 (ZIF-67) shell is first epitaxially grown on a Ni-MOF core to construct a core–shell MOF hybrid as the precursor for the preparation of subsequent electrode materials. Unlike conventional methods that convert only the outer MOF layer, the precisely controlled ion-exchange process converts both the inner Ni-MOF and outer ZIF-67 into a NiCo-PBA precursor while preserving the core–shell spherical morphology. Gas-phase selenization at 350 °C yields the target product, which retains a three-dimensional porous spherical architecture composed of stacked ultrathin nanosheets. Ni and Co are uniformly incorporated into the selenide lattice, forming a single-phase (Ni, Co)Se2 solid solution that shortens ion transport paths and increases active sites. Kinetic analysis reveals a synergistic combination of diffusion-controlled and capacitance-controlled charge storage, enabling rapid charge/discharge. In three-electrode tests, NiCo PBA–Se delivers a specific capacitance of 1642 F·g–1 (738.9 C·g–1) at 1 A·g–1. The assembled asymmetric supercapacitor achieves an energy density of 42.52 Wh·kg–1 at 775 W·kg–1 and powers an electronic timer for 20 min. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the MOF-on-MOF strategy with full conversion of both core and shell and simultaneous maintenance of the core–shell structure for constructing high-performance multimetal selenides.

title: Structural Insights into Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers after Long-Term Operation Using Advanced 3D Focused Ion Beam–Scanning Electron Microscopy Tomography
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are key to sustainable hydrogen production, but their long-term performance is limited by degradation, particularly in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which remains a barrier to commercial viability. Moreover, the need for corrosion-resistant materials and the intricate fabrication of bipolar plates and porous transport layers (PTLs) further impede large-scale deployment and account for a major share of the stack cost. Because lifetime and replacement costs are strongly influenced by the local microstructure and contact conditions, especially at the anode/PTL interface, a multiscale characterization approach combining 3D focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy (FIB–SEM) with time-of-flight mass spectrometry is used to investigate degradation in an MEA after several thousand hours of operation under industrially relevant conditions. The 3D reconstruction and ppm-level chemical mapping show that local contact heterogeneities at welds in an expanded-metal mesh PTL act as degradation hotspots. At these sites, intensified catalyst utilization accelerates iridium dissolution, driving iridium migration and deposition as extended filaments into the membrane. Concurrently, membrane voids are formed beneath these sites, accompanied by iron contamination detected at both contact types. In contrast, general contact regions mainly show a thin redeposition layer without voids or filaments. These findings provide a mechanistic framework that links local contact conditions and microstructural heterogeneities to coupled catalyst and membrane degradation, supporting design rules for improved PEMWE durability.

title: Rational Synthesis of Sulfonic Acid-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Capture of Trace Strontium in Natural Mineral Water
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As a typical long-lived radionuclide, strontium-90 (90Sr) possesses persistent radiological hazards and exhibits high migratory and diffusive behaviors in groundwater. However, the development of adsorbents for the efficient and highly selective capture of trace Sr(II) remains a great challenge. In this study, covalent organic frameworks (COFs, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H) with different numbers of sulfonic acid groups were rationally synthesized and applied for capturing Sr(II). The introduction of sulfonic acid groups onto TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H endowed them with high adsorption capacities of 136.4 and 68.3 mg g–1 toward Sr(II), which were 12-fold and 6-fold higher than that of TpPa without sulfonic acid groups, respectively. Meanwhile, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H exhibited fast adsorption kinetics, capturing 99% of Sr(II) within 3 and 10 min, respectively. In addition, TpPa-2SO3H also exhibited high selectivity, excellent anti-interference performance, and regeneration ability without high calcium backgrounds. Characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that sulfonic acid groups in TpPa-2SO3H promoted Sr(II) capture through strong ion-exchange interaction. TpPa-2SO3H was further applied to extract trace Sr(II) in natural Sr-containing mineral water samples. The results showed that the extraction efficiency for Sr(II) exceeded 95% within 5 min. Furthermore, the selectivity for Sr(II) was investigated by the distribution coefficients (Kd), and the Kd was 5.6 × 104 mL g–1 for TpPa-2SO3H toward Sr(II), approximately 400 times higher than those of Na(I) and K(I), respectively. This work not only developed a promising strategy to extract trace Sr(II) from real samples but also broadened the application of COFs in separation science.

title: First observation and interpretation of ion cyclotron emission from energetic ions accelerated by lower hybrid waves in a tokamak plasma
abstract: We report the first observation of ion cyclotron emission (ICE) from a tokamak plasma during lower hybrid wave (LHW) injection and electron cyclotron resonance heating. Using a novel approach derived from linear kinetic theory, we infer key parameter values for the LHW-accelerated fast-ion distribution which drives the observed ICE spectra, and for the bulk plasma. These ICE spectra from deuterium plasmas in the EAST tokamak exhibit peaks at successive deuterium cyclotron harmonics, consistent with the collective relaxation of energetic deuterons through the magnetosonic cyclotron instability (MCI). By carrying out a multi-dimensional parameter scan of MCI growth rates in high-resolution two-dimensional ( ) wavenumber space, we obtain best-fit values for: the magnetic field; plasma density; background electron and ion temperature; and the concentration of fast deuterons, together with their energy, pitch ( ) and thermal spread. We find that the observed ICE spectrum is likely driven by 770 keV deuterons, plausibly accelerated through LHW–ion interactions, which then undergo the MCI. The assumptions of the linear analytically based model include an infinite homogeneous plasma, and a ring-beam distribution of fast deuterons. Our results demonstrate a new scenario in which ICE serves as a passive diagnostic of energetic ion populations, and invite further investigation of the ICE–LHW connection.

title: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Threat learning requires rapid adaptation, but how the brain weights successive aversive experiences remains unclear. Here we show that many male mice exhibit delayed freezing acquisition during auditory fear conditioning. A trial-wise discount reinforcement learning model captured these dynamics through transient attenuation of early associative updating. Medial prefrontal neurons projecting to the periaqueductal gray constrained acquisition and subsequent cue-evoked freezing: inhibition increased freezing, whereas activation reduced it. Calcium imaging of individual neurons identified a subpopulation with delayed post-shock responses that declined during learning and predicted the model-derived discount-like variable. Temporally restricted inhibition implicated activity extending beyond the shock in constraining early acquisition. Local somatostatin interneurons showed increasing shock-evoked activity and provided inhibitory input to these projection neurons, suggesting a mechanism for relaxing this constraint. These findings link the trial-wise weighting of aversive experience to a prefrontal inhibitory microcircuit and provide a framework for understanding individual differences in threat memory formation.

Comparative investigation of temperature-dependent defect evolution and irradiation hardening in CVD and ITER-like tungsten
abstract: Chemical vapor deposited tungsten (CVD-W) is known for its high thermal stability of the microstructure and lower susceptibility to deuterium-induced blistering compared to ITER-like W (IL-W). However, it remains unclear whether these advantages extend to displacement damage tolerance. To address this, CVD-W and ITER-like tungsten (IL-W) were irradiated with 6 MeV copper ions up to 0.6 dpa at room temperature (RT), 773 K, and 973 K. Transmission electron microscopy, defect statistics, and nano-indentation revealed comparable damage accumulation and irradiation hardening in both materials across all investigated temperatures. At RT, both materials exhibited dense dislocation networks and loops, together with very sparsely distributed voids, resulting in comparable increases in hardness. At elevated temperatures, these networks disappeared, giving way to dislocation loop strings and dislocation lines, along with an increased density of voids, accompanied by further irradiation hardening. The dispersed barrier hardening model analysis indicates that the dominant contribution to irradiation hardening transitions from dislocation structures at RT to voids at elevated temperatures. In addition, differences in dislocation morphology and nature were observed between the two materials. Displacement damage defects in CVD-W exhibited higher mobility than in IL-W, as evidenced by an expanded damage layer, a higher degree of dislocation loop ordering into one-dimensional strings, a larger fraction of glissile 1/2 dislocation loops, and a greater proportion of loops exceeding 10 nm at ⩾773 K, mainly owing to its lower impurity content. This further supports void-dominated hardening at elevated temperatures, as different dislocation morphologies observed at elevated temperatures had minimal impact on the overall hardening. These findings provide valuable insights into the irradiation response of CVD-W under fusion-relevant conditions.

title: Spatiotemporal Molecular Control of Crystallization for Efficient Perovskite/Organic Tandem Photovoltaics
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perovskite/organic tandem solar cells (PO-TSCs) offer a route toward overcoming the efficiency limitations of single-junction photovoltaics. However, wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite sub-cells limit their performance, where uncontrolled crystallization leads to compositional heterogeneity, defect accumulation, and severe halide phase segregation. Here, we develop a template-bridge dual-control (TBDC) strategy using 2-thiophenemethylammonium bromide (2-ThMAB). Precisely controlling the introduction timing and spatial distribution of 2-ThMAB maximizes molecular regulation of crystallization. Surface-anchored 2-ThMAB molecules act as growth templates to induce (100) crystal growth, while grain-boundary-localized molecules regulate halide migration through molecular bridging, enabling homogeneous crystallization. The WBG perovskite films exhibit enhanced out-of-plane (100) orientation, reduced defect density, and suppressed halide phase segregation. Consequently, the optimized WBG device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.13% with improved operational stability. Integrated into PO-TSCs, the optimized WBG sub-cells deliver a PCE of 26.62%. This strategy enables concurrent control of crystallization and halide redistribution of efficient, stable tandem photovoltaics.

title: Regulation of Anionic Redox Reaction Voltage by Energy Band Modulation for Li-Rich Cathodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anionic redox reaction (ARR) promises high energy density for Li-rich cathodes yet suffers from severe voltage decay. Here, we investigate ARR voltage modulation in a Li2S-modified quasi-solid Li-rich cathode (Li2S-LRM), which exhibits a distinct low-voltage ARR plateau (2.0–2.8 V). Combining in situ XRD, S K-edge XANES, EELS, Ar-etched XPS and DFT calculations, we validate in situ electrochemical sulfur doping. Upon cycling, the material forms bulk LixS/Li–S–O species alongside a dominant Li2SO3/Li2SO4 polyanion interphase that realizes oxygen trapping. Vacancy-cluster formation facilitates reversible S-involved charge compensation, where sulfur redox activity progressively intensifies during long cycling. Enabled by the band-modulation and oxygen-trapping effects, Li2S-LRM achieves a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.6% and suppressed voltage decay (0.28 vs. 0.83 mV cycle–1 for pristine LRM). This work deepens mechanistic insights into ARR and provides rational design guidance for high-performance anionic-redox cathodes.

title: Anion Sublattice Engineering Induced Niobium-Tungsten Oxide with Near-Zero Residual Strain for Stable 100 C Cycling Capability
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wadsley-Roth W3Nb14O44 is a fast-charging anode material but suffers from low electronic conductivity and electrochemical polarization. Here, anion-sublattice engineering is employed to regulate its electronic structure and Li+ storage kinetics. Density functional theory and kinetic analyses reveal that an appropriate concentration of oxygen vacancies enhances electronic conductivity, moderates Li+ adsorption, and facilitates Li+ diffusion, thereby reducing charge-transfer and diffusion impedances at low temperatures. In situ XRD and synchrotron radiation X-ray 3D nanocomputed tomography reveal reversible structural evolution with near-zero residual strain after cycling. Consequently, WNO-x delivers 77.4 mAh g–1 at 200 C and retains 72.6% capacity after 6000 cycles at 100 C while exhibiting low-temperature electrochemical activity. Moreover, the WNO-x||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cell delivers 85.8 mAh g–1 at 20 C and retains 77.1% capacity after 3000 cycles, with cycling capability at –30 °C. Such structure-property insight provides a strategy for designing niobium-based oxide anodes toward fast-charging and low-temperature batteries.

title: Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation to Multicarbon Products: Mechanisms, Catalyst Design, and Scale Demonstration
abstract: Photothermal CO2 hydrogenation to multicarbon products presents a promising route to mitigate global climate change while simultaneously generating valuable C2+ products for industrial use. However, realizing high activity and selectivity toward multicarbon products remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the intricate nature of reactant activation and the inherently sluggish kinetics of C−C coupling. This review elucidates the fundamental principles of photothermal catalysis, with a particular focus on the synergistic interplay between light and thermal energy. In addition, the activation pathways of CO2 to C1 intermediates and the subsequent mechanisms of C−C bond formation leading to multicarbon products are systematically examined. On this basis, catalyst design and modification strategies are categorized to enhance reactant activation and facilitate efficient C−C coupling. Furthermore, recent progress in pilot-scale demonstrations is highlighted to showcase the potential for scalable and sustainable CO2 hydrogenation technologies. By addressing the current challenges and outlining future research directions, this review aims to accelerate the development of efficient photothermal processes for CO2 valorization. Highlights:1 Photothermal synergistic mechanism and reaction pathways from CO2 to C2+ products are systematically elucidated, providing a mechanistic basis for multicarbon product synthesis.2 Photothermal catalyst modification strategies are comprehensively summarized from a pathway-oriented perspective to enhance reactant activation and promote C−C coupling toward C2+ products.3 Recent photothermal scale demonstrations are highlighted, underscoring the practical potential of scalable and sustainable CO2 hydrogenation technologies.

title: Non-ionic Phthalocyanine Additives Enable Synergistic Passivation and Strain Buffering in Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The long-term stability of high-efficiency n-i-p perovskite solar cells is limited by coupled defect migration, residual lattice strain, and thermal–mechanical degradation. Here, we develop a non-ionic, interface-enriched zinc phthalocyanine derivative, 4PCSZnPc, as a molecular stabilizer for simultaneous defect anchoring and strain buffering. Unlike ionic additives that may introduce mobile species, 4PCSZnPc is distributed throughout the film, with enrichment near the buried SnO2/perovskite interface. Peripheral N/O/S heteroatoms coordinate with under-coordinated Pb2+ sites, while the Zn-regulated macrocyclic center interacts with iodide-related defects, forming dual-site Lewis acid–base anchoring. Meanwhile, the rigid phthalocyanine framework reduces residual tensile stress and may hinder strain-assisted ion migration. These combined effects of defect passivation and strain buffering reduce non-radiative recombination, improve film uniformity, and enhance thermal robustness. Consequently, 4PCSZnPc-treated devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.88% (certified 26.74%), a T80 lifetime of 1358 h under 1-sun at 85 °C, and 95% retention after 200 thermal cycles, providing a design principle for future thermally resilient photovoltaics.

Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High‐Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure
abstract: ABSTRACT Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities—such as metal–dielectric–metal nanopatch antennas—offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP–positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis
abstract: Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of meta ‐ and para ‐substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron‐donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron‐withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom‐to‐boron donation, and π‐acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron‐containing reagents and functional molecules.

title: MgO Facets as Regenerable Molecular Oxygen Reservoirs in Oxidative Coupling of Methane
abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface‐sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}‐faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface‐bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C 2+ formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well‐designed surface structures.

title: Quantifying the hierarchical topological decay of fluid knots
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
In this paper we analyze the hierarchical topological cascade of knotted and linked filaments associated with the natural decay of superfluid vortex tangles. This is done by using an algebraic reformulation of knot polynomial invariants to quantify the topological states of the cascade process. By interpreting the evolutionary paths associated with vortex knot dynamics as geodesic flows in an appropriate knot polynomial space defined by adapted Jones polynomials [X. Liu, R. L. Ricca,
                    J. Phys. A Math. Theor.
                    45
                    , 205501 (2012).], we introduce an entanglement index to quantify the probability density of occurrence of each topological state. By this method we analyze all prime knots, links, and composites up to 8 crossings, and show that this measure detects accurately the decreasing topological complexity observed in simulations and laboratory experiments. By a comparative analysis carried out with data based on an alternative measure (complexity degree), we show that this entanglement index proves to be a more robust and reliable quantifier. The theoretical framework proposed here can be applied to other types of physical systems, where networks of filamentary structures are subject to continuous topological change and reorganization.

title: Synergy between Gq and Gi proteins for the antipsychotic-like effects of mGlu2 receptors
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The capacity of one G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) to modulate signaling outputs of another is a phenomenon with potential implications for neuron function and therapeutic action. Notably, Gi/o-coupled receptors have been shown to generate calcium signals after costimulation of Gq-coupled receptors, an effect resulting from a crosstalk between signaling cascades. But the relevance for brain function and for therapeutic applications remains largely unclear. Here we show that Gi/o-coupled metabotropic glutamate 2 (mGlu2) receptors can generate calcium signals in neurons. It results from either agonist activation or constitutive activity of a Gq-coupled receptor endogenously coexpressed with mGlu2, independently of dimerization. Specifically, the constitutively active platelet-activating factor receptor (PAFR) plays an essential role in mGlu2-calcium signaling in hippocampal neurons, an effect largely inhibited by PAFR inverse agonists and genetic variants. This mGlu2-PAFR crosstalk is required for the cognitive and behavioral rescue produced by mGlu2 agonists in a mouse model of NMDA receptor hypofunction. These data highlight the complexity of GPCR signaling and provide key insights on therapeutic strategies for psychiatric disorders.

title: The p38α MAPK–MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nuclear F-actin facilitates DNA damage repair and contributes to cancer chemoresistance. However, the regulatory mechanisms controlling its dynamic polymerization in response to genotoxic stress remain poorly defined. A major barrier in nuclear actin research is the lack of tools for precise, high-throughput analysis. To systematically investigate nuclear F-actin assembly in DNA damage response, we developed a deep learning pipeline, named nFANet, for high-throughput detection and analysis of nuclear F-actin. Here, using ovarian cancer—a malignancy where chemoresistance is a major clinical obstacle—as a model, we showed that platinum-based chemotherapy robustly induces nuclear F-actin assembly. A subsequent kinome screening, in combination with the application of nFANet, identified the kinase p38α MAPK as a critical upstream regulator of platinum-induced nuclear F-actin assembly. Mechanistically, the p38α MAPK–MK2 signaling pathway promotes formin-mediated nuclear F-actin assembly in response to chemotherapy. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockout of the p38α MAPK–MK2 pathway sensitized ovarian cancer cells to platinum-based therapy. Our work uncovers a key mechanism governing nuclear actin remodeling under genotoxic stress and lays the foundation for identifying a patient subgroup likely to benefit from therapeutic targeting of this pathway.

The quantum agreement theorem
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Intersubjective consistency asks when different observers of a physical system, reasoning from a shared theory, will agree on their probability assessments. Classical probability theory provides a benchmark in the form of the Agreement Theorem [R. J. Aumann,
                    Ann. Stat.
                    4
                    , 1236–1239 (1976)]. We study the quantum mechanics (QM) analog to the classical Agreement Theorem in a finite-dimensional tripartite setting in which two observers obtain information via local projective measurements. We represent their mutual awareness by common certainty, which is formally an infinite hierarchy of certainty operators concerning the probability of an event of interest. We first prove that if the observers’ measurements commute with one another and with the property of interest, common certainty forces their probability assessments to coincide, thereby recovering a QM analog to the classical Agreement Theorem. We then construct a one-parameter family of qutrit–qubit–qubit models in which one observer’s measurement does not commute with the property and common certainty of disagreement occurs—a distinctively QM phenomenon. The mechanism is coherence between branches distinguished by one but not the other observer’s measurement. When measurement outcomes are stored in a classical register, the resulting dephasing removes this coherence and restores agreement. Finally, we prove that QM does not permit the extreme

                    configuration in which Alice is certain of a property and is also certain that Bob is certain of its negation. These results aim to turn debate in QM about observer-dependent facts into precise mathematical conditions for when intersubjective agreement or disagreement in QM can be sustained.

title: Sex differences in the genetic basis of human recombination within 190,000 parent-child pairs
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Meiotic recombination drives genetic diversity and chromosome segregation, yet the genetic factors governing variation in human recombination rates across studies remain poorly understood. Here, we analyze 112,144 maternal and 78,653 paternal meiosis events across four countries and identify 58 independent genomic regions (24 unique across phenotypes) associated with recombination frequency and location. These include six novel female-specific regions harboring genes linked to ovarian function and a seventh novel region linked to male recombination, with many loci demonstrating sex-dependent effects. The between-sex genetic correlation is 0.374 (0.072 SD). While DNA markers account for 30-40% of individual-level variation in recombination rate, previously known global modulators explain only 37.7% (2.7% SD) of this variation in females and 47.1% (3.8% SD) in males. We create a polygenic predictor that significantly predicts recombination rates in women and men after adjusting for age and birth year. Furthermore, female recombination correlates significantly with reproductive outcomes and aging, after adjusting for study ascertainment. In the largest meta-analysis to date of human meiotic recombination, these findings uncover novel sex-specific loci and clarify the polygenic architecture underlying meiotic variation.

title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Notable differences between histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch have been extensively researched at peripheral and spinal levels. However, the way in which the brain processes histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch remains unknown. We discovered that the posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (pPVT)→the nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcMed) circuit exhibits reverse response patterns to histamine-dependent or histamine-independent itch and serves as a central anti-pruritic role. Mechanistically, histamine-dependent itch activates excitatory inputs from the lateral hypothalamus (LH) to mobilise the anti-pruritic centre, thereby buffering its intensity. In cases of chronic itch, however, there is a decrease in the efficiency of the anti-pruritic circuit’s postsynaptic transmission, thereby promoting itch sensitisation. Our research reveals that histamine-dependent and histamine-independent itch are processed differently in the mouse brain, offering insights into the neural mechanisms underlying chronic itch sensitization.

title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Parasympathetic nervous system activity, vital for restorative sleep, is influenced by vagal sensory afferents, but how these shape brain-body correlates of sleep remains open. Here we combined vagal sensory neuron (VSN) stimulation in the mouse with EEG/EMG, heart rate, brain-body temperature, noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC) neuron population activity measures and in vitro synaptic physiology to investigate the effects of VSN activation on sleep-wake states. We show that chemogenetic VSN stimulation during the resting phase induced a non-rapid-eye-movement sleep (NREMS)-like state with enriched, but homeostatically regulated, low-frequency (0.75–4 Hz) EEG activity, yet suppressed REMS. Simultaneously, brain-body temperatures dropped while LC activity increased. The gradual recovery towards normal NREMS-REMS-cycles was accelerated by external warming, identifying cooling as key contributing factor. We conclude that VSN activation can promote brain-body correlates as a continuum of normal NREMS while engaging wake-promoting forebrain neuromodulation, revealing a coexistence of classically incompatible sleep- and wake-associated signatures.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based emergency load shedding for power system frequency security with knowledge-guided decision refinement and experience augmentation
Humanized yeast ORC drives R-loop dependent transcription-replication conflicts and global gene dysregulation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The Origin Recognition Complex (ORC) recruits Mini-Chromosome Maintenance (MCM) hexamers to initiate eukaryotic DNA replication. While yeast ORC binds specific DNA motifs, human ORC binds sequence-agnostically nucleosome-depleted promoter regions. Here, using a mutant yeast model that recapitulates the human ORC binding landscape, we demonstrate that pervasive and unscheduled ORC binding at promoters in the compact yeast genome generates R-loop associated transcription-replication conflicts and disrupts gene expression across thousands of genes. Unexpectedly, we also uncover that substituting endogenous gene promoters with a replication origin sequence maintains robust transcription. We reveal that this intrinsic, promoter-like function relies on the ability of origins to form a nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) encoded within the origin’s sequence composition. However, origin-substituted loci reposition the +1 nucleosome which drives the transcription machinery to select alternative transcription start sites (TSSs). Thus, origins and promoters share an intrinsic chromatin structure-controlled ability to drive transcription initiation. Together, our results show that origin licensing in compact genomes relies on sequence-specific, coupled origin licensing to insulate transcription from the replication machinery.

title: Intrinsic neural dynamics reveal a body-part-specific topography in mouse secondary motor cortex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mammalian sensory cortex (S1) has a well-characterized body part-specific topography. However, most motor cortex atlases to date are only coarsely defined. Here, we demonstrate that optical mapping of neuronal activity in awake mice reveals a distinct, body-part specific organization of mouse secondary motor cortex (M2). This M2 topography was identified by recognizing that intrinsic neuronal fluctuations are selectively synchronized between homologous sub-regions of S1 and M2. These fluctuations were strongest during rest and quenched during movement, and were not prominent in corticospinal neurons (CSNs), indicating that they do not represent motor output. Functional characterization of M2 sub-regions during spontaneous movements confirms body-part specificity, and stronger engagement during multi-effector coordinated actions. Structural connectivity atlas tracings from S1 regions confirm projections to homologous M2 sub-regions. These results reveal an important underlying topography within M2, and demonstrate intrinsic neuronal dynamics as a window into the functional architecture of the motor cortex.

title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30–60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immunocompromised individuals remain at risk of severe COVID-19. This multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent (Ancestral/BA.1) mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. A total of 139 immunocompromised adults received AZD7442 followed 28 days later by vaccination. AZD7442 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Serum AZD7442 concentrations peaked at day 28 and remained detectable across disease cohorts at day 180. Anti-Spike antibody responses increased after AZD7442 and reached their highest levels after vaccination. Although binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting S2, the S1 N-terminal domain and receptor-binding domain epitopes not bound by AZD7442, and increased S2-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses were cross-reactive between ancestral and Omicron variants. Our findings support consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development. The trial is registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry (ISRCTN53507177).

title: Multi-dimensional nonisothermal modeling of polymer electrolyte membrane electrolysis cells
Epithelium stratifies via nucleation and growth induced by foam-geometric instability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Epithelial stratification, the transition from a monolayer to a multilayer structure, occurs across a wide range of phenomena. Recent studies have identified several cell behaviors as triggers, including junctional tension, cell density and geometry, and topological defects. However, how these factors drive stratification throughout the entire epithelium remains poorly understood. Here, we show that epithelial stratification proceeds through a nucleation-and-growth mechanism. Combining cell culture with three-dimensional vertex modeling, we demonstrate that multilayer origins emerge in a dispersed manner and expand across the epithelium through disordered intermediate states. This transition is induced by a mechanical instability inherent in the foam-like geometry of the epithelium. Moreover, the nucleation-growth concept applies to embryonic skin development and intestinal cancer transformation. These findings conceptualize epithelial stratification as a form of structural transition governed by foam mechanics, offering a physical perspective on various epithelial developments.

title: Comparative genomics analysis of luminescent and non-luminescent fireflies reveals mechanisms underlying adult light organs development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The genetic and developmental basis for the gain and loss of complex traits remains a central question in evolutionary biology. We investigate the loss of the adult light organ (LO) in the diurnal non-luminous firefly Pristolycus diversecostatus as a natural case of lineage-specific gene loss. A high-quality genome assembly of Pri. diversecostatus, combined with comparative multi-omics and functional analyses with its luminous relative Aquatica leii, reveals that LO loss correlates with large-scale gene family contraction and transcriptional rewiring of three core metabolic modules. RNAi experiments in Aqu. leii show that Laccase2 is required for LO integrity and bioluminescence. Key regulators of LO-specific cuticle transparency are identified, and a homeobox centered gene regulatory network is uncovered. This multi-omics study provides a genome-wide perspective on the regulatory modules underlying a complex organ and offers a framework based on regulatory network simplification for understanding the formation and loss of complex traits in evolution.

title: Physics-guided multimodal ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting via predictive sky imaging
A hierarchical metabolic flux orchestrates cell cycle transitions in bacteria
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mechanisms interlinking metabolic cues with cell cycle programs remain unknown. We show that an oscillating cytosolic redox critically governs cell cycle transitions in Caulobacter crescentus. By integrating evolutionary genetics with metabolic flux tracing, we uncover temporally orchestrated shifts in core metabolic pathways that remodel cytosolic redox across the cell cycle. Early stages channel carbon flux toward unsaturated fatty-acid synthesis and a reverse-TCA to drive cytosolic oxidation-coupled G1-to-S transition. The later stages depend on an enhanced forward-TCA cycle that promote cytosolic reduction-driven proliferation. Strikingly, perturbing fatty-acid synthesis or reverse/forward-TCA cycle uncouples growth from proliferation. Intriguingly, a biphasic glucose uptake program dictates the cell cycle-stage-specific metabolism. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized metabolic-redox circuitry that coordinates cell cycle progression in bacteria. They further unveil several metabolic branchpoints as promising targets for chemical intervention to disrupt critical and conserved cell cycle events, with potential applicability to bacterial pathogens.

title: Enhancing photovoltaic hydrogen production by interfacial thermal–moisture nexus regulation
Hydrogen crossover of chemically degraded PEMFC membranes: Microstructural-driven transport and cross-scale mitigation insights
Regional infrastructure repurposing: Pathways from assessment to geothermal energy production and storage
abstract: Addressing the growing demand for sustainable energy, we explore the innovative potential of repurposing existing subsurface infrastructure for geothermal energy production and energy storage. We present an integrated technical, economic, and legal framework for repurposing regional-scale infrastructure to systematically evaluate and optimize geothermal resource utilization. The states of Berlin and Brandenburg in Germany serve as a model area, with field studies in Groß Schönebeck and Lusatia demonstrating practical infrastructure repurposing. Results show that 12 of the 17 evaluated wells are potentially suitable for repurposing, with hydrothermal energy (HE) emerging as the most promising option. Economic viability is achievable by targeting the Middle Buntsandstein formation at depths exceeding 2400 meters and temperatures above 86 ∘ C, utilizing well doublets with a minimum of 750-meter spacing. Reservoir simulations indicate that optimized development schemes can achieve gross thermal power ranging from 2.9 to 7.6 M W t h with a Levelized Cost of Heat (LCOH) ranging from € 0.035/kWh to € 0.08/kWh. This is achievable through exploration near existing wells and direct connection to district heating networks. While Borehole Heat Exchangers (BHEs) offer faster implementation, their economic viability is challenging due to low thermal power and proximity requirements. Recognizing a mismatch between existing subsurface data and heat demand areas, the Landesamt für Bergbau, Geologie und Rohstoffe (LBGR) has initiated a new 2D seismic exploration campaign in 2025 for the Lower Lusatia area, leveraging well-established district heating and hydrocarbon infrastructure. This research demonstrates an economic strategy for reusing infrastructure for heating and energy storage, supported by strategic government initiatives, and provides a replicable decision-making workflow to guide geothermal energy development.

title: Forecast-free real-time V2B control of battery swapping stations as distributed battery assets via imitation learning
The Iberian blackout: A black swan or a gray rhino? A protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment
abstract: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian power system collapsed after a rapid voltage rise that led to widespread generation disconnections and loss of synchronism. The final report of the ENTSO-E Expert Panel attributes the blackout to several interacting factors including ineffective voltage control, fixed power factor operation, misaligned protection settings, manual shunt reactor switching, and limited observability. These factors raise a general question: given the current state, can the next trip, ramp, topology action, or shunt switching raise the voltages measured by overvoltage relays above their settings before voltage controls respond? We answer this with a protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment. For each candidate event, the method computes the voltage at every overvoltage relay over the relay time window from a dynamic model of the network, its controls, and its relays. It predicts which relays trip after a first trip, identifies assets whose relay or measurement data are insufficient for a safety conclusion, and, when one exists, computes a minimum-cost fast reactive power action that keeps all relay voltages below their settings. Case studies on four benchmark systems and a 2000-bus system that reproduces the mechanism of the Iberian blackout show that the method flagged every event that caused a secondary trip within the relay window, never declared safe a plant that tripped within that window, and, on the benchmarks, found fast reactive power actions that prevented the trips within the relay window whenever it judged such actions feasible. These results were validated with nonlinear time-domain simulations. The implementation code and a visual guide of this work are publicly available.

title: Decoupling instantaneous and cumulative stress: Physics-guided capacity prediction for lithium-ion batteries under stochastic cycling
