Common-path evaluation of electric boiler and thermal storage dispatch in Finnish district heating under electricity-price uncertainty
abstract: The value of uncertainty-aware district-heating dispatch depends on when prices become known and how long heat remains in storage. This study develops a price-taking mixed-integer linear model for a Finnish system with biomass CHP, a 50 MW th electric boiler (EB), a natural-gas peak boiler, and thermal energy storage (TES). Daily 72 h problems implement the cleared first 24 h and propagate each policy's realised TES state. Deterministic, stochastic, and budgeted robust policies are compared on one 2023 hourly path and on 800 held-out price trajectories; their economic differences are assessed against TES value and parameter sensitivity. With 200 MWh th TES, annual costs are EUR 4.902, 4.920, and 4.939 million, respectively, compared with EUR 4.783 million for a rolling perfect-foresight benchmark. Stochastic dispatch has the lowest held-out mean cost and regret, while deterministic dispatch has slightly lower P 95 and CVaR 95 . TES saves EUR 1.974 million a − 1 relative to matched no-storage dispatch; the stochastic and robust annual premiums are only EUR 0.037 and 0.075/MWh th . Storage mainly shifts heat within one day. A 200-sample annual rolling sensitivity analysis identifies CHP power-to-heat ratio, EB capacity, fuel price, and TES duration as the dominant cost drivers. Biases of ±5% and ± 10% in look-ahead heat demand preserve the annual policy ranking. The EB dispatch-weighted carbon intensity is approximately 26 g CO2/kWhel, below the national consumption-weighted mean of 37.69 g CO2/kWhel.

title: Photovoltaic greenhouses in the European south: balancing energy generation and agricultural productivity - an economic analysis
abstract: This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of photovoltaic greenhouses in representative Mediterranean regions in Spain and Italy. A techno-economic model was developed to analyze the interaction between photovoltaic technology choice including present-day crystalline silicon PV (c-Si), current-state Organic Photovoltaics (OPV) modules with 63 W m −2 , and a projected future OPV scenario with 145 W m −2 , greenhouse electricity demand profiles, PV coverage levels, battery storage integration, remuneration schemes and crop yield responses to shading. Without taking crop yields into account, results show that greenhouse electricity demand and the resulting self-consumption potential are the dominant drivers of economic performance. Under high-demand conditions several configurations become profitable, reaching net present values (NPVs) of up to 51,640€ in Bari and 22,176€ in Almería. Under the optimistic OPV145 scenario, which combines a projected module output of 145 W m −2 with future upscaling-related cost reductions, NPVs reach values comparable to the present-day c-Si PV reference in selected high-demand configurations. Profitability declines under less favorable performance assumptions, with initial performance losses exerting a stronger economic effect than higher annual degradation rates. The current-state OPV63 scenario, based on commercially oriented module cost assumptions and 63 W m −2 output, remains economically constrained across most configurations, although NPVs at low PV coverage indicate that moderate improvements in efficiency or costs could enable feasibility. When crop yield impacts are incorporated, profitability becomes strongly crop-dependent. High-value crops such as strawberries are better able to offset PV investment costs, as the shading effect can enhance crop yields. Lower-value crops remain economically challenging. Sensitivity analysis indicates that, if the PV system alone does not achieve break-even, additional crop revenues of up to 4700€ year −1 in Bari and 6400€ year −1 in Almería are required to reach economic break-even. Conversely, economically viable configurations can withstand revenue losses of up to 3600€ year −1 and 1600€ year −1 , respectively. Overall, the results demonstrate that photovoltaic greenhouse systems can become economically viable under favorable demand conditions, suitable crop selection and future OPV cost and performance improvements.

title: Joint hierarchical SOH and SOC balancing control strategy in dynamically reconfigurable battery systems based on deep learning and deep reinforcement learning
Strategies for meeting future gas demand while mitigating stranded asset risks under decarbonization
CCR8-depleting antibodies restore response to radiotherapy plus anti-PD1 therapy in head and neck cancer by targeting intratumoral CCR8+ regulatory T cells
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite advances in immunotherapy (IO) and radiation therapy (RT), anti-PD-1 (aPD-1) therapy has provided only modest benefit in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) for reasons that remain poorly understood. CCR8 is a chemokine receptor selectively enriched on tumor infiltrating regulatory T cells (Tregs), making it an attractive candidate for therapeutic targeting. Given our knowledge that immunosuppressive T-regulatory cells are associated with resistance to RT and IO, but have no effective targeting strategy in HNSCC, we investigate the depletion of tumor specific Treg subsets on tumor growth in female mice. In human and murine HNSCC, we characterize a subset of CCR8+ Tregs that are an immunosuppressive cell population associated with incomplete response to RT and IO. In preclinical models of HNSCC, we find that RT drives CCR8+ Treg infiltration into the primary tumor to promote tumor growth and recurrence, which can be reversed with administration of CCR8-depleting antibodies (aCCR8). Finally, we show that resistance to RT+aPD1 combination therapy is mediated by aPD1 activation of CCR8+ Tregs to facilitate tumor growth, which can be reversed with aCCR8. These findings reveal the immunosuppressive profile of CCR8+ Tregs in HNSCC and pave the way for novel combination strategies of IO in HNSCC.

title: Failure of TSPO-dependent metabolic compensation marks the loss of mitochondrial bioenergetic adaptation in parkin-deficient neurons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neurons require mitochondrial bioenergetic flexibility to withstand chronic mitochondrial quality control failure, yet the compensatory safeguards that preserve mitochondrial functional output during neurodegenerative progression remain unclear. Here, using parkin-deficient fly models, we identify an early mitochondrial metabolic signature characterized by reduced pyruvate and increased glutamate and α-ketoglutarate. Substrate-specific mitochondrial respiration and ATP assays showed impaired pyruvate-supported bioenergetic capacity but preserved glutamate-supported bioenergetic capacity, supporting a transient glutamate-linked compensatory state before neurodegenerative deterioration. We identify neuronal TSPO upregulation as an adaptive compensatory mechanism that sustains glutamate-supported mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity under parkin-deficient conditions. In human iPSC-derived neurons, parkin deficiency was similarly associated with TSPO upregulation, and TSPO modulation altered neuronal vulnerability. TSPO induction was controlled by JNK-Jun/Nrf2 signaling, whose age-associated attenuation compromised compensation and accelerated neurodegeneration. Thus, loss of TSPO-dependent glutamate-linked bioenergetic compensation marks the transition from mitochondrial adaptation to neurodegenerative deterioration under parkin-deficient conditions.

title: LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish luteal cell identity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite advances in assisted reproductive technology, success rates remain modest, largely due to implantation failure and inadequate support of early pregnancy. Corpus luteum function and consequent progesterone secretion are essential for these processes. Large luteal cells are the primary source of progesterone production, yet the transcriptional programs that define their identity remain unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Liver receptor homolog-1 as a key regulator of large luteal cell function. Loss of Liver receptor homolog-1 disrupts lipid droplet accumulation and downregulates key steroidogenic genes. Mechanistically, Liver receptor homolog-1 undergoes chromatin-binding reprogramming during luteinization, establishing regulatory regions that couple lipid metabolism to steroidogenesis. Large luteal cells integrate energy metabolism with steroid hormone production and promote nuclear acetyl-coenzyme A synthesis via Acyl-CoA synthetase short-chain family member 2, linking metabolic reprogramming to epigenetic control. These findings establish Liver receptor homolog-1 and Acyl-CoA synthetase short-chain family member 2 as key regulators coordinating lipid homeostasis, chromatin regulation and fertility.

title: miProbe: microbial peptide repository of biological embeddings
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microbial peptides represent a vast yet largely underexplored component of microbial dark matter, offering a valuable reservoir of bioactive molecules. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized peptide mining, demonstrating high-throughput screening capabilities in tasks such as functional prediction and de novo design. To fully unlock the potential of microbial resource, we present miProbe (https://www.biosino.org/iMAC/miProbe), an integrative platform hosting 1.08 × 109 microbial peptides from disparate habitats. Uniquely, miProbe bridges the gap between raw sequences and AI applications by providing 8 TB of precomputed protein language model embeddings (e.g., ESM2-650M and ProtT5-XL-U50). Our analysis reveals substantial variation in peptide diversity and functional properties across habitats and microbial taxonomic groups, and highlights the utility of large-scale embedding resources in functional peptide mining. Equipped with robust APIs for seamless model integration, miProbe establishes a diverse and scalable data resource to accelerate AI-driven exploration of microbial dark matter and the rational design of novel therapeutics.

title: High-precision mapping of non-uniform SOC distribution inside lithium-ion batteries via multi-dimensional ultrasound features and physics-guided deep learning
Directional motility of crystallizing cholesterol on supported lipid bilayers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cholesterol crystallization within phospholipid bilayers necessarily remodels the surrounding membrane, creating dynamic feedback between growing crystallites and locally changing membrane. Using fluorescence microscopy, we show that lipid-coated, cholesterol-rich crystallites self-propel on the bilayer surface along directional trajectories, including circular, unidirectional, and reciprocating motion. We hypothesize that crystallite motilities arise from local cholesterol depletion in the underlying bilayer, generating gradients in composition, rigidity, and thus adhesion, which induce directional forces analogous to those involved in haptotaxis and/or durotaxis. Fluorescence lifetime imaging with a mechanosensitive probe reveals time-resolved changes in membrane packing, consistent with this mechanism. Single particle tracking and mathematical modeling support the mechanical plausibility of a working model in which crystallization-induced cholesterol redistribution may generate dynamic rigidity gradients at crystallite–membrane interface. Tuning membrane states yields a quantitative operating map that relates composition to motility, providing model-dependent design guidance for controlling cholesterol crystallite transport on lipid interfaces.

title: A Bioinspired Phytyl Tripod Anchor for Engineering Liposomal and Cellular Surfaces as a Robust Colloidal Delivery Platform
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the phytyl chains of chlorophylls and tocopherols, we developed a robust phytyl tripod anchor for cell surface engineering in this work. The anchor exhibited markedly stronger membrane anchoring than the widely used 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine (DSPE) anchor, as reflected by a lower critical micellization concentration (0.119 vs 0.189 mM) and a more negative Gibbs free energy of liposome binding (–29.85 vs –28.15 kJ/mol). Using this anchor, we established a liposome-relayed bioorthogonal manipulation platform that enables site-specific cell surface engineering in vivo. In a zebrafish inflammation model, liposomes decorated with amphiphilic hyaluronic acid (HA) first delivered the phytyl tripod anchor selectively to inflamed tissue, and subsequently injected clickable catalase and liposomal curcumin were then captured in situ via bioorthogonal click chemistry, anchoring them onto the target cell surface. This two-step strategy produced substantially enhanced therapeutic effects. We further extended the platform into a photothermal enhanced liposome delivery system. Clickable magnetic nanoparticles, synthesized via a PEGylated gallic acid approach, were bioorthogonally conjugated to cell membranes and liposomes through the phytyl tripod anchor. Curcumin was additionally derivatized with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting KKAA peptide to enable organelle-specific delivery. In an inflammation model with RAW264.7 cells, this photothermal-enhanced system significantly improved the anti-inflammatory efficacy. The developed phytyl tripod anchor and the derived bioorthogonal strategies hold great promise for precision cell surface engineering and targeted delivery of bioactives.

title: Interface Engineering of Magnetic Ni x Co3– x O4 Cathodes by Field Polarity for Li-O2 Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium-oxygen (Li-O2) batteries offer ultrahigh theoretical energy density, but sluggish cathodic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR)/oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics restrict practical application. Here, magnetically tunable NixCo3–xO4 (NCOx) spinel cathode catalysts were prepared by regulating the Ni:Co ratio to clarify the relationship among catalyst magnetization, magnetic-field polarity, and Li-O2 battery performance. Increasing Ni content raises the fraction of high-spin octahedral Ni2+, enhancing saturation magnetization; NCO3 (Ni:Co = 2:1) exhibits the highest Ms (28 emu/g) and strongest response under 300 mT. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a polarity-dependent effect: an N-pole field decreases Rct from 27.42 to 19.74 Ω, whereas an S-pole field increases Rct, likely because it aggravates the spin mismatch between catalyst electrons and triplet-state O2, thereby increasing the interfacial charge-transfer barrier. Density functional theory (DFT) descriptor calculations show that the high-spin (HS)-initialized reference configuration strengthens O2 adsorption (–2.95 eV) and exhibits more favorable calculated ORR/OER energetics than the low-spin (LS)-initialized reference configuration; these calculations do not explicitly simulate the external magnetic field. Under optimal NCO3/N-pole/300 mT conditions, the discharge voltage increases by 107 mV and cycling life exceeds 990 h at 0.2 mA cm–2. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations show that the N-pole-facing magnetic-field condition changes the discharge-product morphology from irregular agglomerates to more uniformly distributed platelet-like structures. Ex situ Li 1s X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is consistent with more extensive removal of Li2O2 containing products during recharge, although it does not by itself prove complete Li2O2 decomposition or suppression of Li2CO3 formation. This work establishes a cooperative strategy combining catalyst magnetic design and magnetic field regulation, providing insights into the rational design of magnetic field-assisted Li-O2 batteries.

title: A Series of TTDO-Based Energetic Cocrystals: From Supramolecular Assembly and Structural Analysis to Energetic Performance and Combustion Modulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The inherent trade-off between high energy output and safety remains a critical bottleneck in the development of advanced propellants and high-energy-density materials. Here, we present a supramolecular assembly strategy using 2,4,6-triamino-1,3,5-triazine-1,3-dioxide (TTDO) as a Lewis base host to construct energetic cocrystals. Guided by COSMO screening, five nitro-containing Lewis acid energetic molecules were successfully cocrystallized with TTDO. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals diverse protonation behaviors and extensive hydrogen-bonding networks, while electrostatic potential analysis shows that the positions of electrostatic potential extrema shift upon cocrystallization, correlating with significantly reduced mechanical sensitivity. Notably, TTDO-LLM-116 and TTDO-NMTT serve as multifunctional additives in ammonium perchlorate (AP)-based composite propellants. Incorporating only 10 wt % of these cocrystals merges the two-stage decomposition of AP into a single exothermic event and reduces the decomposition activation energy from 250.2 kJ·mol–1 to 107.4 kJ·mol–1 and 63.3 kJ·mol–1. Laser ignition experiments confirm enhanced combustion with a substantially shorter duration. As combustion additives, these cocrystals reduce the activation energy of AP while avoiding the energy-dilution effect commonly encountered with inert metal oxide catalysts. This work establishes TTDO-based cocrystals as a versatile platform for developing low-sensitivity, high-performance energetic materials, and advanced combustion modifiers for propellant applications.

title: Acquisition of Ultra-low Friction by a 2D Heterogeneous Interface at a High Temperature
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving robust lubrication across extreme temperature ranges remains a fundamental challenge in tribology. Here, we report a MoS2/Ti/Ag nano-doped film, fabricated via scalable magnetron sputtering, that exhibits self-adaptive ultra-low friction from ambient conditions to 450 °C. We distinguish the governing mechanisms at homogeneous (self-mated) and heterogeneous (paired with hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C:H)) interfaces, respectively. While room-temperature superlubricity in self-mated pairs arises from the shear-induced alignment of long-range ordered planes but degrades under thermal stress, the heterogeneous interface maintains an ultra-low friction coefficient of 0.02–0.04 throughout the entire temperature spectrum. At elevated temperatures, we reveal a possible dynamic reconstruction process: graphitization of the a-C:H transfer film driven by localized sp2-C clustering synergizes with Ag migration to restructure the contact area. This friction-activated mechanism may entrap carbon fragments and liberate MoS2, prompting its spontaneous re-alignment into an ordered, low-friction configuration. These findings uncover a thermally resilient, self-adaptive lubrication strategy with broad implications for aerospace and industrial applications.

title: GSH/pH Dual-Responsive Zwitterionic mRNA Nanocomplexes for Tumor-Enriched mRNA Delivery in a B16F10 Melanoma Model
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapy offers a programmable route to melanoma treatment, but its translation is limited by nuclease degradation, off-target biodistribution and endolysosomal trapping. Here we report a glutathione (GSH)/pH dual-responsive mRNA nanocomplex (mRNA-NC) fabricated by one-pot in situ polymerization of N-(3-aminopropyl)methacrylamide (APMA), 1-vinylimidazole (VI), N,N′-bis(acryloyl)cystamine (BACA), and 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) on the mRNA template. At an N/P ratio of 40, the carrier reached an encapsulation efficiency of 92.7 ± 2.1% and a loading capacity of 87.4 ± 3.2 μg mg–1, forming monodisperse particles of 126.4 ± 7.2 nm (polydispersity index, PDI, 0.14). The zwitterionic corona limited plasma protein adsorption to 12.6 ± 1.5 μg mg–1 (4.6-fold lower than jetPEI/mRNA), kept hemolysis at 0.8 ± 0.2%, and extended the serum half-life of the mRNA to ≈27.4 h, roughly 9-fold longer than naked mRNA. Release was gated by both triggers: 86.5 ± 3.7% of the cargo was released within 8 h under 10 mM GSH, whereas leakage under physiological conditions remained ≤ 12%; in a 4 h matrix, pH 5.5 plus 10 mM GSH released 85 ± 6.8% versus 12 ± 1.5% at pH 7.4 without GSH. In B16F10 cells, the nanocomplex was taken up in a dose- and energy-dependent manner, entered the lysosomal compartment, and escaped over time in a manner consistent with imidazole-mediated proton-sponge buffering (a hypothesis; intralysosomal pH was not measured directly), producing a peak firefly luciferase (FLuc) expression of 56,140 ± 3280 RLU mg–1 protein at 24 h, about 1.5-fold higher than jetPEI/mRNA, with 93.6 ± 3.9% cell viability and 6.7 ± 1.2% lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release. In B16F10-bearing albino C57BL/6 mice, a single intravenous dose produced tumor-dominant bioluminescence (peak 5.7 × 106 photons s–1 at 6 h), a tumor enrichment index of 1.22 ± 0.18 (vs 0.31 ± 0.03 for jetPEI/mRNA) and 2.42 × 107 FLuc mRNA copies μg–1 tumor RNA at 12 h, while all 7-day safety indicators remained at phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) levels. These results demonstrate that a single zwitterionic nanocomplex can integrate stealth, dual-triggered release, and endosomal escape for safe, tumor-enriched mRNA delivery. While this study focuses on delivery performance and reporter gene expression, it lays a solid foundation for future therapeutic applications with functional mRNA.

title: Loading-Dependent Osteogenic Performance of Core–Shell Nanocomposite-Reinforced Poly(ε-caprolactone) Scaffolds for Bone Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bone defect repair remains challenging due to the complex biological processes involving inflammation, angiogenesis, and osteogenesis. Although therapeutic ions and natural antioxidants have been individually investigated for bone regeneration, the biological performance of scaffolds incorporating multiple functional components at different loading contents remains to be fully explored. In this study, we designed a core–shell nanocomposite (GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8) consisting of Ga/Te-codoped mesoporous bioactive glass (GaTe-MBG) as the core and curcumin-loaded ZIF-8 as the shell. The nanocomposite was incorporated into poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) at different contents (0, 5, 10, and 15 wt %) to fabricate three-dimensional (3D)-printed composite scaffolds. The designed scaffolds were intended to provide a multifunctional platform integrating curcumin with Ga, Te, Zn, Si, and Ca ions. Among the investigated formulations, the scaffold containing 10% GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8 (by weight) exhibited the most favorable overall biological performance, including antioxidant activity, favorable inflammation-associated responses, enhanced osteogenic differentiation, and angiogenesis-related effects. In a rat cranial defect model, the 10% scaffold demonstrated improved bone regeneration compared to the other groups. RNA sequencing analysis revealed differential gene expression and enrichment of inflammation- and osteogenesis-related pathways, including IL-17, TNF, and MAPK signaling, suggesting potential associations between the scaffold-induced cellular responses and these signaling pathways. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of the combined GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8 nanocomposite for bone tissue engineering and identify 10% as a favorable loading content within the investigated range, providing insights into the design of multifunctional composite scaffolds for bone regeneration.

title: Nickel Nanoparticle-Modified Carbon Nanotube Films for Energy-Efficient Out-of-Oven Curing and Damage Self-Sensing of Basalt Fiber/Epoxy Composites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotube (CNT) films can serve as a Joule heating source for low-energy out-of-oven curing, but their electrothermal performance is limited by the CNT–CNT junction resistance. Metal nanoparticles can bridge adjacent CNTs and reduce the junction resistance, but at excessively high concentrations, particle agglomeration offsets this effect. In this study, a nickel (Ni) nanoparticle-modified CNT/thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) conductive film was prepared and used for Joule heating curing and damage self-sensing of basalt fiber-reinforced epoxy composites. Within the investigated range of Ni dispersion concentrations, the conductivity of the film increases first and then decreases. To interpret this behavior, a phenomenological competition model and a Monte Carlo resistor-network model were established, attributing this nonmonotonic change to the competition between metallic bridging and agglomeration loss. Based on the modeling and experimental results, 2 mg·mL–1 was identified as the Ni concentration with the best overall performance within the investigated range. The resulting film reached 80.96 °C at 9 V and maintained uniform and stable heating during 3600 s of continuous heating and 30 heating–cooling cycles. Subsequently, basalt fiber-reinforced polymer composites (BFRPs) were prepared using the conductive film via an out-of-oven curing process. The BFRPs exhibited mechanical properties similar to those of oven-cured samples while additionally acquiring electrothermal and damage self-sensing functions. This study provides a viable design strategy for the development of basalt fiber-reinforced composites with both electrothermal and damage self-sensing capabilities.

title: Multifunctional Shape-Memory Composite Films with Coupled Morphing–Transparency–Luminescence Modulation via Interfacial Engineering and Hybrid Nanoparticle Design
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Shape-memory polymers offer programmable deformation, yet their use in storing and regulating optically readable information remains limited. Inspired by the adaptive optical behavior of glass squid, we developed a multifunctional shape-memory composite film integrating programmable morphing, reversible transparency modulation, optical-state storage, and phosphorescent readout. The film combines refractive-index-matched phosphorescent carbon dots/silica nanoparticles (CDs/SiO2 NPs) with a poly(ethylene-co-vinyl acetate) (EVA) shape-memory matrix. Mechanical programming generates interfacial microcavities, decreasing the transmittance from 88.4 to 18.6% while fixing the programmed optical state without continuous external force. Thermal shape recovery promotes transparency restoration and reveals the concealed information. Meanwhile, the CDs/SiO2 NPs provide visible-light-excited afterglow observable for approximately 6 s for dark-state recognition. The integration of programmable morphing, transparency modulation, and phosphorescent readout enables dynamic anti-counterfeiting/encryption and adaptive visual signaling.

title: Magnetically Reconfigurable Liquid Metal Microdroplet Networks Enable High Thermal Conductivity and Self-healing in Dynamic Polymer Composites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The integration of high thermal conductivity and autonomous self-healing capability in thermal interface materials remains a critical challenge for next-generation electronic devices. Herein, we design a liquid metal (LM) magnetic droplet composite: TA-coated iron particles (Fe@TA) are compounded with Ga68.5In21.5Sn10, ultrasonicated into LM magnetic droplets, and dispersed in a dynamic polymer matrix. The TA shell architecture serves a dual function: it prevents deleterious alloying between iron and gallium-based LM, while the polyphenolic moieties of TA establish coordination interactions with Fe2+/Fe3+ and Ga3+/In3+ ions, synergistically ensuring interfacial structure and the stability. Under magnetic actuation, Fe@TA enables the directional migration and controlled deformation of LM droplets within the matrix, promoting droplet–droplet contact and the formation of efficient thermal pathways. Meanwhile, the magnetic field guides the droplets toward the damaged region, inducing matrix displacement to close the fracture gap and facilitating dynamic bond reformation, which substantially enhances the self-healing capability. Remarkably, the healed LMMC70 composite exhibits a 100% enhancement in thermal conductivity compared to its pristine sample, attributable to the synergistic magneto-thermal effect that drives droplet aggregation at damage sites, reinforces interfacial thermal contacts, and restores structural continuity through effective dynamic bond reorganization. In addition, the LMMC90 composite integrates high thermal conductivity (5.6 W·m–1·K–1), ultralow contact thermal resistance (0.1 K·cm2·W–1), excellent electrical insulation (1011 Ω·m), and effective self-healing capability. This work offers a viable strategy for designing intelligent thermal interface materials with magnetic-field-assisted thermal management and autonomous damage healing, holding great promise for reliable thermal management in advanced electronics.

title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks@Bacterial Cellulose Mixed-Matrix Membranes for Pollution Elimination
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) represent promising porous photocatalytic candidates for water remediation, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by their powdery nature, poor machinability, and limited recyclability. Herein, we report a facile in situ growth strategy to immobilize methyl-modified (HOF-101-CH3), fluorine-modified (HOF-101-F), and pristine HOF-101 nanocrystals within the three-dimensional interconnected nanofibrous network of bacterial cellulose (BC), yielding HOFs@BC mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). Robust interfacial hydrogen bonding and physical cross-linking are constructed between HOF crystallites and BC nanofibers, which effectively suppress HOF aggregation, improve mechanical tolerance, and grant the composite membrane favorable hydrophilicity for aqueous-phase operation. Benefiting from the electron-donating methyl substituent, HOF-101-CH3-m delivers a more negative surface zeta potential (–28.8 mV), elevated charge-carrier separation efficiency, and superior dye-selective performance. It achieved a high selectivity ratio of 49.5 (permeation flux: 174 L m–2 h–1 bar–1) toward mixed cationic methylene blue (MB) and anionic methyl orange (MO), with 99.1% MB removal and merely 2% MO adsorption. After five separation-regeneration cycles, the membrane retains a selectivity ratio above 41.5 and maintains approximately 84% of its initial selectivity performance. Under visible-light irradiation, abundant reactive oxygen species (1O2, ·OH, and H2O2) are generated by the embedded HOF-101-CH3, endowing the membrane with photocatalytic self-cleaning capability. Notably, HOF-101-CH3-m achieves complete photodegradation of bisphenol A (BPA) within 50 min and maintains 95.3% degradation efficiency over five cyclic photocatalytic runs. This work demonstrates a feasible structural-engineering route to transform intractable powdery HOFs into mechanically robust multifunctional membranes, offering insights into the future design of HOF-derived functional materials toward integrated selective dye separation and photocatalytic elimination of organic water pollutants.

title: Stable Magnesium Negative Electrodes Achieved via Dy Microalloying for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) are a promising alternative technology to lithium-ion batteries owing to the abundant resources, high theoretical volumetric energy density, and relatively high safety. Nevertheless, the nonuniform deposition/dissolution behavior, interfacial passivation, and exacerbated polarization under high current densities of magnesium metal negative electrodes severely impede their practical implementation. In this study, we propose a Dy microalloying strategy to regulate the microstructure and deposition/dissolution behavior of the magnesium negative electrode. The incorporation of low-concentration Dy (0.7 wt %) induces grain refinement and crystal texture evolution and alleviates galvanic corrosion due to the similar electrode potentials of Dy and Mg. This synergistic effect enhances the electrochemical reaction kinetics, structural integrity, and interfacial stability, thereby improving the uniformity of Mg deposition/dissolution. Therefore, the Mg–0.7Dy alloy negative electrode achieves a long cycle life exceeding 2500 h in symmetric cells at 1 mA cm–2 and 1 mA h cm–2. Moreover, the Mg–0.7Dy∥Mo6S8 full cell maintains a specific capacity of 59.67 mA h g–1 after 4000 cycles at 5 C, corresponding to a high capacity retention of 93.84%. This work demonstrates the feasibility of regulating the microstructure and deposition/dissolution behavior of the magnesium negative electrode through Dy microalloying engineering, offering a feasible strategy for developing high-performance negative electrodes for RMBs.

title: Hierarchical Composite Scaffold That Synergistically Combines Orderly Active Factor Release with Scaffold Degradation for Enhanced Bone Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Effective bone regeneration requires biodegradable scaffolds to provide temporary mechanical support while progressively creating space and delivering bioactive cues in step with tissue healing. However, achieving synergy between orderly active particle release and scaffold degradation remains a major challenge. This study aimed to develop a hierarchical scaffold for sustained bioactive-ion delivery and bone-defect repair. The scaffold consisted of a 3D-printed poly(p-dioxanone) (PPDO) framework and a freeze-dried gelatin network. Magnesium oxide-coated chitosan microspheres (MgO@CS) were incorporated into gelatin to support early cell recruitment and angiogenesis, whereas citrate-functionalized amorphous calcium phosphate (Cit-ACP) was embedded in PPDO to provide sustained osteogenic stimulation. During in vitro degradation, gelatin was largely removed within 5 weeks, progressively opening space for tissue infiltration. PPDO fibers showed morphological erosion at weeks 7–8 but persisted as the principal structural framework. The scaffold continuously released Mg2+, Ca2+, and citrate during the 14-day observation period. Cell experiments demonstrated enhanced cellular recruitment, vascularization, and osteogenic differentiation. In a rat calvarial defect model, the scaffold enhanced bone formation and improved BV/TV. These results demonstrate that coupling stage-matched scaffold degradation with compartmentalized bioactive-ion delivery provides a promising strategy for coordinating vascularized bone regeneration.

title: Oscillatory Chemical Networks in Silicon Nanofluidic Chips for Ultra-low-power Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chemical reactions offer unique opportunities for energy-efficient and adaptive computing. We integrate fluidic networks filled with the oscillatory Belousov–Zhabotinsky (BZ) reaction in silicon microchips to investigate the potential of these networks for on-chip chemical computation. Using nanofluidic confinement and networks of thousands of microreactors (5–30 μm) connected by nanochannels, we demonstrate stable oscillations under 300 nm vertical confinement and estimate an intrinsic chemical energy expenditure of ≈17 fJ per cycle at nanoscale reaction volumes. Reaction–diffusion waves propagate signals with diffusion lengths of ≈40 μm and speeds up to 123 μm s–1, while light-sensitive modulation provides dynamic control over the reaction dynamics, offering a route toward programmable architectures. These features support large fan-out, weighted connections, and reconfigurable pathways, laying the foundation for chemical logic, neuromorphic networks, and adaptive systems. Our results position oscillatory chemistry as a promising route toward ultra-low-power computing and bio-inspired architectures.

title: Photonic-assisted ingenious agile non-periodic oscillator (PIANO)
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The development of high-performance frequency-agile microwave signal generators has long been constrained by the inherent limitations of electronic technology. To overcome this challenge, researchers have increasingly turned to photonics, leveraging its high-frequency and broad-bandwidth capabilities. Here, we introduce and demonstrate a Photonic-assisted Ingenious Agile Non-periodic Oscillator (PIANO), which enables high-performance frequency-agile microwave signal generation with flexible frequency agility, ultra-low phase noise, rapid switching speed, and large time-bandwidth product (TBWP). The key innovation of PIANO lies in incorporating a dynamic frequency-shifting module into an optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) cavity, thereby extending the conventional delay-based OEO framework by decoupling frequency-agility behavior from the cavity-delay constraint. During experiments, PIANO successfully generated various flexible frequency-agile waveforms, with a frequency-switching time of 27 ns, phase noise as low as −134 dBc/Hz@10 kHz, and TBWP up to 1,440,000. This work offers a promising approach to high-performance frequency-agile microwave signal generation for applications such as radar and communication systems.

title: Anion manipulation for breaking through 3.0 V of aluminium–graphite batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aluminium-graphite batteries offer low cost and intrinsic high safety. However, the voltage window mostly remains limited because conventional chloroaluminate ionic-liquid electrolytes with Lewis-acidic Al2Cl7−([AlCl3–AlCl4]−) anions are intrinsically moisture-sensitive and unstable beyond 2.5 V. To extend the voltage window, a polytetrafluoroethylene/AlF3 framework‑confined, fluorine-rich chloroaluminate ionic-liquid composite quasi-solid-state electrolyte cosolvated with 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl ether is designed for constructing stable aluminium-graphite batteries with a cut-off voltage of 3.0 V. With the presence of AlF3, the Al2Cl7− is regulated through AlF3-associated chloroaluminate interactions, which reduces its activity and suppresses its electrochemical decomposition in the range of 2.5–3.0 V. Meanwhile, the fluorinated ether coordinates with the AlCl3 units in Al2Cl7− and promotes the formation of a fluorine-rich artificial interface on the graphite, essentially improving the electrochemical stability via alleviating electrochemical decomposition of AlCl4− up to 3.0 V. Furthermore, ion transport channels could be well maintained during large mechanical deformation induced by anion-intercalation/deintercalation of graphite interlayer. Therefore, the Al|electrolyte|graphite cells deliver discharge capacity beyond 137 mAh g−1 up to 3.0 V (specific current: 5.0 A g−1) (compared to 64 mAh g−1, charged up to 2.5 V at 5.0 A g−1) along with stable cycles beyond 35,000, demonstrating long-term high-voltage operation in rechargeable aluminium–graphite batteries.

title: Non-equilibrium resonance scattering in intramolecular charge transport drives conformational changes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Intramolecular charge transport is conventionally described as proceeding along a static ground-state potential, with the carrier acting as a passive probe of a fixed electronic landscape. Here, using alkanethiolate-based molecular junctions, we show that the carrier itself can drive conformational reorganization once the applied bias brings backbone-delocalized molecular orbitals into the transmission window. Combined electrical and in situ structural measurements resolve a threshold-activated transition to a gauche-defect state coincident with the onset of orbital-mediated transport. We rationalize this coupling through a quantum resonance scattering framework in which accessible orbitals act as scattering potentials that transiently host the injected charge, depositing energy into nuclear motion with an efficiency set by molecule–electrode coupling and Franck–Condon overlap. The framework quantitatively reproduces the measured response and predicts the enhanced behavior of amide-containing junctions. Together, these results suggest that charge-transport–structure feedback can be understood in terms of microscopic parameters governing resonance-mediated energy transfer, and that these parameters may be tuned through chemical design.

title: Percolation and site energy distribution jointly control Li+ transport in disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Disordered rocksalt positive electrodes are promising candidates for high-energy batteries, yet their ion transport kinetics is constrained by an incomplete understanding of Li transport in disordered environments. Conventional percolation theory focuses on topological connectivity but often overlooks the critical role of the energy landscape. Here, leveraging actively fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potentials combined with experimental validation, we quantitatively resolve the interplay between Li percolation connectivity and the Li-site energy distribution. We reveal a trade-off whereby increasing cation disorder enhances topological connectivity but concurrently broadens the site energy distribution, inducing a rugged energy landscape that suppresses overall diffusion. To reconcile these conflicting factors, we construct a design map spanning the full Li–Mn–Ti–O composition space, establishing a Li-site energy rectified percolation metric that transforms their interaction into a quantifiable descriptor. This framework enables the identification of Li1.3Mn0.4Ti0.3O2, which delivers a specific capacity of 294 mAh g−1. Furthermore, we demonstrate that inducing a phase transition toward a partially disordered spinel-like state simultaneously enhances percolation connectivity and narrows the energy landscape, achieving a specific capacity of 316 mAh g−1. This work provides insights into the ion transport mechanisms in disordered electrode materials and offers practical design principles for battery systems.

title: Deep learning models for ADITYA-U MHD equilibrium
abstract: This work presents an integrated deep learning framework for rapid magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equilibrium estimation in the ADITYA-U tokamak. A free-boundary equilibrium database containing 100,760 cases was generated using the pyIPREQ Grad–Shafranov solver from experimentally derived operating conditions spanning 766 ADITYA-U plasma discharges, with constraints representative of circular limiter plasmas near the flat-top phase. The database was used to develop a cascaded framework for predicting scalar equilibrium quantities, 1d safety factor profiles, and 2d poloidal flux profiles. Dense neural networks, principal component analysis (PCA), convolutional neural networks (CNN) and physics-informed neural networks (PINN) were investigated within this framework. The error propagation, cross-models consistency and ablation study of Grad–Shafranov residual were performed for the proposed framework. Across the test dataset, the models achieve median mean absolute errors of for the safety factor profile and for the normalized poloidal flux profile. The largest model requires approximately 1ms per equilibrium inference on a multi-core CPU. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework as a fast surrogate for equilibrium analysis, experiment planning and real-time plasma control applications for ADITYA-U experiments.

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components
abstract: Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.

title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low-recycling scrape-off layer: a one dimensional gyrokinetic study
abstract: A liquid lithium boundary offers a possible route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless such that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length ( ) estimates presented here, can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but more complete models are needed. We present a gyrokinetic simulations, with one configuration-space dimension and two velocity-space dimensions, of low and higher-recycling LTX- SOL conditions using Gkeyll, an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line from the low-field-side midplane to the high-field-side limiter. Gkeyll is used to evolve kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, the electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses with experimentally constrained density and temperature at the low field side mid-plane. The low-recycling case develops a hotter SOL, a larger electrostatic potential variation along the field line, and a density response that is not recovered with an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure of the field equations. This indicates that kinetic-electron dynamics and the associated ambipolar potential are important for maintaining quasi-neutrality and reducing electron end loss from the field line in the low-recycling regime. Collisionality scans show that, as the ion neoclassical collisionality is reduced below unity, the ion distribution develops a stronger non-Maxwellian structure. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, especially for the low-recycling case, because ions become mirror trapped, and electron transport is suppressed by the ambipolar electrostatic potential to maintain quasi-neutrality. These results suggest that low-recycling lithium-wall operation in LTX- accesses a SOL regime in which mirror trapping and electrostatic modification of electron transport alter the field-line residence time relative to conventional high-recycling fluid expectations. These SOL modifications are expected to become more pronounced in larger devices.

title: Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance
Electronic Modulation Engineering of Pt-Modified TiO2 Nanotube-Confined Co Catalyst for Efficient Low-Temperature Catalytic Oxidation of CH3SH
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Methanethiol (CH3SH) is a typical malodorous volatile organic pollutant, and its efficient low-temperature catalytic degradation remains both an urgent priority and a formidable challenge in odor abatement. Herein, we leveraged the unique curved surface architecture of titanium dioxide nanotubes ((TiO2 NTs) and developed a targeted electronic-modulation strategy in which cobalt (Co) species were confined within the nanotube channels via vacuum impregnation, followed by the photodeposition of platinum (Pt) onto the outer surface as an electron-withdrawing layer to yield a composite catalyst (Co@TiO2 NTs-Pt). Catalytic performance evaluations showed that Co@TiO2 NTs-Pt exhibits excellent low-temperature activity toward CH3SH oxidation, achieving approximately 95% conversion at room temperature and enabling complete oxidation of sulfur-containing intermediates at even lower temperatures than those required with Co@TiO2 NTs. Comprehensive characterization indicated that depositing Pt on the exterior surface enhances the electron-deficient environment within the nanotube cavity and induces surface lattice distortion, thereby raising the oxidation state of the confined Co species and increasing the concentration of oxygen vacancies. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further confirmed that this electronic-modulation strategy significantly strengthens CH3SH chemisorption and activation on the catalyst surface. Furthermore, in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) elucidated the reaction pathways governing CH3SH oxidation over the catalyst surface. Overall, this study deepens the understanding of electronic confinement effects in TiO2 NTs and provides a theoretical basis and technical guidance for designing advanced catalysts for the efficient low-temperature abatement of malodorous organic pollutants.

title: A two-stage lithium-ion battery voltage sensor fault diagnosis framework integrating reconstruction screening and prediction confirmation
Multidimensional Protein-Based Antimicrobial Materials: Construction, Mechanisms, and Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bacterial contamination and associated infections remain persistent threats to global public health. Proteins, as renewable biomacromolecules with diverse functional groups, programmable hierarchical structures, and favorable biocompatibility, have emerged as versatile building blocks for antimicrobial materials. Through self-assembly, amyloid-like aggregation, interfacial engineering, and chemical or physical functionalization, proteins can be constructed into zero-dimensional (0D) micro/nanoparticles, one-dimensional (1D) fibers, two-dimensional (2D) films and coatings, and three-dimensional (3D) hydrogels, aerogels, and sponge scaffolds. Dimensional architecture extends beyond morphological classification: it governs active-site exposure, interfacial contact, mass transport, mechanical properties, and antimicrobial-agent retention and release, thereby determining bactericidal activity, resistance to bacterial adhesion, and antibiofilm performance. Nevertheless, the relationships connecting dimensional construction, interfacial structure, antimicrobial mechanism, and application-specific performance remain fragmented. This review therefore adopts dimensionality as the central framework for critically examining the structural design, assembly, and functionalization of protein-based antimicrobial materials across 0D–3D architectures. Particular emphasis is placed on how dimensional features regulate the antimicrobial mechanisms involving membrane disruption, cell-wall hydrolysis, reactive oxygen species generation, physical bacterial trapping, controlled antimicrobial release, and resistance to bacterial adhesion. Recent advances in the applications of these antimicrobial materials, categorized by their dimensional architectures, are further evaluated across biomedicine, food preservation, functional textiles, and agriculture in relation to their operating environments and functional requirements. Finally, challenges concerning mechanistic validation, long-term stability, scalable manufacturing, biological safety, and application-specific evaluation are critically discussed to identify barriers to practical implementation and future directions for technological translation. Emerging opportunities in AI-assisted protein and peptide design, precise interfacial engineering, and multifunctional integration are further highlighted to guide the rational development of next-generation protein-based antimicrobial materials.

title: Interfacial Integration of Cross-Kingdom Membranes Establishes a Rechargeable Energy Cascade
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Engineering modular adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-mediated energy transduction pathways from the bottom up faces two key bottlenecks: first, detergent-dependent reconstitution typically impairs protein activity and energetic coupling efficiency due to disrupted native lipid environments and randomized protein orientation; second, physically separated ATP production and consumption modules suffer from severe diffusional ATP losses and inefficient intermodule cascade coupling. To address both limitations, we report a programmable, nondestructive strategy to construct a high-performance artificial organelle—the “chrometabosome”—through orthogonal peptide-driven fusion of photosynthetic chromatophores and energy-consuming erythrosomes. Bypassing detergent solubilization and reconstitution, this strategy not only preserves membrane proteins in their native lipid environment and functional state but also colocalizes ATP-producing and ATP-consuming modules within a single nanoscale compartment. This colocalization reduces the dependence of ATP utilization on intervesicle transport, producing a 3- to 4-fold kinetic enhancement at lower vesicle concentrations relative to nonintegrated controls. This light-rechargeable system offers a modular framework for versatile biohybrid energy nanosystems.

title: Frequency-constrained robust unit commitment for an integrated electricity-heat system considering heterogeneous resources
Power-sensitive partnerships for just nature-based solutions in urban informal settlements
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nature-based solutions should better redistribute benefits and reduce climate risks for vulnerable groups in urban informal settlements. To enable this, we argue for power-sensitive partnerships and a deep commitment to pluralism in values, ways of knowing, and understandings of nature.

title: Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS2 has long been considered a prime example of a Mott insulator driven by strong electron correlations. However, this view has been recently challenged by proposals which favor a band insulating state arising from interlayer dimerization. This ongoing debate opens a frontier in 1T-TaS2 research focusing on stacking order, and raises a fundamental question with broad implications for two-dimensional materials: can electronic phases be engineered by actively tuning interlayer coupling? Here, using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that uniaxial strain drives 1T-TaS2 from its insulating charge-density-wave phase into a stable metallic phase. This metallic phase, distinct from hydrostatic-pressure-induced or non-equilibrium hidden phases, emerges via a strain-induced rearrangement in the interlayer stacking of the Star-of-David charge order, effectively disrupting interlayer dimerization. Furthermore, the emergent metallic phase exhibits a significant quasiparticle mass renormalization, a hallmark of strong electron correlations, indicating its correlated nature and proximity to a Mott instability. This finding necessitates a re-evaluation of the interplay between structural and strong correlations in 1T-TaS2. The present results establish uniaxial strain as a powerful method for tuning the interlayer coupling, opening pathways for exploring quantum phases inaccessible under ambient conditions.

title: Techno-economic optimization of a low-carbon ammonia synthesis system integrated with coal-to‑hydrogen and power-to‑hydrogen production
Plant responses to blue light absorbing agrivoltaic systems
Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. It incorporates at least one method from each major MADM family and includes strategies to enhance resilience against rank reversal. Material consumptions are aggregated into satisfaction or criticality indices, while Monte Carlo simulation captures uncertainty and variability in consumption, lifetimes, and operational conditions. The methodology is applied to the EU including eight electricity generation technologies (wind, solar PV, solar CSP, hydro, biomass and waste, nuclear, coal, and natural gas) and 33 raw materials. Despite minor differences among MADM methods, the framework consistently converges on a ranking in which wind and solar PV are the most material-critical technologies, followed by solar CSP; coal, natural gas and nuclear occupy intermediate positions; biomass and waste, and hydro are the least critical alternatives. These findings highlight that EU decarbonisation strategies must be complemented by targeted raw material policies, including diversification of supply, recycling, material substitution, and strategic planning, to ensure that the transition to renewable electricity is not only low-carbon but also materially resilient and secure.

title: Climate-driven screening maps and design rules for PCM-assisted cooling of photovoltaic modules
Sublevel-selective electron spin hyperpolarization of triplet radical pairs in metal–organic frameworks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies because their electronic structures can be synthetically tailored and integrated into higher-order assemblies. Photogenerated radical pairs can exhibit spin hyperpolarization under ambient conditions, yet extending such spin dynamics from isolated molecules to structurally organized materials remains challenging. Here, we report a metal–organic framework that regulates the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within locally well-defined donor–acceptor arrangements. N,N’-di(4-pyridyl)−1,4,5,8-naphthalenetetracarboxdiimide is introduced into a zinc tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin-based framework. Dense donor–acceptor packing promotes efficient quenching of the porphyrin singlet excited state and selectively forms strongly coupled triplet radical pairs polarized in the zero-spin projection sublevel. These radical pairs exhibit narrow electron paramagnetic resonance signals and long spin-lattice relaxation times. Their spin-lattice relaxation dynamics persist in various guest solvents and vary with guest identity, demonstrating a route to chemically responsive spin materials based on porous, locally organized donor–acceptor frameworks.

title: Geopolitical exposure in cross-border electricity transmission: Evidence from Baltic desynchronization and interconnection disruptions
The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: Triarm Polycaprolactone Interface for Spatially Controlled Functionalization of Carbon Nanotube Fibers
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotube fibers (CNTF) with exceptional strength, electrical, and thermal conductivities possess the potential for deployment in electrochemical and analytical applications. For such applications, CNTF are typically encapsulated using polymeric interface membranes such as polyvinyl chloride (PVC) for accommodating functional elements or recognition molecules. These membranes typically assemble stochastically on CNTF surfaces owing to the nonuniform interfacial interaction energies between the characteristic groups of the polymers and the CNTF surface. This stochastic assembly of encapsulating membranes subsequently inhibits the homogeneous distribution of recognition molecules on the CNTF surface, which influences the analytical performances. Herein, a triarm polycaprolactone (3-PCL) block copolymer is designed to homogenize the interfacial energies between the polymeric membranes and the CNTF surface. The 3-PCL interface is hypothesized to enable spatially controlled assembly of polymeric membranes on the CNTF surface and subsequently a homogeneous distribution of recognition molecules. As an illustration, the CNTF with a 3-PCL interface is demonstrated as an ion-selective microelectrode (ISE) for selective and sensitive detection of ammonium ions (NH4+) via homogeneous incorporation of a NH4+-specific ionophores within an encapsulating PVC membrane on the CNTF surface. An LOD and linear response range of 1 × 10–7 M and 1 × 10–7 to 1.0 × 10–1 M, respectively, were achieved. These values are an order higher as compared to ionophores incorporated within the PVC membrane on the CNTF surface without the 3-PCL interface. Further, a linear two-arm polymer (2-PCL) was evaluated as an interface for validation of significantly higher and stable analytical responses that could be achieved using the 3-PCL interface. Thus, the 3-PCL possesses the potential to be an ideal interface for incorporation of functional materials and recognition elements within polymeric membranes on the CNTF surface for the development of high-performance electrochemical and analytical devices.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
Energy poverty in an era of geopolitical instability: The role of Chinese FDI and south–south cooperation in Africa
abstract: The rising geopolitical fragmentation, driven by geopolitical tensions, conflicts and wars, has reshaped the global energy landscape, increasing uncertainty and vulnerability in energy markets. These disruptions present serious challenges for different economies in the Global South, where countries already face significant difficulties in facilitating energy transition and mitigating energy poverty. In this context, South-South cooperation may represent an important tool to address energy challenges, particularly through foreign investment. This study investigates the contribution of Chinese FDI to reducing energy poverty in Africa through different channels and whether conflict conditions influence the extent to which Chinese FDI contributes to improving energy outcomes. Our study contributes to the literature on the role of Chinese foreign capital in reducing energy poverty in Africa by examining both the underlying mechanisms and the potential role of conflict conditions in shaping these effects. To empirically explore this complex nexus, we rely on Structural Equation Modelling using a set of energy and socioeconomic variables from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal a significant positive association between Chinese FDI and energy performance, with the prosperity channel representing the main mechanism. This association appears weaker in conflict-affected contexts, suggesting that geopolitical stability conditions the extent to which foreign investment is associated with improved energy outcomes. Policymakers in the region should consider creating a more attractive and stable investment environment to promote trade ties with Chinese companies, as these ties could be used as a tool to alleviate energy poverty.

title: Is inclusive green growth resilient to energy-related geopolitical risk? The role of energy affordability as a binding constraint
Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Systematic and precise regulation of coordination environments in single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains challenging due to thermodynamic constraints and kinetic traps. Herein, we report a thermodynamic-guided strategy to tailor the local coordination of Fe single atoms on CoWO4 support by regulating oxygen chemical potential. Via fine-tuning hydrogen partial pressure during pyrolysis, a series of Fe1Ox SACs is synthesized with well-defined Fe-O coordination numbers ranging from 3 to 6. Combining operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations, Fe1O4 is identified as the optimal configuration for hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) electrosynthesis, which delivers balanced kinetics by moderating free water dissociation for *NH3 generation and strengthening HCHO chemisorption via pronounced Fe 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization near the Fermi level. As a result, the Fe1O4 SAC achieves a HMTA yield of 0.21 mmol h−1 cm−2 with 83.04% Faradaic efficiency at 1.75 V and stability over 200 h in a flow cell. This work establishes a universal thermodynamic approach for precise coordination engineering of single-atom electrocatalysts and provides a general paradigm for kinetically balancing complex multi-intermediate electrocatalytic systems.

title: Dynamic chlorine vacancies enable X-ray-specific afterglow
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Afterglow luminescence in inorganic materials is conventionally attributed to pre-existing static defects that trap and gradually release charge carriers. However, the observation of afterglow activated only by specific types of excitation sources, such as X-ray-specific afterglow in certain phosphors, highlights an opportunity to move beyond this static trap model. Here we show that Bi3+ doped Cs2ZrCl6 crystals exhibit afterglow exclusively under X-ray excitation, with no such effect under ultraviolet illumination. We demonstrate that this behavior arises from the in-situ generation and self-healing of metastable chlorine vacancies (VCl) specifically driven by X-ray irradiation, directly correlating with afterglow kinetics. Advancing beyond previous vague attributions to Frenkel defects, our multimodal evidence unambiguously pinpoints VCl as the operative defect species. This discovery challenges the paradigm that afterglow requires static pre-existing traps, establishing a dynamic mechanism where metastable defects are created by the probing radiation and gradually disappear when radiation is removed. We further manipulate the afterglow kinetic through Sn4+ induced modulation of vacancy formation energy, extending the afterglow duration to multiple hours while maintaining a high light yield of 55670 photons MeV−1 and a low detection limit of 30.81 nGyair s−1. Finally, we integrate these crystals into a flexible PDMS composite film for X-ray imaging, achieving a high spatial resolution of 23.6 lp mm−1 that enables high-fidelity imaging of curved objects via time-resolved readout. Our findings open an avenue for designing smart scintillators with programmable, radiation-specific responses, with implications for flexible radiography and beyond.

title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising laser-gain media for their direct bandgap and strong excitonic effects. However, existing TMD lasers typically rely on mechanically exfoliated or high-temperature chemical-vapor-deposition-grown materials, with their atomic-scale thickness inherently limiting the available optical gain volume. Here, we report room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 (BM-MoS2) thin films in whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) cavities. Using solution exfoliation and spray coating under ambient conditions, we produce area- and thickness-scalable BM-MoS2 films composed of electronically decoupled MoS2 monolayers separated by organic spacers. This layered architecture preserves the intrinsic monolayer excitonic properties while providing a tunable gain volume beyond that of an isolated monolayer. Integrated with WGM cavities, the thickness-scalable BM-MoS2 films enable a balance between the quality (Q) and optical confinement (\(\varGamma\)) factors. Power-dependent measurements reveal key lasing signatures, including a threshold-like input-output crossover accompanied by linewidth narrowing at a pump power of approximately 1.4 nW, and pump-induced polarization selection. Solution-processable BM-MoS2 thus offers a scalable gain medium for thin-film laser photonics.

title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-numerical-aperture (NA) oblique plane microscopy enables noninvasive fluorescence imaging of subcellular dynamics without radical sample modification. However, performance degrades at depth in multicellular specimens as scattering and refractive-index heterogeneity raise out-of-focus background. We report a two-photon oblique plane microscope that improves resolution at depth by combining high-NA single-objective detection with multiphoton plane illumination. The microscope achieves ~ 300 nm lateral and ~ 650 nm axial resolution, with single-molecule sensitivity and 5 × faster volumetric acquisition (up to 3.25 × 106 voxels s−1). In multicellular contexts, near-infrared nonlinear excitation enhances contrast throughout the illumination depth by ~ 2 × and restores volumetric resolving power by > 2 × relative to linear excitation. We demonstrate these capabilities through molecular imaging of epithelial tissue, stem-cell-derived gastruloids, and living fruit fly embryos, including multicolor transcription-factor dynamics, optogenetic subcellular control, and single-mRNA tracking, all using standard glass-based mounting.

title: Chirality inversion in DNA-assembled nanorod superlattices via site-specific asymmetric anchoring of single nanospheres
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) chiral superlattices of plasmonic nanoparticles have attracted considerable interest due to their broad potential across various fields. However, achieving facile control over their handedness without compromising structural integrity remains a persistent challenge. Here, we report a distinct class of 2D superlattices, 4-arm pinwheel arrays with tunable configurations, through defined patch size mismatch in DNA origami-templated assembly. A superlattice framework possessing preconfigured mirror-image units is created and utilized as a platform for DNA programming of chirality. We demonstrate a single-degree-of-freedom strategy that controls the handedness of the entire superlattice through DNA-enabled site-selective and asymmetric binding of a single gold nanoparticle into the mirror-image units. These local minimal perturbations preserve long-range crystalline order while generating opposite chiroptical responses via altered plasmonic near-field coupling. Our work expands the design scope of programmable materials toward chiral functional metasurfaces, and establishes a chirality-engineering approach that circumvents global structural reconstruction.

title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Kondo insulators are paradigmatic strongly correlated materials, traditionally found in f-electron compounds. They originate from the hybridization between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, which opens a gap in the electronic spectrum. Two-dimensional moiré systems provide a new route to flat bands with strong electron correlation, which host localized moments at half filling. Here we report signatures, based on local conductivity measurements using microwave impedance microscopy, of a Kondo insulator in a moiré superlattice of monolayer WS2 / bilayer WSe2, in which one WSe2 layer carries flat moiré bands and the other dispersive ones. When both layers are partially doped with two holes per moiré unit cell in total, an insulating state appears when the moiré band contains less than one hole. The insulator becomes metallic above a certain threshold magnetic field, evidence for the singlet nature of the Kondo insulator, and the observed behavior is reproduced by a periodic Anderson model. Our results open a route to simulating Kondo physics in tunable moiré systems.

title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cracking of polyolefins is a prerequisite for their selective conversion over microporous zeolites to value-added small molecules such as monocyclic aromatics. However, cracking and aromatization often proceed concurrently, creating an intrinsic accessibility-selectivity conflict that limits aromatic yield and productivity. This paper describes a strategy that temporally decouples polyolefin cracking from selective aromatization in one-pot with tandem catalysts. This strategy delivers an aromatic yield of ca. 60.3 wt% within 0.5 h at 380 °C from postconsumer polyolefins over 40 consecutive cycles, corresponding to an aromatic space-time yield of 11 g gcat−1 h−1, more than twofold higher than reported values of ≤ 5 g gcat−1 h−1. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal that self-pillared pentasil zeolite rapidly and processively cracks polyolefins to small olefinic intermediates below 320 °C, enabling temporal decoupling of low-temperature cracking from higher-temperature aromatization through distinct dominant kinetic windows. Process modeling further suggests favorable economic potential and life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions 26% lower than fossil-based aromatics production and 66% lower than incineration. This work establishes temporal decoupling as a reaction-engineering strategy for reconciling polymer accessibility with micropore-controlled selectivity in plastic upcycling.

title: Preadipocyte-Derived Decellularized Extracellular Matrix-Functionalized Three Dimensionally Printed Scaffolds Regulate Vascularized Adipose Tissue Regeneration via Modulation of Selected Paracrine Factors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The clinical efficacy of soft tissue reconstruction is severely hindered by unpredictable graft resorption and inadequate vascularization. Traditional synthetic implant scaffolds offer mechanical support, with limited bioactivity for adipose tissue regeneration. In this study, we developed a “three-in-one” bioinstructive platform (dPCL) integrating structural support, signal induction, and immunomodulation by functionalizing a 3D-printed polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) derived from 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. The obtained dECM-functionalized scaffold provided essential biochemical cues. In vitro assays demonstrated that dPCL significantly enhanced preadipocyte adhesion and adipogenic differentiation. Besides, the dECM-functionalized scaffold was found to modulate the secretion of selected paracrine factors, markedly upregulating the secretion of adiponectin, VEGF, and IL-10, which facilitated cell differentiation and robust endothelial network formation.
