In vivo evaluation in a murine subcutaneous model confirmed that dPCL scaffolds effectively supported the formation of stable, well-vascularized adipose tissue. Furthermore, the dECM-functionalized scaffold enhanced the recruitment and accumulation of proregenerative M2 macrophages, maintaining an M2-dominant tissue microenvironment that facilitated graft integration. In summary, current findings demonstrate that integrating cell-specific dECM with 3D-printed scaffolds creates a multifaceted bioactive platform that overcomes the critical barriers of vascularization and metabolic integration, presenting a highly promising strategy for functional soft tissue regeneration.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Multicomponent Cycloadditions
abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions provide a powerful strategy for constructing complex cyclic frameworks from simple unsaturated building blocks with high atom and step efficiencies. This Review highlights the progress made in transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions based on the size of the cyclic products formed. First, reactions that construct five-membered rings, including [2 + 2 + 1], [3 + 1 + 1], and [2 + 1 + 1 + 1] cycloadditions, are discussed with an emphasis on key reactive intermediates, such as carbon monoxide, vinylidenes, carbenoids, and nitrenes. Next, six-membered-ring-forming processes, particularly [2 + 2 + 2], [3 + 2 + 1], [4 + 1 + 1], and [2 + 1 + 2 + 1] cycloadditions, are described, highlighting combinations of alkynes, alkenes, and heteroatom-containing components. The Review then covers strategies for constructing seven-membered rings via [3 + 2 + 2] and [4 + 2 + 1] cycloadditions. Finally, emerging methods that enable the formation of eight- and nine-membered rings through higher-order multicomponent cycloadditions are described. This Review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the conceptual framework, mechanistic principles, and synthetic possibilities of transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions by organizing them according to ring size and cycloaddition components.

title: From biological principles to battery interfaces: recent progress in bio-inspired design for aqueous zinc-ion batteries
Molecular Bridging Flexibility Enables Closed‐Pore Engineering in Hard Carbon for Enhanced Plateau Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closed pores are critical structural motifs that enable low‐voltage plateau capacity in hard carbon (HC) anodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet their controllable construction through precursor molecular design remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate molecular bridging flexibility as an effective design principle for regulating closed‐pore formation in HCs. The flexibility/rigidity of polymer precursors is tailored by distinct bridging configurations, namely Ar─CH 2 ─Ar and Ar─O─C bridges, where oxygen‐containing bridges enhance segmental flexibility. During early‐stage pyrolysis, flexible precursor segments provide higher conformational freedom, inducing curved carbon skeletons and promoting the formation of semi‐open sub‐1 nm pores. Driven by high surface energy, these semi‐open pores undergo pore‐mouth closure during high‐temperature pyrolysis, generating abundant closed pores. The resulting HC exhibits a closed porosity of 0.12 cm 3 g −1 and a pore size 1.13 nm, which enhances plateau capacity and sodium‐ion diffusion kinetics. Consequently, the flexible‐precursor‐derived HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 356.1 mAh g −1 and a plateau capacity of 242.7 mAh g −1 . Moreover, a practical 1.2 Ah pouch cell achieves 217.2 Wh kg −1 and retains 81.2% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work establishes a molecular‐level strategy for closed‐pore engineering in HC anodes for high‐performance sodium‐ion batteries.

title: Semiconductor‐Plasmon‐Enabled Efficient Neodymium Electroluminescence in Lead‐Free Perovskite Near‐Infrared Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide‐doped lead‐free perovskite nanocrystals are promising candidates for near‐infrared (NIR) optoelectronics, yet their performance is limited by inefficient exciton‐to‐lanthanide energy‐transfer, surface non‐radiative losses, and intrinsically slow 4f‐4f radiative transitions. Here, we report highly efficient Cs 3 YCl 6 :Sb 3+ , Nd 3+ nanocrystals enabling high‐performance NIR photoluminescence and electroluminescence. The isolated [YCl 6 ] 3− octahedral framework confines excitons and facilitates efficient Sb 3+ ‐induced localized defect‐state emission sensitization to Nd 3+ , leading to intense NIR emissions at 890, 1070, and 1350 nm with an ultra‐high NIR photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 65.9% for Nd 3+ ‐based lead‐free perovskite nanocrystals. Sotalol molecular passivation further suppresses surface non‐radiative recombination and improves energy‐transfer efficiency from 51.5% to 66.8%. Moreover, Cu 2‐x S is introduced as a semiconductor localized surface plasmon resonance layer, its broad NIR plasmonic absorption peak with a maximum near 1070 nm, overlaps well with the Nd 3+ emission, thereby selectively accelerating the spontaneous radiative decay at 890 and 1070 nm by 4.1‐and 9.2‐fold, respectively. Consequently, the optimized NIR light‐emitting diodes delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 10.89%, a peak power density of 3.8 mW cm −2 , and a T 50 lifetime of 389 min, representing a breakthrough among various rare earths‐doped NIR light‐emitting diodes.

title: Interfacial Trap and Field Regulation Enables Bias‐Switchable Dual‐Mode Organic Photodetectors for Adaptive Near‐Infrared Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating high‐gain photomultiplication (PM) and low‐power photovoltaic (PV) modes into a single organic photodetector (OPD) enables adaptive sensing across varying light intensities. However, reconciling efficient carrier extraction in the PV mode with high trap‐assisted photomultiplication gain in the PM mode, while maintaining comparable temporal responses, remains challenging. Here, we employ a perovskite nanocrystal@ferroelectric polymer (PNC@FP) composite as a multifunctional interlayer that simultaneously facilitates hole transport and regulates trap‐assisted photomultiplication in dual‐mode OPDs. While the PNCs supply shallow Pb 2+ trap states as the PM‐inducing layer, the FP matrix concurrently partially passivates surface defects to suppress non‐radiative recombination, imposes a permanent dipole field that facilitates hole extraction under 0 V (PV mode), and enhances dielectric screening at the interface, which extends trap‐induced band bending, thereby narrowing the effective barrier for hole tunneling under forward bias. Consequently, the device achieves external quantum efficiency (EQE)/specific detectivity (D*) values of 48.8%/4.18 × 10 12 Jones (PV, 0 V) and 10,656%/3.18 × 10 13 Jones (PM, 1 V) at 850 nm, while maintaining µs‐scale responses in both modes. A programmable circuit further enables autonomous PV/PM switching with light intensity, as demonstrated by real‐time recovery of binary‐coded 850 nm optical signals under dynamically varying illumination.

title: Reconstructing Colloidal NiO x Contacts for Efficient and Lamination‐Resilient Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) increasingly rely on NiO x /self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) buried contacts, yet the geometric and surface heterogeneity of colloidal NiO x on textured fluorine‐doped tin oxide (FTO) compromises SAM assembly, perovskite crystallization, and interfacial strain uniformity. Here, β‐acryloyloxypropionic acid (CEA) is used to reconstruct both the mesoscale organization and exposed facets of NiO x . Through carboxyl anchoring and photoinduced interparticle coupling, CEA converts zero‐dimensional NiO x aggregates into chain‐connected assemblies that form conformal contacts while retaining colloidal processability. CEA also preferentially adsorbs on high‐energy NiO(111) facets, producing a NiO(100)‐dominated surface that promotes homogeneous SAM assembly. This coupled dimensional and facet reconstruction improves bottom‐interface crystallization, suppresses non‐radiative recombination and residual microstrain, and limits stress localization during BIPV‐grade lamination. The resulting PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.53% and a stabilized output of 27.52%, while 833.70 cm 2 modules deliver 20.85%. After lamination, semitransparent bifacial modules retain 98.98% and 99.56% of their initial front and rear‐side PCEs, respectively, and maintain 89% and 88% after 2400 h under ISOS‐L‐3 and ISOS‐D‐3 protocols. This work establishes molecularly reconstructed NiO x as a scalable interface for efficient and lamination‐resilient perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Multi‐Timescale UV Memory With Wavelength‐Programmable Retention for Robust Graded Discharge‐Risk Warning
abstract: ABSTRACT Graded ultraviolet (UV) arc‐discharge warning requires optoelectronic memory that converts transient UV inputs into photocurrent traces retaining both recent signal changes and longer discharge history. Here, we report a C8‐BTBT/Sr 2 Nb 3 O 10 heterostructure for wavelength‐programmable multi‐timescale UV memory. Inspired by wavelength‐selective photoreception in mantis shrimp eyes, the heterostructure maps different UV excitation wavelengths onto distinct photocurrent‐decay profiles, achieving an approximately 44‐fold separation in the decay time between 350 and 280 nm excitation, with the device response evolving from rapid recovery to sustained retention. This wavelength‐dependent relaxation is supported by optical‐gap contrast, staggered energy alignment, and oxygen‐vacancy‐associated trapping, establishing the physical basis for multi‐timescale UV memory. Applied to graded discharge‐risk warning, the multiwavelength memory readout recognizes the early‐warning state with 99.2% accuracy under normal monitoring and increases the disturbed‐condition average accuracy by 29.3 percentage points relative to no‐memory readout. These results establish excitation‐wavelength‐programmed UV memory as a front‐end strategy for temporal readout and robust graded risk warning.

title: Scalable Hybrid Photocatalysts for Visible‐Light Degradation of Waterborne Organic Contaminants
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic micropollutants in aquatic environments pose persistent risks to human health and ecosystems, yet current remediation technologies face scalability, stability, and secondary pollution challenges. Here, we report a visible‐light‐responsive photocatalyst prepared by covalently immobilizing benzothioxanthene imide ( BTI ), a ton‐scale industrial dye, onto macroscopic oxide supports (Al 2 O 3 , zeolites). The densely grafted BTI forms H‐aggregates that suppress radiative decay, enabling efficient interfacial electron transfer, generating hydroxyl (OH • ) and superoxide (O 2 •– ) radicals without co‐catalysts. This system achieves degradation of a diverse range of contaminants (e.g., dyes, pharmaceuticals, and agrochemicals) into CO 2 and CO under low‐intensity visible light, with no detectable activity loss over 12 months of continuous operation. A pilot‐scale flow reactor packed with millimeter‐sized BTI ‐functionalized beads demonstrates efficient treatment of real dye mixtures under ambient conditions, highlighting scalability, recoverability, and compatibility with decentralized wastewater treatment. This work establishes a sustainable, modular platform for water purification, particularly in resource‐limited settings.

title: Covalently Integrated MXene–Fluorinated Polymer Electrolytes for 714 Wh Kg −1 Lithium–Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer electrolytes are promising for high‐energy and safe lithium–metal batteries yet limited by inadequate mechanical integrity, sluggish Li + transport, and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Here, we report a covalently integrated MXene–fluorinated gel polymer electrolyte (MF‐GPE) through in situ polymerization. Acrylate‐grafted MXene nanosheets act as chemically anchored crosslinkers within a fluorinated polymer network, distinguishing from conventional physically blended composites. The covalent framework not only mechanically reinforces the polymer matrix but also regulates Li + solvation structure and lowers the activation energy for Li + transport. Consequently, the MF‐GPE enables uniform lithium deposition and constructs robust, inorganic‐rich interphases on both lithium–metal anodes and high‐voltage cathodes. It delivers an ionic conductivity of 3.3 mS cm −1 at 25°C and supports stable cycling of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 , LiCoO 2 and LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4 cathodes at cut‐off voltages up to 4.9 V. Notably, a MF‐GPE based Li||LiCoO 2 pouch cell achieves cell‐level energy densities of 713.9 Wh kg −1 at 4.8 V and 605.2 Wh kg −1 at 4.6 V, maintaining stable operation over 60 cycles, while 18650 cylindrical cells operate stably for 500 cycles. Ah‐class pouch cells demonstrate outstanding safety under nail‐penetration and overcharge tests. These findings establish covalent MXene‐polymer integration to couple ion solvation structure and interphase stabilization for high‐energy, abuse‐tolerant lithium–metal batteries.

title: Spin Transport in Epitaxial Magnon Junctions With Pt‐Nanoparticle‐Decorated Y 3 Fe 5 O 12 /Gd 3 Ga 5 O 12 /Y 3 Fe 5 O 12
abstract: ABSTRACT The excitation, propagation, manipulation, and detection of magnons are central to magnonics. High‐quality ferromagnetic insulator (FI)/antiferromagnetic insulator (AFI)/ferromagnetic insulator (FI) magnon junctions are predicted to achieve nearly 100% magnon junction ratio (MJR), making them attractive for non‐volatile spintronic/magnonic devices. However, lattice‐mismatched AFI spacers generally disrupt the epitaxial growth of the top low‐damping yttrium iron garnet (Y 3 Fe 5 O 12 , YIG) layer, degrading its crystalline quality and limiting magnon transmission. Here, we demonstrate that Pt‐nanoparticle decoration enables fully epitaxial magnon junctions with a well‐defined antiparallel magnetic configuration. The incorporated Pt nanoparticles enhance the coercivity of the top YIG layer while preserving its high crystalline quality and low magnetic damping. A clear magnon junction effect is observed, yielding an intrinsic MJR of 23% extracted by peak analysis. Besides, it is found that possible long‐range magnetic order induced by Fe diffusion into the GGG spacer may give rise to interlayer exchange coupling and enhance magnon transmission, leading to an increased MJR at low temperatures, whereas paramagnon‐mediated spin transport is proposed to dominate at elevated temperatures. Our results provide new insights into spin/magnon transport in epitaxial magnon junctions and offer a promising strategy for developing high‐performance magnonic devices.

title: Design Principles of Bioadhesives for Wearable and Implantable Bioelectronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Bioadhesives have emerged as essential materials for bridging the interface between medical devices and biological tissues, offering conformal, biocompatible, and minimally invasive adhesion in complex physiological environments. Their importance is particularly evident in wearable and implantable bioelectronics, which demand stable integration with dynamic and often moist tissues. Wearable devices must maintain long‐term skin contact while accommodating motion and sweat, whereas implantable systems require secure fixation to internal organs and tissues while limiting inflammation and fibrosis. In both applications, conventional adhesives fall short in achieving reliable adhesion under such conditions. Bioadhesives address these challenges by enabling intimate tissue‐device contact and supporting mechanical and electrical performance. However, the design of bioadhesives for biomedical electronics involves multifaceted requirements, including interfacial toughness, energy dissipation, biological compatibility, and environmental adaptability. This review organizes the field through a design‐evaluation‐integration framework that links interfacial chemistry and energy dissipation with physiological constraints, application‐matched evaluation, failure‐mode feedback, and device‐level performance. We also discuss practical considerations related to biodegradation, anti‐swelling, immune response, and delivery strategies for difficult‐to‐access sites. By identifying application‐dependent trade‐offs among adhesive, mechanical, electrical, and biological requirements, this framework supports the comparative assessment of bioadhesives for wearable and implantable electronic systems.

title: High‐Efficiency Perovskite‐Organic Tandem Solar Cells Enabled by Perovskite Crystallization Optimization and Metal‐Free Interconnecting Layer
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite‐organic tandem solar cells (PO‐TSCs) offer a promising route toward high‐efficiency and cost‐effective photovoltaics by combining wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with narrow‐bandgap organic solar cells. Nevertheless, achieving high‐performance PO‐TSCs still faces key challenges: open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) loss in the WBG perovskite sub‐cell and optoelectrical loss at the interconnecting layer (ICL). Here, we incorporate 4‐nitrophenethylamine hydrochloride (4N‐PEACl), a functional additive bearing a strong electron‐withdrawing group (‐NO 2 ), into the WBG perovskite precursor solution to modulate crystallization kinetics and passivate bulk defects. This additive significantly improves crystallinity and phase stability, suppresses non‐radiative recombination and enhances charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the optimized 1.85 eV WBG single‐junction PSC achieves a champion efficiency of 19.79%, with V OC increasing from 1.349 to 1.388 V. Furthermore, the optimal PO‐TSC achieves an efficiency of 27.10% with an ICL of PCBM/AZO/SnO 2 /PEDOT:PSS/Ph‐4PACz. This work highlights the efficacy of ‐NO 2 ‐functionalized molecules in improving WBG perovskite film quality and provides new design strategy for low‐cost but effective ICLs in PO‐TSCs.

title: Decoding Tumor Metabolic Dysregulation Through Single‐Cell Analysis Informs the Inverse Design of Therapeutic Nanozymes
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐node interventions often fail against tumor metabolic networks due to dynamic compensation and pathway redundancy, necessitating synergistic, multi‐node strategies. However, translating high‐dimensional single‐cell omics into physicochemical parameters for materials design remains a major challenge. Herein, a cross‐scale inverse design paradigm for therapeutic nanozymes is proposed that maps single‐cell metabolic demands onto quantum‐chemical descriptors. Using hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a model, integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and metabolic flux analyses revealed a triple vulnerability network involving lactate accumulation, focal hypoxia, and oxidative stress imbalance. Guided by first‐principles calculations and multiparameter screening based on reaction energy barriers and Bader charge transfer, 260 candidate materials were evaluated. This screening identified a nitrogen–phosphorus dual‐coordinated gold single‐atom nanozyme (APNC) with exceptional lactate oxidase (LOX)‐, catalase (CAT)‐, and peroxidase (POD)‐like activities and strong piezoelectric polarization. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that APNC remodels the HCC microenvironment by depleting lactate and alleviating hypoxia, thereby disrupting glycolysis and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). APNC‐mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieved 95% tumor inhibition in vivo. This inverse design strategy bridges single‐cell metabolic profiling and atomic‐scale material engineering, establishing a versatile framework for precision nanozyme development across tumors and metabolic disorders.

title: Ion‐Access Engineering for High‐Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte‐Gated Transistors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrolyte‐gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low‐voltage operation and strong ionic–electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography‐free ion‐access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet‐printed solid‐state electrolytes. Laser‐defined pores penetrating the top electrode and semiconductor layer create direct ionic pathways to the channel region, significantly enhancing ionic–electronic coupling. As a result, the devices exhibit more than two orders of magnitude enhancement in transconductance (up to 9.17 mS), over 300‐fold enhancement in current density reaching 51.8 A cm −2 , and an on/off ratio approaching 10 7 , together with accelerated switching dynamics compared to devices without pore structures (>6‐fold reduction in turn‐on time constant). This ion‐access engineering strategy is compatible with multiple organic semiconductor materials and provides an effective structural strategy for overcoming ionic transport limitations in vertical OEGTs. Moreover, array‐level demonstrations and a proof‐of‐concept NARMA2 reservoir computing task (NMSE = 0.107) further illustrate the scalability and neuromorphic application potential of this platform.

title: A Scalable Protrusion‐Targeted Electrolyte Enables 500 Wh Kg −1 Lithium Metal Batteries With 500‐Cycle Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is severely impeded by limited cycle life arising from irreversible lithium dendrite growth. Herein, we design a scalable, protrusion‐targeted electrolytes to achieve industrial‐scale LMBs through retarding the formation of dendritic lithium embryos. The site‐selective‐blocking molecules preferentially adsorbs onto protrusive sites of lithium deposition, which inhibits the local lithium deposition rate to block dendrite initiation. More importantly, the abundant polar functional groups of adsorbed molecules induce directional enrichment of anions, achieving passivation repair of fresh dendritic lithium. This synergy of selective adsorption and interfacial repair effectively inhibits the self‐amplifying growth of lithium dendrites, thereby mitigating continuous electrolyte consumption. An 8 Ah‐level pouch cell with 500 Wh kg −1 delivers an impressive capacity retention of over 80% after 525 cycles. Furthermore, we show large‐scale production of electrolytes for preparing industrial‐scale LMBs. This design offers a viable approach for long‐life LMBs at an industry compatible scale.

title: A Perspective on Continuous Superlattices and Device‐by‐Design Pathways Toward Electrically Driven Perovskite Lasers and Cooperative Emission
abstract: ABSTRACT Halide perovskites are emerging optical gain media; however, electrically assisted lasing is currently prohibited by Joule heating, ion migration, injection imbalance, high‐density non‐radiative recombination, and contact‐related optical losses. This Perspective summarizes recent progress on optically pumped micro‐ and nanolasers and identifies materials and resonator architectures relevant to electrical operation. We further distinguish current‐induced lasing from superradiance and superfluorescence stemming from cooperative exciton emission. We then consider continuous perovskite superlattices containing experimentally verified periodic electronic potentials, as a proposed platform for controlling carrier transport, energetic disorder, and optical transitions. If such architectures also preserve coherent and spectrally homogeneous exciton synchronization, they may support transient cooperative emission. Steady‐state bad‐cavity cooperative lasing is a distinct, more demanding objective requiring common‐mode synchronization and repumping that sustains collective coherence. By separating established demonstrations from proposed materials concepts, we outline a materials‐ and device‐design roadmap toward electrically driven perovskite lasers and cooperative light sources.

title: Biomimetic Optically Encoded Hydrogel Fiber Enables Simultaneous Olfactory‐Mechanosensory Perception for Robotic Plume Tracing
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision‐denied environments. Yet current olfactory‐mechanosensory systems typically rely on separated sensing units, limiting co‐localized mechanochemical discrimination. Here, we report a biomimetic flexible optical fiber (BFOF) comprising a coaxial hydrogel fiber with distributed, self‐assembled odor‐sensitive metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) on its exterior, enabling simultaneous decoding of wind vectors and olfactory cues within a single compact optical architecture. Inspired by the spatially integrated mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors in ant antennae, the BFOF employs conformal MOF‐hydrogel interfaces to enhance evanescent‐field coupling without compromising receptor activity or waveguiding, partitioning multidimensional airflow attenuation and odor fluorescence into separable optical channels for low‐crosstalk olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion. Therefore, it achieves high sensitivity, fine directional selectivity, and fast temporal response across a wide range of airflow conditions. It identifies 16 individual gases, 96 mixtures, and the physiological states (unripe, ripe, overripe, and rotten) of 8 fruits with high accuracy. Coupled with a lightweight machine‐learning framework, this work establishes rapid, precise, and closed‐loop anemotactic navigation and multi‐target odor tracing in complex three‐dimensional (3D) spaces, offering a compact optical sensing platform for embodied robotic olfaction beyond static gas classification.

title: Gigacycle Fatigue Resistance and Cyclic Phase Separation in Metastable Nanocrystalline Cu–Ag Alloy Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanocrystalline metals derive their exceptional strength from a high density of grain boundaries (GBs), but under cyclic loading those same boundaries are unstable, driving abnormal grain growth that seeds fatigue cracking. Solute‐mediated grain boundary stabilization is shown here to extend nanocrystalline fatigue life by orders of magnitude. A metastable nanocrystalline Cu–42 at.% Ag alloy thin film survives 1.2 billion cycles at strain amplitudes exceeding 1.1%. To our knowledge, no other metallic thin film has shown gigacycle fatigue resistance at such extreme strain amplitudes, while comparison with literature data requires care given differences in testing conditions. A combination of microresonator‐based very‐high‐cycle fatigue testing, electron microscopy, and atomistic simulations reveals a composition‐dependent transition in the governing mechanism. In dilute Cu–3Ag, solute clusters kinetically pin interfacial disconnections and slow boundary migration, extending fatigue life but not preventing eventual failure via abnormal grain growth. In contrast, concentrated Cu–42Ag exhibits stable grain boundaries for over a billion cycles. Fatigue damage is ultimately associated with a previously unreported fatigue‐induced phase separation: strain‐enhanced transport decomposes the metastable solid solution into semi‐coherent Cu‐ and Ag‐rich domains. Solute‐stabilized nanocrystalline alloy thin films thus offer a route to gigacycle fatigue resistance in microdevices, and cyclic phase separation emerges as a distinct damage mode.

title: Correction to “Lipid Nanoparticles Optimized for Targeting and Release of Nucleic Acid”
Li–B–Mg Composite Foils With a LiB 0.88 Microrod Array Enable Ultrathin Self‐Supporting Lithium Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting lithium foils (USSLFs, ≤50 µm) are highly desirable for high‐energy‐density batteries, as eliminating current collectors enhances energy density and reduces material costs. However, the intrinsic mechanical vulnerability of metallic Li remains a critical barrier to both the fabrication and long‐term cycling of USSLFs. Herein, we develop a Li‐rich Li–B–Mg composite foil (LBM) through sequential melt alloying followed by post‐solidification thermomechanical processing, yielding a dense and interconnected LiB 0.88 microrod array with LiMg and MgB 2 lithiophilic phases within the Li‐rich matrix. This architecture enables large‐area (>170 cm 2 ) self‐supporting foils down to 15 µm while preserving a high Li content. During cycling, the microrod array redistributes local stress and restrains deformation, preserving the internal architecture and accessibility of lithiophilic sites. These sites, in turn, favor Li accommodation within the electrode interior, suppressing surface Li accumulation and alleviating local stress concentration. This self‐sustained coupling between stress regulation and lithiophilic guidance supports stable cycling for over 5000 h in symmetric cells using 50 µm LBM foils with about 10% thickness expansion, while 15 µm foils cycle for over 500 h at a depth of discharge of about 37.4%. This work advances the design of practical USSLFs for high‐energy lithium metal batteries.

title: Pulsed Electrosynthesis of Conformal High‐Entropy Metallic Glass Skins for Durable Industrial Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs) combine compositional diversity with a grain‐boundary‐free amorphous topology, making them attractive as electrocatalytic interfaces. However, their synthesis remains challenging because multicomponent transition‐metal alloys favor crystallization over vitrification. Here, we report a room‐temperature pulsed electrosynthesis (PES) strategy that kinetically traps HEMG skins, defined here as continuous, conformal HEMG coatings approximately 100 nm thick, directly on practical electrodes under ambient aqueous conditions. Using crystallization‐prone FeCoNiMo, millisecond ultrahigh‐current pulses induce burst multimetal nucleation while suppressing diffusion‐mediated crystallization, enabling programmable control over crystallinity, morphology, and composition. The resulting chemically homogeneous, grain‐boundary‐free skins suppress localized corrosion and structural collapse, favoring spatially distributed surface reconstruction. FeCoNiMo HEMG‐skinned electrodes sustain alkaline hydrogen evolution at 2 A cm −2 for over 1,300 h, whereas crystalline counterparts fail within approximately 200 h. As bifunctional electrodes in an anion‐exchange‐membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), they achieve 1 A cm −2 at 1.706 V and operate for 1,200 h, outperforming the Pt/C‖IrO 2 benchmark under identical conditions. Roll‐to‐roll upgrading of commercial Ni mesh (0.5 m × 2 m) further demonstrates fabrication scalability. These results establish PES‐driven HEMG skinning as a practical route for integrating metastable amorphous multimetal interfaces with electrode architectures.

title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
abstract:
Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH
                    3
                    ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.

title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
abstract:
The basal streptophyte
                    Mesostigma viride
                    represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the
                    M. viride
                    PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C
                    2
                    S
                    2
                    M
                    p2
                    L
                    p2
                    -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll
                    b
                    macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.

title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
abstract:
Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year
                    −1
                    during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface
abstract: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

title: Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
abstract:
The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca
                    2+
                    (Ca
                    v
                    2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the
                    Drosophila
                    neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca
                    v
                    2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

title: 4D‐Printed Intelligent Electromagnetic Materials for Adaptive Microwave Stealth and Multispectral Camouflage
abstract: ABSTRACT Increasingly complex and dynamic applications demand intelligent and adaptive electromagnetic (EM) stealth and multispectral camouflage materials with self‐perception, actuation, and regulation capabilities. However, currently available EM materials with predesigned structure and confined EM performances cannot satisfy the diverse dynamic requirements. Herein, we report a general strategy to engineer intelligent reconfigurable EM materials by encoding programmable structures into liquid crystal elastomers with functional coating by topological 4D printing. The stimulus‐response structural reconfiguration establishes distinct EM‐wave interaction regimes and expands the accessible design space for EM functions, enabling the adaptive modulation of EM characteristics and multispectral camouflage. The proposed hypothesis is validated by constructing different reconfigurable structures with versatile functions. For example, the Miura‐origami configuration undergoes spontaneous folding under external stimuli, delivering reversible and seamless modulation from total reflection to broadband absorption (4.49–18 GHz, −21.4 dB). Moreover, reversible and adaptive switching between signal transmission and electromagnetic interference shielding is also achieved via a flower‐shaped “quasi‐Faraday cage”. Combined with outer functional coatings, it affords multispectral camouflage in dynamic and complex environments. Therefore, this work offers a feasible and versatile design route to develop reliable and self‐adaptive microwave stealth and multispectral camouflage materials for next‐generation intelligent systems.

title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
abstract:
Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch
                    +
                    selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H
                    +
                    . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

title: Dynamics of excess renewable energy and implications for its potential use
abstract: Due to wind and solar variability, excess renewable energy could be available, even in systems with substantial storage. Across a wide range of possible systems, excesses typically occur in the afternoon and in spring and fall and persist for up to 7–12 h. Flexible technologies could be designed to utilize these excesses.

title: Plasmonic S‐Scheme Heterojunction‐Mediated Photocatalytic Cascade Reaction for Antibiotic Wastewater‐to‐Hydrocarbon Fuel Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic mineralization of organic pollutants has attracted considerable attention in antibiotic wastewater treatment. However, this process inevitably produces CO 2 , and the efficient treatment and utilization of this environmentally detrimental substance remain a major challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a photocatalytic cascade reaction on a well‐designed plasmonic S‐scheme heterojunction, where plasmonic W 18 O 49 acts as the oxidative photocatalyst for antibiotic mineralization into CO 2 , and amino‐rich g‐C 3 N 4 serves as the reductive photocatalyst to capture the as‐produced CO 2 and hydrogenate it into CO and CH 4 . This cascade reaction directly converts antibiotic‐contaminated wastewater into hydrocarbon fuels, thereby reducing CO 2 emissions. We show that visible‐NIR‐driven hot electrons in W 18 O 49 transfer to g‐C 3 N 4 to boost CO 2 hydrogenation, while the remaining holes sufficiently oxidize water into · OH. Upon simulated sunlight irradiation, this process enhances the cascade reaction activity. With 5 mg of the S‑scheme heterojunction under 2 h irradiation, ∼86% tetracycline was degraded, lowering the initial wastewater toxicity. The carbon conversion efficiencies for tetracycline‐to‐CO/CH 4 and mineralization‑derived CO 2 ‐to‐CO/CH 4 reached ∼0.60% and ∼2.68%, respectively. This work provides a promising strategy for integrating pollutant degradation with CO 2 valorization via rational design of high‐performance photocatalysts, advancing sustainable wastewater treatment and carbon neutrality.

title: Direct Visualization of Polarity‐Driven Carrier Redistribution in Two‐Dimensional In/CdS
abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic polarization field (IPF) in wurtzite semiconductors has long been proposed as a means to regulate carrier migration in photocatalytic and optoelectronic systems. However, direct experimental visualization of polarity‐driven charge separation remains challenging because intrinsic polarization effects are often obscured by competing surface fields and structural heterogeneity, leading to long‐standing contradictions between theory and experiment. Here, we fabricate well‐defined two‐dimensional In‐doped CdS single‐crystalline flakes (In/CdS) with exposed polar basal planes, providing a model platform to directly probe polarity‐driven carrier redistribution. Kelvin probe force microscopy, combined with photo‐deposition and single‐molecule fluorescence imaging, reveals opposite carrier accumulation on the two basal surfaces of individual flakes, with the upper surface serving as an electron‐rich reduction site and the bottom surface acting as a hole‐rich oxidation site. The spatially separated carrier distribution enables selective co‐catalyst loading on electron‐accumulated surfaces and boosts photocatalytic H 2 evolution. Ultrafast spectroscopy reveals a long lifetime (>2 µs) of photogenerated electrons and ultrafast electron transfer to co‐catalysts with an efficiency approaching unity. This work provides long‐sought experimental proof of charge separation in polar semiconductors and establishes a paradigm for exploiting intrinsic bulk properties through 2D geometry.

title: Three‐Dimensional Topological Spin Textures Above Room Temperature in NdCo 3 Magnet
abstract: ABSTRACT Recently, topological spin configurations, such as skyrmions, (anti)merons, and hopfions, have garnered attention because of their scientific importance and potential industrial applications. However, systematically investigating their three‐dimensional (3D) spatial arrangements is essential for understanding their external‐field responses and enabling their practical use. Such investigations remain challenging owing to technical limitations. Herein, we report a comprehensive investigation of the 3D spin configurations in the centrosymmetric rare‐earth magnet NdCo 3 , revealing spontaneous composite stripe‐(anti)merons and dipolar skyrmions across a broad temperature range of 256–378 K. We resolved the random chirality of the (anti)merons by integrating in situ Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (L‐TEM), off‐axis electron holography, neutron diffraction, and micromagnetic simulations, and quantified their finite penetration depths. Furthermore, the dipolar skyrmions were shown to possess depth‐dependent spin textures, evolving from Néel‐type magnetization at the surfaces to Bloch‐type rotation in the intermediate layers. Our results establish NdCo 3 as a robust platform for high‐temperature 3D topological spin textures in centrosymmetric magnets and provide a general experimental–theoretical framework for reconstructing and controlling 3D spin textures in other topological magnetic systems.

title: Drug‐Stiffened Polymer Worms: Allostery‐Inspired Activity Gating and Endogenous Enzyme‐Recharged Catalytic Cycling
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural enzymes achieve efficient and specific catalysis through precise allosteric regulation, a dynamic interplay of conformational rigidity and flexibility that remains largely unrealized in synthetic catalysts. Here, we report an allostery‐inspired polymer assembly whose catalytic and therapeutic functions are gated by programmable changes in supramolecular rigidity. The assemblies initially form flexible worm‐like micelles, whereas drug loading induces coordination‐driven crystallization into rigid nanorods. This rigidification restricts substrate accessibility and electron transfer, concurrently suppressing its peroxidase‐like activity, drug cytotoxicity, and fluorescence. In the glutathione (GSH)‐rich tumor microenvironment, disruption of metal coordination reverses rigidification, restores the flexible morphology, and reactivates all functions. The activated assemblies then use tumor‐overexpressed NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) as an endogenous redox partner, channeling reducing equivalents from reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) to replenish their electron reservoir and enable repeated catalytic turnover. This NQO1‐recharged cascade depletes intracellular GSH and NADH while generating cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals, thereby inducing apoptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis, triggering immunogenic cell death, and eliciting robust antitumor immunity in vivo. By integrating allostery‐inspired structure gating with endogenous‐enzyme‐driven catalyst recharging, this work establishes an adaptive catalytic platform that addresses limitations in the activity regulation and redox cycling of artificial enzymes and offers a strategy for catalytic cancer therapy.

title: Chain‐Regulated Degradation of Polyvinyl Chloride in UiO‐Type Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Converting polyvinyl chloride (PVC) into valuable hydrocarbons is hindered by rapid dehydrochlorination, which produces mainly coke and HCl and limits global recycling to below 8%. Existing strategies activate specific bonds but overlook chain regulation. Here we show that regulating PVC chains within the sub‐nanometer channels of UiO‐type metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) redirects degradation from uncontrolled elimination to size‐selective chain scission. In Zr‐based UiO‐66 and UiO‐67, periodic acidic Zr clusters anchor PVC through Zr─Cl bonds, inducing heterolytic C─Cl cleavage and β‐scission of carbocationic intermediates. The yield of volatile hydrocarbons increases from γ ): UiO‐66 ( γ = 8 C─C bonds) favours C9 hydrocarbons, whereas UiO‐67 ( γ = 10) favours C11 hydrocarbons. Molecular dynamics, thermodynamic calculations, and statistical kinetic modelling reveal that γ and carbocation‐mediated scission events control the carbon number of the products. This work establishes chain regulation as a design principle for controlling polymer degradation.

title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control
abstract:
Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the
                    NAT1
                    motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the
                    NAT1
                    motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of
                    NAT1
                    -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on‐body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio‐signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular‐level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device‐level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device‐level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of an SP without incorporating soft segments into the backbone. This strategy promotes conformational flexibility and suppresses side‐chain interdigitation, enhancing chain dynamics and amplifying mechanical contrast between crystalline and amorphous domains. This facilitates localized stress accommodation and induces the formation of nano‐to‐micro scale crack clusters, termed artificial stretch marks (ASMs), which emulate the adaptive mechanical behavior of human skin. Leveraging this mechanism, ISOSTs maintain 83.8% of maximum current even under 150% strain while preserving synaptic behaviors. Furthermore, physical reservoir computing using the ISOSTs preserves electromyography classification performance under 150% tensile strain. This work presents a biomimetic stress dissipation strategy for intrinsically stretchable and stress‐adaptive neuromorphic electronics.

title: Dynamic Interfacial S–O Bonding Stabilizes Oxygen Redox Through Reversible Electron Confinement
abstract: ABSTRACT The reversible activation of lattice oxygen represents a transformative opportunity for high‐energy battery electrodes but remains fundamentally limited by the instability of oxidized oxygen states. In layered oxide cathodes, oxygen oxidation generates oxygen‐centered hole states that become electronically unstable at particle surfaces, triggering oxygen loss, interfacial reconstruction, and irreversible electrochemical degradation. Here, we develop an interfacial electronic regulation strategy that stabilizes oxygen redox through reversible sulfur–oxygen (S–O) bonding. During charging, dynamic S–O bond formation at the cathode surface confines oxygen hole states and suppresses their delocalization and irreversible evolutions, whereas bond dissociation upon discharge restores the lattice oxygen electronic configuration and enables reversible oxygen redox. Applied to the Na 0.72 Li 0.24 Mn 0.76 O 2 layered oxide cathode, this strategy enables stable oxygen redox activity, mitigates voltage decay, and improves long‐term cycling stability. These findings establish reversible interfacial electron confinement as a general design principle for regulating unstable oxygen electronic states and advancing durable high‐energy‐storage materials.

title: Colloidal Photonic Crystals Toward Scalable Manufacturing and Reliable Functions
abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal photonic crystals (CPCs) have attracted considerable attention because of their specific optical properties and versatile structural functionality. While previous reviews have extensively covered the fundamental design and fabrication principles of functional CPCs, a systematic perspective on their transitioning from laboratory‐scale demonstrations to scalable manufacturing remains less explored. In this review, we therefore specifically fill this gap by summarizing recent advances on colloidal assembly, structural evolution, and stabilization strategies relevant to large‐scale fabrication and application‐oriented use. First, a concise overview of refining the classification of building blocks is provided for establishing a library to construct well‐defined periodic sophisticated photonic nanostructures. Second, we discuss scalable assembly from the perspective of processing constraints on how mild conditions, short assembly times, simplified procedures, and large‐area uniformity can be balanced. This is followed by discussing structural color modulation beyond stimulus‐based classification, and design strategies that enhance color fidelity, mechanical stability, and robustness. Emerging applications of these unique photonic systems, including anti‐counterfeiting, sensing, displays, and bio‐related devices, are highlighted. Finally, this review presents some challenges and perspectives on the development of colloid‐based scalable photonic materials, aiming to provide a scientific framework for bridging laboratory‐scale photonic materials with industrial‐scale manufacturing and reliable functions.

title: 2DIR hyperspectral imaging of polariton propagation reveals fewer dark modes per polariton
abstract: Change in chemical reactions under strong coupling with confined electromagnetic cavities has been previously experimentally observed. However, theoretically, the number of molecules per cavity mode is too high to explain the experiment. In this work, the authors experimentally measure this number, and find that it is much smaller than assumed, using 2DIR imaging and, thus, lay the foundation for better understanding polariton phenomena and future system design.

title: H-aggregated supramolecular packing lowers exciton binding energy for efficient quinone-phenol-mediated H2O2 photosynthesis
abstract: Controlling how molecules assemble provides a powerful route to regulate the fate of photoexcited states. H-type packing strengthens intermolecular electronic delocalization, weakens exciton binding, and promotes charge generation in perylene diimide (PDI) supramolecules, enabling efficient solar H2O2 photosynthesis. This work establishes supramolecular packing as a molecular design strategy for exciton management and solar-to-chemical energy conversion.

abstract: Photoenzymatic catalysis has enabled an increasingly diverse range of asymmetric radical transformations, yet phosphorus-centred radicals have remained beyond its reach. title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
abstract: ABSTRACT Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open‐shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron‐containing Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π‐conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol ‒1 . Despite their strong open‐shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half‐life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin‐stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone‐dependent aromaticity, tunable near‐infrared absorption, and reversible four‐electron redox behavior. Two‐electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed‐shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red‐shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron‐based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open‐shell materials.

title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO 2 offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO 2 pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters, N ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO 2 radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

title: Highly Efficient Organic Scintillators With Low Detection Limits via Cascade Energy Transfer in TADF‐Sensitized Fluorescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic scintillators have experienced notable advancements in performance, garnering considerable attention and demonstrating promising potential for diverse applications. However, an ideal scintillator requires efficient radiation absorption, rapid radiative decay, excellent stability, and a high light yield; it still remains challenging to simultaneously fulfill these criteria for a single organic material. Here, we propose to fabricate energy transfer cascade organic scintillators based on the TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (TSF) mechanism, in which the functions of x‐ray energy absorption, triplet exciton up‐conversion, and singlet exciton radiative transition are decoupled by three components cooperating to break through intrinsic shackles. As a result, a highlight output of 28.90 times that of anthracene crystal, a record detection limit as low as 17.69 nGy air s −1 , and an imaging resolution of 23.3 lp mm −1 were achieved. This work validates the universality and potential of the TSF mechanism to boost the performance of organic scintillators and is expected to advance the rapid development of organic scintillators.

title: Ribo@DNA: Ribonucleotides as Convenient Handles for Site‐Specific DNA Conjugation
abstract: ABSTRACT DNA conjugates are broadly enabling in biotechnology and medicine, yet methods for synthesizing many of these conjugates are often complex and expensive. Here we report the use of ribonucleotides locally incorporated within DNA oligonucleotides (ribo@DNA) as reactive handles for facile, high‐yield post‐synthesis conjugation in water. The site of reaction is the 2′‐OH group of the ribonucleotide, which is selectively nucleophilic in aqueous solution toward acyl, sulfonyl, and aryl electrophiles. Mass spectrometry data document that the reactions occur in moderate to high conversions with all four ribonucleotides, establishing sequence and positional versatility. Side products are chiefly the result of over‐modification in cases of highly reactive or bulky reagents (ca. 0%–15%). The crude modified oligodeoxynucleotide can be isolated by precipitation, or can be purified readily by high performance liquid chromatography. Examples are documented of incorporation of varied acyl groups with alkanoyl or aroyl structure, sulfonyl groups, aryl groups, clickable residues, fluorophores, and reversible groups. Conjugation reactions at 2′‐O with carboxylic acids, thiols, amines, aryl halides, and alcohols are demonstrated, resulting in broadly varied functional linkages including ethers, esters, carbamates, carbonates, and thiocarbonates. This strategy offers an inexpensive and exceptionally versatile alternative to nucleobase conjugates for modification of DNA.

title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
abstract: ABSTRACT External physical fields have emerged as promising tools for dynamically regulating electrocatalytic reactions, yet how different stimuli influence catalysis within structurally constrained active sites remains poorly understood. We establish structurally constrained Ni single‐atom‐anchored CdS as a model platform to investigate magnetic‐field modulation of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and its relationship to the photoresponse. Operando electrochemical measurements, quasi in situ spectroscopic characterizations, magnetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations reveal fundamentally distinct response pathways. The photo‐induced response is strongly potential‐dependent, with a clear photocurrent response at lower bias, but little additional current under strongly anodic OER conditions. In contrast, magnetic fields regulate the electronic structure of Ni active sites by modifying Ni 3d–S 3p orbital coupling and spin configurations, thereby reducing the free‐energy requirement for the potential‐determining *OH‐to‐*O conversion step without inducing significant changes in the coordination environment. Notably, the catalytic and spin responses observed under magneto‐optical conditions closely resemble those induced by magnetic fields alone, indicating that magnetic‐field‐driven spin regulation dominates OER kinetics in structurally constrained single‐atom active sites. This work demonstrates that different external fields access distinct electronic degrees of freedom and establishes a conceptual framework for external‐field‐regulated electrocatalysis beyond conventional structure‐based catalyst design.

title: Declining environmental predictability erodes reproduction in a tropical seabird
abstract: The authors show that, for a tropical seabird model species, winter–spring phytoplankton blooms kept a stable mean timing but became more variable between years. Breeding synchrony weakened and reproductive success declined and became less consistent over the same two decades.

title: Tuning Mass Transport through Pressure Modulation for Lithium-Mediated Nitrogen Reduction
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction (LiNRR) produces ammonia at ambient pressure and temperature, and gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) have advanced its production rate by intensifying nitrogen availability. However, the mass transport of lithium, nitrogen, and proton donor within the GDE and how the balance of their fluxes governs LiNRR performance remain underexplored. Here, we spatiotemporally varied the balance of species fluxes in a LiNRR GDE by dynamically modulating the pressure difference across the electrode, which altered the position of the gas/electrolyte interface. We found that decoupling the pressures applied during the plating and resting steps of pulsed electrolysis leads to higher ammonia production rates compared to the corresponding static pressure conditions. Decoupled pressure modulation enables even lithium plating during electrolysis and fast transport of nitrogen and proton donor during subsequent ammonia formation steps. This strategy may unlock a new design space for LiNRR by dynamically optimizing the reaction interface.

title: Transition from Dehydration to Rehydration of Chloride Salts near the Melting Point: Thermodynamic Origin and Implications for High-Temperature Corrosion
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molten chloride salts are promising functional media for high-temperature energy systems; however, trace water can accelerate corrosion of structural materials. We investigated changes in water concentration in six chloride salts—LiCl, NaCl, MgCl2, KCl, CaCl2, and ZnCl2—during heating across their solid-to-liquid phase transitions under a nominally inert Ar atmosphere. During solid-state heating, water concentration generally decreased, indicating dehydration. With further heating toward and through melting, however, this trend unexpectedly reversed in five salts except ZnCl2. As these salts entered the liquid phase, their water concentrations increased, marking a transition from dehydration to rehydration. Thermodynamic analysis showed that melting shifts the free energy balance toward water incorporation through enthalpic and entropic contributions. By comparing molten MgCl2 under conditions allowing or restricting entry of Ar gas, we identified trace water in the Ar atmosphere as the source of rehydration. Corrosion tests further showed rehydration substantially increased 316H stainless steel corrosion.

title: Donor–Acceptor Tuning Regulates Viologen Redox Behavior for Selective H2O2 Photosynthesis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Regulating redox-active electron acceptors offers a strategy for directing multielectron photocatalysis beyond conventional charge-separation engineering. Here, we demonstrate substituent-controlled viologen redox regulation in pyrene–viologen porous organic polymers (PyVio-X) for selective H2O2 photosynthesis. Carbonyl functionalization (PyVio-CO) enhances donor–acceptor interactions and charge separation, while facilitating photoinduced viologen radical (V-N+•) formation. PyVio-CO achieves an H2O2 production rate of 1786 μmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light and ambient air, with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.25% and an apparent quantum yield of 4.95%. Mechanistic investigations support sequential O2 reduction involving ·O2– and *OOH intermediates, mediated by reversible V-N2+/V-N+• redox cycling. Enhanced two-electron O2 reduction selectivity and suppressed H2O2 decomposition further promote H2O2 accumulation. This work establishes substituent-controlled redox mediation as a molecular design principle for selective multielectron photocatalysis.

title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre‐branching” strategy for high‐quality SAF production: C 2 ‐C 4 bio‐based vicinal diols convert into C 4 ‐C 6 branched alcohols over CuMgAlO x in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross‐aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in‐situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C 4 ‐C 6 alcohol intermediates into branched C 8 ‐C 16 alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C 4 ‐C 6 alcohols was achieved. In situ spectroscopy and 13 C isotope labeling reveal that Cu + /Cu 0 sites catalyze (de)hydrogenation, MgO promotes C─C coupling via cross‐aldol condensation, acidic AlO x sites induce 1,2‐alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst‐35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al 2 O 3 deliver an 83.3 C% toward C 8 ‐C 16 iso‐alkanes, affording a 64.9% overall carbon yield from ethylene glycol. Without post‐isomerization, the SAF features a ‐65°C freezing point and robust feedstock compatibility with crude biomass polyols. This work provides a new paradigm for controllable synthesis of high‐performance SAF from renewable bio‐diols.

title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing
abstract: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.
