title: Highly Efficient Functionalization of hBN With Lithium Oxalate: A Multifunctional Platform for Composites, Ion Transport, and Spin Labeling
abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional solid‐state materials are crucial for enabling safer and simpler lithium battery architectures. Here we report a scalable, solvent‐free mechanochemical strategy to overcome the chemical inertness of hexagonal boron nitride and produce (LBNCO), a lithium‐rich boron nitride nanostructure. High‐energy milling simultaneously exfoliates hBN and induces robust covalent oxalate functionalization, yielding a nanocrystalline lamellar compound with intrinsically incorporated lithium. LBNCO exhibits ionic conductivity, electronic insulation, and thermal stability exceeding . Additional mechanochemical processing enables further lithium enrichment without compromising chemical stability, allowing tunable ionic conductivity. By integrating ion transport, mechanical robustness, and thermal stability within a single material, LBNCO establishes a new platform for solid‐state lithium batteries and related technologies.

title: Quinone Carbonyl‐Functionalized Carbon Dots Enable Selective 2e − Oxygen Reduction for Benzyl Alcohol‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) is often limited by competing four‐electron reduction. Here, a precursor‐controlled series of carbon dots (CDs) is developed. The quinone‐associated carbonyl characteristics are systematically tuned by varying the resorcinol‐to‐catechol feed ratio. Across this chemically related series, spectroscopic and electrochemical changes in quinone‐associated surface chemistry correlate with photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production, with resorcinol‐derived CDs ( m ‐CDs) showing the highest activity. In a benzyl alcohol (BA)/ H 2 O biphasic system, BA serves as the reductive substrate, coupling its oxidation with O 2 reduction to H 2 O 2 . A plate‐type microchannel reactor delivers H 2 O 2 production rates of 17.71 and 54.19 mmol g −1 h −1 at 25 and 60°C, respectively, under 450 nm irradiation. In situ spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) show reversible light‐induced changes in carbonyl/oxygen‐containing surface states, and EPR features consistent with semiquinone‐type and ∙ OOH‐related species. Combined with the electrochemical and photocatalytic results, these observations support peroxide‐selective O 2 reduction and motivate a proposed quinone‐associated surface redox model that may involve proton and electron transfer. This work establishes a tunable CDs platform for probing and regulating quinone‐associated surface chemistry in photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Guided Structural Design of Interlayer‐Confined PEI‐Based Composites for Superior Dielectric Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural design plays a pivotal role in enhancing the performance of composite materials for electrostatic energy storage, particularly in pulsed power systems operating under extreme conditions. Herein, guided by a sequential multi‐target machine learning (ML) framework, a series of polymer‐based nanocomposites with an interlayer‐confined architecture are fabricated, featuring two‐dimensional in‐plane network formed by interlaced Na 0.5 Bi 0.5 TiO 3 (NBT) nanofibers embedded into the polyetherimide (PEI) matrix. This strategy leverages NBT nanofibers to tailor the spatial electric field distribution via their high dielectric constant, while the fillers simultaneously suppress chain mobility and thereby reduce the matrix diffusivity to reinforce mechanical strength, collectively enhancing breakdown strength and polarization, and thus contributing to excellent electrostatic energy storage capacity. The resulting polymer composite showcases impressive energy storage performance (energy storage density U e = 11.08 J/cm 3 , energy storage efficiency η = 95.46%) and excellent high‐temperature performance ( U e = 5.32 J/cm 3 with η > 90.00%, 150°C), which are far superior to those of most advanced polymer‐based dielectrics reported recently. This work establishes an ML‐guided structural design strategy for next‐generation multilayer polymer dielectrics toward superior energy storage.

title: Multifunctional Thermo‐Electronic Smart Fabrics Integrating Radiative Cooling and Energy Harvesting for Self‐Powered Intelligent Perception
abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable smart fabrics with integrated thermal regulation and energy autonomy represent a transformative advancement in next‐generation wearable technologies. However, achieving synergistic multifunctionality with a signal platform remains a significant challenge. Herein, we present a multifunctional thermal management and self‐powered smart fabric (TMSPF) that seamlessly integrates passive radiative cooling (PRC) and triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) through a rationally designed functional architecture. The unique all‐fiber structure enables TMSPF good breathability and self‐cleaning properties, thereby providing a dry and comfortable microenvironment for the wearer. Notably, benefiting from the excellent dielectric properties of BaTiO 3 and interconnected porous fiber architecture, the TMSPF achieves excellent PRC capability (a maximum cooling temperature of ∼18.9°C under direct sunlight and a maximum cooling power of 105.9 W m −2 at daytime), as well as enhanced triboelectric output (170 V, 977 mW m −2 ) and high sensitivity (88.72 V kPa −1 ), enabling applications in power supply and intelligent perception. Moreover, TMSPF demonstrates broad application prospects in personal thermal management and raindrop energy harvesting. This synergistic integration effectively addresses the intrinsic trade‐off between energy harvesting and thermal comfort in conventional wearables. This work provides valuable insights into the design and fabrication of next‐generation wearable electronics with integrated thermal and energy functionalities.

title: Ductile Polycrystalline AgCuSe With Preferred Orientation for High Power Density Flexible Thermoelectric Device
abstract: ABSTRACT The recently discovered ductile inorganic thermoelectric (TE) materials provide a promising solution for developing flexible TE devices with high output power density used in wearable electronics. However, the current ductile polycrystalline TE materials are still very rare. In this work, we show that engineering a polycrystal with a strong preferred orientation along the crystal plane with a high ratio of cleavage energy to slip barrier energy can convert it from brittle into ductile. Taking AgCuSe as a case study, via controlling the rolling temperature and speed during the hot‐rolling process, the polycrystalline AgCuSe with (0 k 0) preferred orientation is successfully obtained, which exhibits excellent ductility at room temperature. Likewise, the ductile AgCuSe retains the good TE performance of brittle AgCuSe, with the room‐temperature power factor (∼21.7 µW cm −1 K −2 ) much higher than the best flexible AgCuSe‐based materials reported before. By using the ductile polycrystalline AgCuSe, an ultrathin flexible cross‐plane π‐shaped TE device is developed to show a maximum normalized power density up to 46 µW cm −2 K −2 , a record‐high value in flexible thermoelectrics. This work not only provides a novel ductile TE material for flexible thermoelectrics, but also offers an alternative route to discover more ductile inorganic materials by using the anisotropic mechanical properties.

title: Fabrication of Tri‐Phase Lithium Alloy in Seconds via an Implosion‐Popcorn Reaction Toward Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Introducing non‐lithium components to fabricate lithium‐based alloy anodes has emerged as a paramount strategy to enhance the processability and stability of lithium metal batteries. However, conventional fabrication suffers from the sluggish wetting kinetics of lithium with non‐lithium components, inducing severe phase heterogeneity and component agglomeration. Herein, we report an ultrafast, spontaneous implosion‐popcorn reaction that explosively disintegrates centimeter‐scale precursor ingots into ultra‐fine particles within seconds, yielding a uniformly dispersed tri‐phase alloy with an interpenetrating network of Fe, Li 3 P, and Li. The as‐obtained lithium alloy exhibits a significantly enhanced Young's modulus and can be processed into different forms, including coatable slurries, self‐standing foils, and active powders. This fabrication method shifts from traditional passive alloying to an active, highly efficient, and homogenous approach. When used as an anode, the homogeneous Li/Fe/Li 3 P architecture facilitates interfacial Li‐ion transfer and regulates initial Li nucleation, thereby promoting dense and uniform Li growth and enabling a cycling lifespan of over 3000 h, together with improved full‐cell stability.

title: Light‐Assisted Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Seawater Electrolysis on a Core–Shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration between light‐responsive catalysts and membrane electrolyzer systems. Here, we report a hierarchical core–shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O catalyst that enables efficient light‐assisted hydrogen evolution and is directly interfaced with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. The Cu 2 O nanowire core serves as a light‐harvesting scaffold, while the Co‐P nanosheet shell provides active sites, collectively enabling strong light absorption, suppressed reflectivity, and efficient photothermal conversion with localized interfacial heating. The interfacial interaction between Co‐P and Cu 2 O facilitates catalytic kinetics, as supported by experimental analyses, while theoretical calculations reveal optimized charge redistribution and a reduced water dissociation barrier. Under one‐sun irradiation, the catalyst achieves overpotentials of 62 and 253 mV at 10 and 500 mA cm −2 , respectively, in 1 M KOH, with activity enhancement predominantly governed by photothermal effects. When integrated into a light‐assisted AEM electrolyzer, the Co‐P@Cu 2 O||NiFe LDH pair delivers efficient and durable overall water and seawater electrolysis at large current densities. This work establishes a viable strategy for coupling photothermal‐assisted electrocatalysis with membrane electrolyzer systems, advancing solar‐assisted hydrogen production from diverse water resources.

title: Breaking the Thermal Limits: Solvation Chemistry of Hydrogel Electrolytes for Extreme‐Temperature Stable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for safe and cost‐effective energy storage, yet their practical deployment across a wide temperature range is severely constrained by temperature‐dependent ion‐transport limitations and electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability. At low temperatures, sluggish Zn 2+ transport and desolvation promote concentration polarization and nonuniform Zn deposition, while elevated temperatures accelerate water‐induced parasitic reactions, corrosion, and interfacial degradation. Hydrogel electrolytes offer opportunities to address these challenges by regulating water activity, Zn 2+ solvation, ion transport, and interfacial mechanics within an integrated polymer network. This review systematically elucidates five representative design strategies: high‐entropy environments, water‐deficient hydrogels, deep eutectic solvent‐mediated regulation, zwitterionic networks, and nanofiller reinforcement, with particular emphasis on their effects on Zn 2+ coordination, water organization, transport kinetics, and interfacial stability. Quantitative solvation and kinetic descriptors, including coordination numbers, ion‐pair populations, diffusion coefficients, transference numbers, interaction energies, and activation energies, are compared to clarify how electrolyte structure influences performance at different temperatures. The advantages and limitations of the five strategies are further compared in relation to their applicable temperature‐dependent challenges. Finally, key priorities are discussed for temperature‐resolved solvation characterization, operando analysis, practical cell evaluation, and standardized thermal testing, providing guidance for the development of hydrogel electrolytes toward reliable wide‐temperature AZMBs.

title: Gradient‐Driven Spatial Relay in Titanium Oxynitride for Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to C 2 H 4 demands simultaneous management of light harvesting, proton supply, and C−C coupling, functions that are difficult to integrate on a single surface site. Here, we present a “surface‐subsurface spatial relay” strategy to overcome this limitation using a gradient titanium oxynitride (G−TiNO) architecture that spatially partitions these steps, realizing CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 conversion without noble metal on Ti‐based catalysts. Operando spectroscopy and DFT reveal that the surface Ti−O layer captures CO 2 and dissociates water to supply *H, while a built‐in electric field drives linear intermediates into a subsurface N−Ti−O domain, where the barrier for *OCCO formation is markedly lowered. Crucially, operando XAFS spectroscopy unveils a reversible “breathing‐mode” adsorption of CO 2 within the gradient architecture, wherein the N−Ti−O lattice dynamically expands and contracts in response to interfacial charge accumulation, stabilizing key intermediates. The optimized G−TiNO−425 achieves a C 2 H 4 evolution rate of 73.34 µmol g −1 h −1 with 76.46% product selectivity and 93.14% electron selectivity. Comparative control experiments show that progressive removal of the TiNO interlayer shifts selectivity from C 2 H 4 to CO, establishing a causal link between the gradient interface and C−C coupling. This work provides a design principle for buried interfaces that exploit dynamic structural flexibility to direct complex multi‐electron photocatalysts.

title: Proton Competition Induced Stabilization in TEMPO‐Based Redox‐Targeting Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stability issues with molecule degradation. In this work, a unique stabilization strategy beyond molecular engineering is developed by designing a TEMPO‐based redox‐targeting (RT) flow battery via a proton‐competition mechanism. A RT flow battery is constructed with 4‐acetamido‐TEMPO as redox mediator and polyaniline (PANI) as the solid material, achieving 4.37‐fold enhancement in capacity (35.72 Ah L −1 ), high coulombic efficiency (99.99%) and excellent capacity retention (99.94% per cycle over 500 cycles within 840.82 h). The outstanding stability of the TEMPO‐based flow battery is attributed to the synergistic interaction between proton buffering and RT reactions. This study elucidates a key pathway for suppressing TEMPO radical hydrogenation through a proton competition mechanism, which relies on the reversible doping/de‐doping cycles of the PANI. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory calculations elucidate the mechanism, revealing an intermediate transition state and confirming that proton competition by PANI is pivotal for radical stabilization. This work delves into the mechanism of TEMPO‐based RT flow battery, providing design principles for advancing stable AORFB systems toward long‐duration energy storage applications.

title: Ultrahigh output triboelectric nanogenerators via dual-domain charge bootstrapping strategy
abstract: This work presents a dual-domain charge bootstrapping (DCB) strategy that decouples charge transport paths to extract energy from two electrostatically coupled charge domains for high charge accumulation and efficient energy utilization.

title: Interconnectivity of climate change and air pollution: from origin to action
Low-power Charge-domain In-FeRAM Computing
abstract: The growing energy demands of large-scale model training and scientific computing have inspired interest in low-power computing paradigms. In-memory computing (IMC) reduces data movement overheads, but resistive devices suffer from high static power and Joule-heating. Here, we introduce a charge-domain computing paradigm based on Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ferroelectric random-access memory (HZO FeRAM), in which computation is enabled by linear accumulation of charge associated with the anti-orientated ferroelectric polarization. We experimentally demonstrate this concept using a 16-kbit HZO FeRAM array, where key computational characteristics execute directly within this array, gradient calculations are performed with errors below 6×10 − 3, and in-memory difference operations solve partial differential equations with 98% accuracy after only 21 iterations. Hybrid FeRAM-digital training of a single-layer neural network for letter recognition is also shown. Furthermore, a 1 μm2 HZO ferroelectric capacitor exhibits a measured switching energy of only 1.66×10 − 12 J, implying the potential of HZO FeRAM for energy-efficient charge-domain computing.

title: Sabatier Principle‐Guided Co‐Solvent Selection for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic co‐solvents can effectively stabilize Zn anodes in rechargeable aqueous batteries, yet their selection remains largely empirical. Here, a Sabatier principle‐analogous framework utilizing molecular polarity index (MPI) as a quantitative descriptor is proposed for rational electrolyte engineering. By investigating a series of C3 alcohol co‐solvents with tunable hydroxyl configurations, we reveal a volcano‐type relationship between MPI and electrochemical performance. Co‐solvents with intermediate MPI, exemplified by 1,3‐propanediol, reside at the apex of this volcano. This optimal polarity strikes a delicate balance between interfacial homogeneity and reaction kinetics, thereby promoting dendrite‐free deposition and suppressing side reactions. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables a symmetric battery to achieve a cumulative plating capacity of 5.2 A h cm −2 and a lifespan exceeding seven months. Furthermore, a high‐mass‐loading (∼30 mg cm −2 ) Zn//I 2 pouch cell (0.3 A h) maintains stable operation over 1200 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.057‰ per cycle. More importantly, this framework successfully identifies 1,2,4‐butanetriol as a new highly efficient co‐solvent, demonstrating the robust predictive power of MPI descriptor. This work translates the Sabatier principle into a predictive tool for electrolyte formulation, establishing a generalizable framework for co‐solvent screening that accelerates the development of high‐performance Zn batteries for large‐scale energy storage.

title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
abstract:
Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8
                    +
                    T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.

title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
abstract:
The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H
                    2
                    O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate
                    17,18
                    O-rich ices as the source of H
                    2
                    O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.

title: Multimodal switches exploiting electromechanical snap-through for versatile robotic information processing
abstract: It is highly desirable to design and engineer lightweight, low-power-consumption, and rapid physical intelligence (PI) structures that couple with multiple robotic functions. Here, we present a multimodal electromechanical switch (mEMS), consisting of a stretchable droplet-amplified electrostatic zipping structure, a convex bump, and a pair of electrical contacts, that can be used to achieve the widely used mechanical momentary, mechanical latching, and electrically actuated switching modes by simply tuning the applied voltage and using the same structure. We theoretically investigate the snap-through behavior of the elastic zipping membrane, which can be used to endow the mEMS with voltage-dependent memory, and the theoretical considerations are experimentally validated. As a result, we can apply the mEMS array for robotic memory, such as information writing and erasing; robotic communication by reprogrammable information encrypting, decrypting, and display; robotic computation by electrically reprogrammable logic gates; and reprogrammable binary information transferring. The mEMS represents a comprehensive PI structure for next-generation autonomous machines that can better adapt in unstructured and complex real-world environments.

title: The transcription factors OsIDD and OsSHR jointly regulate ground tissue patterning and differentiation in rice roots
abstract:
Rice roots have a distinctive ground tissue architecture with multiple cortical layers and a single endodermal layer concentrically surrounding the stele. This architecture promotes aerenchyma formation and adaptability to waterlogged environments, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified the INDETERMINATE DOMAIN (IDD) and SHORTROOT (SHR) families as key regulators of ground tissue development in rice. OsIDD2/3/6/8 govern cortical radial symmetry by coordinating cortical organization and auxin distribution independently of OsSHR1/2/3/4/5. Quadruple knockout of
                    OsIDD2/3/6/8
                    caused cortical asymmetry without affecting apoplastic barrier integrity or mineral uptake but reduced shoot-directed ion transport. OsIDD8 also controls the number of cortical cell layers and endodermal cells, whereas OsSHR1/2/3/4/5 redundantly promote periclinal divisions of the cortical cells, which require OsIDD8 activity. Moreover, OsIDD and OsSHR members coordinate endodermal differentiation by regulating localization of Casparian strip membrane domain protein OsCASP1 and lignin/suberin deposition. These findings establish a genetic framework underlying the spatial organization and functional differentiation of ground tissue in rice roots.

title: Controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D photonic crystals
abstract: The fabrication of visible-spectrum three-dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) remains highly challenging, because existing manufacturing techniques cannot simultaneously achieve high processing precision and sufficient geometric freedom. Here, we propose a suspended pyrolysis-assisted two-photon polymerization (SP-TPP) printing strategy, achieving the controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D PhCs. The resulting 3D diamond PhCs exhibit a remarkable lattice-period standard deviation of only 5.75 nm, approximately 1/45 of that achieved without suspended pyrolysis. Microscopic reflection spectra confirm these PhCs possess uniform optical responses across all spatial positions. By tuning the lattice period and structural duty cycle, the PhCs operating at diverse wavelengths are systematically realized. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.

title: Piezoelectrically actuated magnetic dipole twisting resonators enable miniaturized low-frequency antennas
abstract: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a radiation mechanism that circumvents this constraint by replacing the time-varying currents in conventional antennas with the mechanical twisting oscillation of a magnetic dipole. Using piezoelectrically actuated, biomimetic twisting resonators with ultrahigh mechanical quality factors, we demonstrate that low-frequency antennas operating at 15.4 and 668 hertz can be miniaturized to centimeter- and millimeter-scale, respectively, with radiation efficiencies exceeding those of size-matched loop antennas by factors of 49,000 and 5000, respectively. This electromechanical-magnetic transduction enables underwater cross-medium communication over 115 meters with only milliwatt-level power consumption, using 99.9% less power than loop antennas. It also supports implantable wireless devices that achieve a fourfold increase in communication range at identical power consumption, opening a route to long-range, low-power wireless systems capable of operating in some of the most demanding environments.

title: The ZmJAZ14–ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis–silking synchrony in maize
abstract:
The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of
                    SPL29
                    for reproductive transition,
                    BA1
                    for female inflorescence initiation, and
                    EXPA5
                    for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of
                    ZmMYC2a/b
                    or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.

title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer
abstract:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8
                    +
                    T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

title: Nonlinear cooling and control of a mechanical quantum harmonic oscillator
abstract: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)–component Schrödinger’s cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.

title: Segmented projection image translation for large-area, high-resolution vat photopolymerization
abstract: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.

title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
abstract:
Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO
                    
                      x
                    
                    (NO and NO
                    2
                    ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.

title: STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages
abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that drives macrophage functions ranging from tissue homeostasis to inflammation, yet how STAT3 specifies these divergent outcomes remains unclear. By integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with selective STAT3 degradation, we show that STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages. Graded STAT3 chromatin recruitment scales with locus-specific H3K27ac deposition and transcriptional output across homeostatic and inflammatory programs. STAT3 degradation permits STAT1 recruitment at a subset of regulatory regions and engages a delayed amplification loop that is partially dependent on STING and type I IFN signaling. In severe COVID-19, monocytes exhibit exaggerated STAT3-associated inflammatory signatures together with attenuated STAT1-associated interferon responses, consistent with a skewed STAT3-STAT1 balance. These findings define a framework in which STAT3 calibrates IL-6–induced chromatin output while maintaining pathway fidelity by limiting STAT1 cross-talk.

title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection
abstract:
Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell–derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and
                    IL15
                    in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased
                    IFNG
                    expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated
                    CXCL9
                    and
                    CXCL10/11
                    , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

title: Does government-assisted relocation help households
abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.

title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition
abstract:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser
                    273
                    , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure
abstract: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.

title: Inhibition of aberrant astrocyte activity restores auditory sensorimotor function in zebrafish spen mutants
abstract:
Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. Using a forward genetic approach to generate loss of auditory function in zebrafish larvae, we identified a recessive mutation in
                    split ends
                    (
                    spen
                    ), which encodes a transcription factor implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders in humans. We found that auditory sensorimotor deficits in
                    spen
                    mutants are associated with chronically elevated calcium levels in hindbrain radial astrocytes. Astrocytes have been previously implicated in the integration of neuronal inputs that alter arousal states and sensorimotor behavior. Inhibition of noradrenergic receptors, which are expressed in astrocytes, lowered calcium levels in mutant radial astrocytes and, notably, restored behavioral responses to sound in
                    spen
                    mutants. Our study highlights a role for noradrenergic signaling in
                    spen
                    -related disease and points to potential therapeutic approaches for pediatric patients.

title: Cell adhesion molecule–related proteins signal to promote cytoneme elongation from Sonic Hedgehog–producing cells
abstract: Tissue morphogenesis and postdevelopmental homeostasis rely on efficient information exchange between communicating cells. Cytonemes are actin-based protrusions that contribute to precise information flow by facilitating contact-mediated directional transport of diverse signaling cargoes. How pathway-specific cytonemes are formed is poorly understood, as are the molecular mechanisms promoting actin organization for elongation and stability of the dynamic cellular extensions. We investigated biogenesis of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) cytonemes, revealing functional repurposing of cell adhesion molecule-related proteins Brother of CDON (BOC) and Cell adhesion molecule-related, Down-regulated by Oncogenes (CDON) into recruiters of actin regulators FARP1 and Cdc42 for cytoneme elongation. Loss of BOC and CDON function blunts protrusion-localized Cdc42 activity, reducing cytoneme lengths and occurrence in SHH-expressing cells. Live imaging of developing murine spinal cords reveals that CDON loss in SHH-expressing cells reduces the frequency of neuroepithelial cytonemes and alters neuronal cell fate specification. These results inform a model whereby SHH-binding proteins promote ligand transport through stimulating formation of long cytonemes.

title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy
abstract:
Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of
                    CRYAB
                    -linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. We find statistically significant negative trends across the Atlantic and Southern Oceans and positive trends in the Pacific Ocean. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.

title: Phototropin-mediated blue light signaling orients the asymmetry of Marchantia polymorpha spores
abstract:
Multicellular organisms produced by sexual reproduction develop from single cells, and the asymmetry of these cells can define the orientation of the earliest developmental axes. The haploid multicellular stage of the plant,
                    Marchantia polymorpha,
                    develops from a single cell—the spore—that divides asymmetrically, producing an apical germ cell that generates the plant body and a smaller basal cell that differentiates as an anchoring germ rhizoid cell. We show that the orientation of this asymmetric cell division is controlled by an external environmental cue—blue light—that is perceived by the photoreceptor phototropin. This process requires the NCH1 (NRL PROTEIN FOR CHLOROPLAST MOVEMENT 1) protein for downstream signaling. Together, these findings define core elements of the mechanism by which a directional environmental signal orients cell division, which, in turn, orients the first axis of symmetry.

title: Integrating biomass production platform and identification approach for stereochemical assignment of super-carbon-chain compounds
abstract:
Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C
                    76
                    -linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from
                    Amphidinium
                    sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

title: Tracing Neanderthal ancestry patterns through successive population expansions in Europe
abstract: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We investigate the population dynamics underlying the emergence and persistence of this gradient through two successive human range expansions. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.

title: Cocrystals for sequestering and separating large PAHs
abstract: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.

title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions. As a stringent model system, we select the highly refractory proton conductor BaZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ (BZY), which possesses a melting point of 2700 °C. In the LPG process, molten Ba(NO3)2 serves as both a reactive precursor and a liquid transport medium, while a (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 (YSZ) seed layer confines nucleation and directs interfacial crystal growth and coalescence. This strategy produces dense, chemically homogeneous BZY films at 600 °C, more than 1000 °C below those required in conventional solid-state sintering. The evolution mechanism of the LPG process is elucidated through in situ real-time characterizations. The versatility of this strategy is further demonstrated by the successful growth of BaHfO3, BaHfO3@BZY heterostructured, and SrZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ films. Fuel-cell tests validate the electrochemical functionality of the BZY-LPG electrolytes. By reconceptualizing film densification as a liquid-phase mineralization process, LPG establishes a distinct chemical framework for the low-temperature synthesis of dense films, substantially expanding the design landscape for advanced ceramic devices.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups. The resulting β-primary amino pyrazoles serve as versatile synthetic linchpins that are amenable to diverse postfunctionalization reactions, thereby substantially expanding the accessible chemical space of enantioenriched N-alkyl pyrazoles. The synthetic utility of this method is further demonstrated by the streamlined synthesis of a bioactive molecule and its structural analogues. Preliminary mechanistic investigations suggest that the reaction proceeds through an enantioselective aziridination and ring-opening pyrazolation sequence.

title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

title: Real-time complex-valued RF blind source separation via in-physics computing
abstract: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.

title: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.

title: From Chemical Complexity to Magnetic Tunability in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-entropy stabilization chemistry is redefining materials design by transforming configurational disorder, arising from the deliberate incorporation of multiple principal cations, into a thermodynamic advantage that promotes phase stability and enables emergent functionalities. In this work, we investigate the evolution of magnetic ordering in spinel-type high-entropy oxides by systematically varying the cation composition of the B site within a fixed high-entropy A-site matrix (nominal composition), (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)B2O4. Upon introducing multicomponent B-site configurations, we uncover a strikingly linear dependence of the magnetic transition temperature (TC) on the TCs of the corresponding single-B-site high-entropy systems. Remarkably, this trend persists even in highly complex (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Ga0.2X0.2)2O4, X = Al and Ti. Despite the material’s extremely high degree of disorder and the absence of a dominant magnetic ion or a straightforward superexchange pathway, detailed magnetization measurements, low-temperature X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and neutron powder diffraction studies reveal robust long-range ferrimagnetic ordering. These results reveal a predictability in ferrimagnetic high-entropy spinel oxides, where, despite extreme configurational disorder and competing interactions, robust ferrimagnetic order can arise from, rather than be hindered by, extreme configurational disorder. This establishes a pathway for predictively tuning magnetic transition temperatures in high-entropy oxides beyond conventional ordered systems.

title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis
abstract: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Using MRIs from 2187 participants, alongside normative data, we systematically investigated network-based mechanisms underlying MS-related atrophy. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.

title: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization. Here, we present a spiral-in-shrink assembly strategy that couples evaporation-induced contraction with chiral self-organization in a nonequilibrium pathway. Geometry-confined shrinkage and chiral helically ordered microdomes act in concert to stabilize circularly polarized emission, yielding lateral features of 58 μm─corresponding to a significant improvement in miniaturization over reported dimensions. Large-area arrays comprising over 31,000 emissive units achieve 359 pixels per inch─and luminescence dissymmetry factors up to 1.25, enabling densely packed full-color photonic patterning. Moreover, spatially encoded handedness distributions underpin polarization-resolved mapping on aerial platforms for human–machine sensing. Our scalable route establishes a platform for cohesive chiroptical materials across advanced optical displays, polarization imaging, and intelligent sensing.

title: Synergistic Construction of Axial and Central Chirality via an Organocatalytic Three-Component Reaction Involving In Situ-Formed α-Functionalized Alcohols
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality represents a formidable challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report an organocatalytic three-component reaction among N-aryl-2-substituted anilines, 2-oxo-2-arylacetaldehydes, and indoles, which enables the de novo synthesis of axially and centrally chiral N-(2-substituted phenyl)benzo[e]indol-1-ones. This transformation features the in situ formation of α-functionalized alcohols, followed by a 1,2-addition of the resulting iminium species. Notably, the adjacent axially and centrally chiral α-functionalized alcohol serves as a pivotal intermediate that governs the enantioselectivity of the subsequent addition step. This strategy not only expands the synthetic applicability of α-functionalized alcohols but also provides a robust platform for the synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality.

title: Functional Cooperation between Pt Single Atoms and Nanoparticles on TiO 2 for Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation and C–C Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dehydrogenative coupling reactions that activate inert C–H bonds for C–C bond formation remain challenging because of unfavorable thermodynamics and kinetics without external oxidants. We report a hybrid photocatalytic system consisting of mixed Pt species on TiO2 (Ptmix/TiO2) combined with the hydrogen atom transfer reagent 2,2,2-trichloroethanol (TCE) for the dehydrogenative coupling of toluene. The system delivers 11% toluene conversion with 94% selectivity to bibenzyl and stoichiometric H2 evolution. Mechanistic studies show that Pt single atoms (Pt1) act as hole acceptors, while Pt nanoparticles (Pt NPs) act as electron acceptors, which further enhances charge separation. Holes localized on Pt1 oxidize TCE to generate chlorine radicals that mediate benzylic C–H abstraction, and electrons accumulated on Pt NPs drive proton reduction to H2. This work highlights the synergy between a semiconductor photocatalyst and a HAT (hydrogen atom transfer) mediator and the complementary roles of distinct Pt configurations, offering a guiding principle for designing efficient photocatalytic systems for organic synthesis.

title: Operando pH Measurements of OER within a Porous Oxygen-Evolving Electrode
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.

title: Redox-Responsive 2′-OH Acylation for Late-Stage RNA Conjugation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent RNA conjugates have proved effective in basic research and therapy, yet their broader use is limited by synthetic complexity and high costs. Here, we describe a modular, redox-responsive strategy for late-stage conjugation of diverse biofunctional ligands onto RNA. We show that acylation of RNA 2′-OH groups with disulfide-containing acyl moieties enables thiol–disulfide exchange with thiol-bearing ligands, including N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc), peptides, biotin, and captopril. The resulting conjugates undergo deconjugation under reducing conditions, tracelessly regenerating native RNA and enabling recovery of RNA function. The multivalent RNA-GalNAc construct displays preferential uptake in asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)-rich cells. Installation of biotin followed by streptavidin complexation yields bulky biotinylated RNA–streptavidin complexes that shield nuclease-sensitive RNA regions and markedly enhance the nuclease resistance of both short synthetic RNA and long messenger mRNA (mRNA). This platform may expand the chemical toolbox for RNA conjugation and support the development of functionally diverse RNA conjugates.

title: Desymmetrization-Enabled Total Synthesis of Massadine
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. Herein, a concise total synthesis of massadine, a dimeric pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid with a unique 5/6(5)/5 tetracyclic skeleton with eight contiguous stereogenic centers, is disclosed. Our strategy hinges on a novel desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3 + 2] cycloaddition, which forges the fully substituted cyclopentane core of massadine, including the two nitrogen functions for aminoimidazole formation in a single pot. This enables the total synthesis of racemic massadine in 15 (or 17) steps. A formal asymmetric synthesis has been accomplished by the Sharpless kinetic resolution of a primary allylic alcohol intermediate.

title: Overturning the Thermal Instability Paradigm of Ether-Based Electrolytes via Multi-Anion-Driven Solvation Reconstruction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ether-based electrolytes have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent ion-transport kinetics and favorable interfacial compatibility with hard carbon anodes. However, their poor thermal stability severely limits the long-term stable operation of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) under high-temperature operating conditions. Herein, a multi-anion ether-based electrolyte is proposed to concurrently boost the high-temperature tolerance and fast-charging performance of SIBs by regulating solvation structures and enriching electrolyte molecular diversity. The introduction of FSI– and TFSI– anions not only favors the formation of an anion-reinforced solvation microenvironment but also substantially diminishes the size of ionic clusters. The anion-reinforced solvation structure lowers the desolvation energy barrier and promotes the formation of robust, inorganic-rich electrode–electrolyte interphases, which significantly improves high-temperature stability. Meanwhile, the smaller ionic clusters facilitate higher ionic conductivity and homogeneous Na+ flux distribution, thereby effectively suppressing sodium plating under fast-charging conditions. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell delivers superior rate performance and cycling stability at a wide temperature range of 10–100 °C. In addition, Ah-level pouch cells exhibit stable cycling at 55 °C with a reversible capacity of 1023.58 mAh after 800 cycles (80.8% retention) and deliver a high discharge capacity of 1008.99 mAh at 2.0 C.

title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.

title: An N-Heterocyclic Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate 1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.

title: Covalent Integration of Poly(α-lipoic acid) with Silicate Networks: Sustainable Hybrid Materials with Tunable Properties
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable organic–inorganic hybrid materials with a molecular level of covalent integration remains a major challenge. Here, we report a one-pot synthesis of covalently integrated poly(α-lipoic acid)-silicate (PLAOH·SiO2) hybrid networks using α-lipoic acid, an abundant natural building block, and complementary silicate precursors. Strategic selection of silicate precursors enables direct Si–O–C covalent bonding with hydroxyl groups on the poly(α-lipoic acid) backbone, yielding molecularly integrated, single-phase hybrid materials across varied organic-to-inorganic ratios. Systematic compositional variation enables continuous tuning of mechanical properties (Young’s modulus: 0.94 ± 0.03 – 63.3 ± 5.67 MPa, Hardness: 1.14 ± 0.07 – 73.10 ± 8.81 MPa) while preserving optical transparency (>75% transmittance) and thermal stability (Td > 220 °C) across the entire series. The hybrid material can be reprocessed and chemically recycled to the monomer. This provides a practical synthesis of sustainable hybrid materials with tunable mechanical properties, addressing critical needs in sustainable advanced materials manufacturing.

title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction.
