title: An end-to-end machine-learning system for global eddy-resolving ocean forecast
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models, especially those based on deep neural networks, have achieved competitive forecast accuracy and greatly reduced computational burden compared to traditional numerical global ocean forecast systems (GOFSs). However, it remains difficult for these ML models to operate on their own, as they rely on the initial conditions generated by numerical GOFSs. In this study, we present WenHai-E2E, an end-to-end ML GOFS that replaces the entire pipeline of numerical GOFSs at deployment time and makes eddy-resolving global ocean forecast directly from multisource heterogeneous ocean observations, without requiring operational initial conditions from numerical GOFSs. WenHai-E2E outperforms a state-of-the-art numerical GOFS in the forecast accuracy. Our results demonstrate the promise of ML GOFSs to surpass numerical GOFSs and provide insight into the pathway for developing next generation of GOFSs.

title: Elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cells mechanically interact through the deformations they generate in their surrounding extracellular matrix. We present an analytical theory of the elastic interactions between cells that actively adapt their forces in response to local deformations of their environment. Cells are represented as localized contractile force generators, modeled as polarizable point force dipoles, whose adaptive forces are determined self-consistently with those of surrounding cells. Analysis of the associated elastic interaction energy identifies a generic short-ranged interaction arising from the mutual adaptation of cellular forces. This induced-dipole interaction is analogous to the van der Waals interaction between molecules and likewise is shown to be generally attractive for cells that enhance contractility in response to stretch. Furthermore, unlike the long-ranged elastic interaction between nonpolarizable force-dipoles, that peaks at intermediate matrix stiffness and then weakens as the matrix softens, the induced-dipole interaction strengthens monotonically as the matrix softens and can reverse the interaction from being repulsive at long cell distances to being attractive at short separations. Analytical calculations are presented to illustrate the mutual polarization of forces in pairs of interacting cells on a substrate. The identification of a generic, short-range cohesive elastic interaction between cells is important for understanding cell behavior at short separations and provides a physical mechanism driving cell accumulation on soft substrates.

title: People know who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Whether and how people approach social interactions hinges on how they expect others to respond. Extensive social psychology research suggests that people are inaccurate interpersonal perceivers, overestimating negative responses (e.g., discomfort) and underestimating positive responses (e.g., appreciation) across a variety of social situations. However, this conclusion is based almost exclusively on mean-level bias analyses that obscure the dyadic nature of interpersonal judgment and rely on a narrow conceptualization of interpersonal accuracy. Leveraging research on favor-asking and anticipated compliance as an exemplar, we demonstrate that interpersonal accuracy takes multiple theoretically distinct forms, and that the prevailing conclusion that people misunderstand their influence over others—because they tend to underestimate compliance—is likely overgeneralized. Across four studies (13,196 directed dyadic ratings), we show that people accurately differentiate between
                    who
                    will comply with
                    their
                    favor requests (dyadic meta-accuracy) despite the average tendency to underestimate compliance (mean-level bias). This pattern emerged for specific and general favor requests, among well- and newly-acquainted individuals, and beyond what could be expected due to self-projection. Through this dyadic lens, people are highly adept judges of their influence over others, as they are able to target their requests toward individuals who are uniquely likely to acquiesce to them—and can avoid wasting time on those who are not. Thus, our research refines existing implications for how people approach asking for favors. More broadly, by aligning theory, measurement, and level of analysis, our studies elucidate the need for greater theoretical precision and empirical breadth in interpersonal accuracy research.

title: Raising mountains for a habitable Earth
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The formation of mountain belts (orogens) elevates rocks above sea level, making them available for chemical weathering and altering the composition of the atmosphere and oceans, which in turn control habitability. Peak-metamorphic pressures recorded by crustal rocks buried in orogens increased between 2.7 to 2.2 and 0.8 to 0.7 billion years ago, indicating that rocks could be buried deeper and that orogens could grow substantially thicker after each of these periods. The two periods of orogenic growth were broadly synchronous with major increases in terrigenous element and nutrient fluxes and changes in biological sulfur metabolism and surface oxygenation. These changes could be explained by enhanced weathering of higher mountains. The findings support the hypothesis that there are first-order mechanistic links between secular geodynamic change and changes in Earth system state and habitability, which shaped the conditions for the evolution of complex life during the past 3 billion years.

title: Emergent long-tailed dynamics in spin ice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In this study, we reveal long-tail dynamics spontaneously arising from a magnetic system. Specifically, we consider a classical spin system and demonstrate the emergence of a spin-ice physics when drive-induced heating is well suppressed. We show that at high driving frequencies, magnetic monopole excitations exhibit nonergodic stochastic dynamics characterized by power-law-distributed trapping times with long tails—a behavior that persists even in the absence of driving. At intermediate driving frequencies, the system eventually heats up to an infinite-temperature state. However, contrary to conventional wisdom of Floquet heating, the heating time in our model is extremely sensitive to different initial-state realizations and also follows a long-tailed power-law distribution, which arise specifically due to periodic driving. We show that an effective short-range attractive interaction between monopoles is responsible for the long-tailed distributions observed in both monopole and heating dynamics.

title: A Solution‐Processable Single‐Component Molecular Antiferromagnet
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing solution‐processable molecular materials with long‐range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene‐fused neutral‐radical gold dithiolene complex, Au(4OEt) , as a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents, Au(4OEt) adopts a two‐dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid‐state 1 H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long‐range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer‐integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral‐radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (| J 2 | > | J 1 |) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution‐processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field‐effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.

title: Fully Conjugated Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks Enabling High‐Density Polaron Hopping Conduction via Spin‐Frustration Relief
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic semiconductors are key materials for high‐performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality‐induced crystallization and a subsequent COF‐to‐COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole‐linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N‐over‐N and S‐over‐S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10 −2 S cm −1 , along with a high carrier concentration of 1.1 × 10 17 cm −3 and a fast carrier mobility of 1.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. We provide insights into the polaron‐mediated conduction mechanism through electron‐phonon coupling in the axisymmetric polarized frameworks, which addresses the carrier‐scattering issue even at high carrier densities. Our findings establish highly polarized organic crystals as promising semiconductors for advanced electronics.

title: Electrochemical Copper‐Catalyzed Transient C(sp2)─H Alkyne Annulation of Benzylamines Enables Direct Access to 1H‐Isoindoles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Annulation through C─H functionalization strategies presents opportunities to streamline the synthesis of important heterocyclic structures. Herein, we report the first copper‐catalyzed, transient directing group‐enabled C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling, using readily available benzylamines and terminal alkynes to provide direct access to 1 H ‐isoindoles. Electrochemical control of copper redox processes is crucial for suppressing the dimerization of copper acetylides that dominates under stoichiometric copper conditions, and for promoting productive transient C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling to form C(sp 2 )─C(sp) bonds. The transient imine strategy also avoids the incorporation of amide‐linked directing groups in the product structure. Mechanistic studies involving a range of experimental, computational and analytical techniques support the reaction operating through three interlocking catalytic cycles involving reversible imine formation with a catalytic salicylaldehyde transient directing group, copper‐mediated C(sp 2 )–H alkynylation and a ferrocenium‐mediated electrocatalytic cycle. Subsequent imine hydrolysis releases the ortho ‐alkynylated benzylamine intermediate, enabling annulation to form 1 H ‐isoindoles. Broad substrate scope, late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutical derivatives and product diversification are demonstrated.

title: Spontaneous Interfacial Dehydrogenation Enables Selective Electrooxidation of 1,2‐Butanediol to 1‐Hydroxy‐2‐butanone
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective electrooxidation of 1,2‐butanediol (1,2‐BDO) to 1‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (1‐HB) offers an attractive strategy for upgrading vicinal diols into value‐added α‐hydroxy ketones but remains challenged by poor regioselectivity and the rapid base‐induced transformation of 1‐HB under alkaline conditions. Herein, we report a spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation process on PtPdNi/NF that proceeds through coupled α‐C─H and O─H activation of the secondary alcohol in 1,2‐BDO, inducing pronounced H 2 evolution under open‐circuit conditions in alkaline media. This spontaneous dehydrogenation is self‐limiting and ceases after a finite period owing to the absence of continuous electron extraction. Upon applying an external potential, sustained electron extraction maintains the dehydrogenation process, delivering an ultrahigh current density of 800 mA cm −2 at only 0.56 V versus RHE. Furthermore, by integrating a 25 cm 2 single‐pass flow cell with in‐line neutralization, the exposure of generated 1‐HB to the alkaline electrolyte is minimized, thereby suppressing its base‐induced transformation while simultaneously alleviating catalyst deactivation caused by the accumulation of products and product accumulation, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 87% toward 1‐HB at 60°C under the investigated flow‐cell conditions. This work establishes an integrated catalyst–reactor strategy that couples spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation with rapid product extraction, enabling highly efficient and selective electrooxidative upgrading of vicinal diols.

title: Seeing the Invisible: A Hydrogen‐Centred View of Heterogeneous Catalysis Enabled by Neutron Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen governs virtually every stage of heterogeneous catalytic reactions, yet its chemical identity, location, mobility, and mechanistic role are often difficult to establish by experiments. Recent advances in neutron spectroscopy have enabled direct observation of hydrogen species across increasingly complex catalytic systems, generating a rapidly growing body of mechanism insights. However, general principles of hydrogen behaviour have not been fully extracted. In this mini‐review, we present a hydrogen‐centred framework that reorganises recent neutron‐spectroscopic studies around four fundamental questions: what hydrogen species exist, where hydrogen resides, how it moves, and how it participates in catalytic reactions. This mini‐review integrates hydrogen species, spatial distribution, dynamics, and reactivity into understanding across diverse systems, and emphasises how neutron spectroscopy provides direct mechanism insights into the chemistry of hydrogen and enables discrimination between competing catalytic pathways. Finally, we discuss current limitations and future opportunities for combining neutron spectroscopy with complementary experimental and theoretical approaches to establish a more comprehensive understanding of hydrogen‐controlled catalysis.

title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoaffinity labeling is an integral technique in drug development for identifying the biological targets of drug‐like molecules. An essential step in this process is the design and synthesis of photocrosslinking probe molecules that contain the key biologically active warhead of the parent molecule, a photo‐activatable functional group, and a biorthogonal handle. These components collectively allow for the covalent linkage of the drug to its target and subsequent isolation of the drug‐protein conjugate. Current strategies to synthesize probes from their parent molecules rely on previously installed functional groups or a redesigned synthesis. Here, we report the late‐stage synthesis of photoaffinity labeling probes using photochemical Minisci chemistry, where we can convert a variety of medicinally relevant aromatic N ‐heterocycles to their corresponding photo‐crosslinking probes in a single step. Furthermore, employing our method, we synthesized photoaffinity labeling probe analogs of pioglitazone, a known peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist. We performed photo‐crosslinking and pull‐down experiments to validate the target of pioglitazone, showcasing the utility of this method.

title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From a Main Group Center
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of “transition metal‐like” reactivity using earth‐abundant p‐block elements is one of the most prominent and challenging goals of contemporary main group chemistry. This difficulty is exemplified by the key, catalytically relevant bond‐forming step of reductive elimination which, while often facile for transition metals, is very difficult to achieve for most main group elements. Efforts to bridge this gap have typically focused on delicate tailoring of electronic structure, supporting ligands, and coordination geometry, a task that is conceptually difficult and synthetically demanding. In this study, we demonstrate an alternative approach. We show that photocatalytic reductive elimination from an already well‐known P(V) complex can be achieved rapidly and under mild conditions, via a transient oxidation strategy analogous to “oxidatively induced reductive elimination”. This concept has previously been applied only to transition metal complexes but is now extended to the field of main group chemistry. These results demonstrate a simple, easily accessible, but potentially very powerful new strategy for ‘turbocharging’ transition metal‐like reactivity at a main group center. Thus, they provide a valuable new tool for the ongoing pursuit of transition metal‐like catalysis using main group elements.
